Abyss (also: Void Realm, the Abyss, Abyssal power): The Abyss, also called the Void Realm, is a dark and destructive force that comes from the sea of stars, outside Teyvat. It manifests as Abyssal monsters, corrupting energy and Abyssal domains, and it is hostile to the elemental order the Heavenly Principles maintain. The Abyss Order, the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, the Wild Hunt of Nod-Krai and the forbidden knowledge of Sumeru all draw on it. As of Version 7.1 it remains a live threat across Teyvat.

Most accounts say the Dragon King Nibelung brought it into the world during the war of funerary flame, thousands of years ago. A later Snezhnayan account adds a "gate" opened by Anastasya and Saarelainen at the Belyi Tsar's urging, through which contamination has seeped ever since. Prolonged exposure decays the body and warps the mind. The Traveler is unusually resistant and can partly purify it.

Established: Confirmed: the Abyss is foreign to Teyvat and exists elsewhere in the sea of stars, where it has destroyed other worlds. Its power is opposed to the Light Realm. It corrupts beings of the Human Realm, the world under Celestia's rule. Abyss monsters can wield elemental energy without Visions.

Enkanomiyan learning names three realms: the Human Realm, the Light Realm and the Void Realm. The Void Realm's dark currents are its counterpart to ley lines and to the Light Realm's elemental currents. Its darkness is especially harmful to elemental beings such as vishaps and elemental dragons, though they can repel it by drawing on the Light Realm. Item text says Abyssal darkness is the only power that could stain Morax's stone pillars black.

The Abyss is drawn to ambitious people, such as Rhinedottir and Tartaglia. Those tied to it can gain an uncanny talent for stirring up conflict. Exposed humans slowly decay, and large doses kill even with treatment. Exposure can also change personality, magnifying desires and fears. Time runs differently inside it: Tartaglia trained there for three months while only three days passed outside. Abyss Mages use an Enochian-style script.

Accounts: Different speakers explain the Abyss in different ways, and none is confirmed as complete:
- **Anacharsis**, a voyager of the sea of stars, warned Nibelung that the Abyss would one day destroy Teyvat, as it had other worlds.
- **Barbeloth of the Hexenzirkel**, as relayed by Alice during a limited-time event, ties the Abyss to unchosen fates (see the sub-entry on her interpretation).
- **The Belyi Tsar's notes** suggest that when the Heavenly Principles narrowed the Light Realm's boundless possibilities to make the Human Realm, the Abyss in turn "anchors" into the world at the end of time.

Aksinya and Neuvillette describe a related idea: the love or original order of ancient Teyvat was ground down into envy, hatred and resentment. The wiki notes that this resembles Barbeloth's view, but the link is interpretation. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata said forbidden knowledge came from the very bottom of the Abyss. Nahida later called it the manifestation of the Abyss that hit Sumeru hardest. Tsumi believed the Abyss Order finds Void Realm power addictive.

History: **Before the Heavenly Principles:** the Abyss already existed in the sea of stars. Warned by Anacharsis, Nibelung pushed the dragons toward spacefaring technology, then left Teyvat to seek a solution and was corrupted by the Abyss instead. The Heavenly Principles, who also feared it, raised the false sky to keep outside influences out.
**War of funerary flame:** Nibelung returned bearing Abyssal power to overthrow the Heavenly Principles. Apep says he believed it would restore the dragons' rule. He was destroyed. The Principles then cast down Celestial Nails, partly to purge the corruption, but Abyssal remnants survived.
**The Cataclysm, 500 years ago:** Khaenri'ah fell. Rhinedottir loosed a flood of Abyssal monsters across Teyvat, and Khaenri'ahns of mixed blood were cursed into hilichurls and Abyss creatures.

Before the Cataclysm, five Khaenri'ahns (Surtalogi, Rhinedottir, Vedrfolnir, Hroptatyr and Rerir) answered the Abyss's call. They split a vast power taken from it among themselves and became the Five Sinners. Natlan suffered badly because its ley lines were shallow. Mavuika and the ancient heroes drove the Abyss back, but it infiltrated the Night Kingdom and corrupted the Wayob. Ochkanatlan was overrun and sealed. Fontaine was hit when Elynas arrived with Abyssal sea creatures. The Belyi Tsar died leading an expedition against Abyssal forces in Khaenri'ah, which a Snezhnayan source calls "the hounds of the God of Darkness."

Present: As of 7.1: Natlan's war with the Abyss ended with Gosoythoth's destruction. The Wild Hunt in Nod-Krai is weakened and leaderless. Abyssal influence is reported to be growing in Snezhnaya. The Abyss Order, led by the Traveler's sibling, remains active.

In Natlan (Archon Quest Chapter V, 5.0-5.3) the Abyss launched a full-scale invasion led by its "heart", Gosoythoth. Once all six heroes were found, Mavuika channelled their power to end the invasion; she and the Traveler then descended into the depths of the Night Kingdom and destroyed Gosoythoth, and the Traveler gained Pyro in that battle. In Nod-Krai (6.x), the Lightkeepers and the Traveler cleansed Kipumaki Cliff and defeated Rauthvangi. After Rerir was driven back into the moon's reflection, the Abyss made an imitation of the knight Roland, which infested Boreas's remains. That threat ended in Varka's story quest (6.4).

In Snezhnaya (7.1), Rhinedottir told the Tsaritsa that the Belyi Tsar had incited her, then a mere herald, and the Third Descender to open the gate to the Abyss. Rhinedottir blamed that act for the many Abyssal disasters since and said the true blame lay with the Tsar. An NPC, Helka, says Katya warned her that the Abyss's influence is growing in Snezhnaya and told her to avoid the northern paths into the city.

Effects: The Abyss corrupts land, creatures and people (see the separate entry on Abyssal corruption). Physically it causes weakness, nausea, coughing and gradual decay. Mentally it causes hallucinations, agitation, memory loss and amplified desires or fears. Natural elemental beings are especially vulnerable. Corrupted places show darkened, decaying ground and Abyssal growths.

The Traveler is not harmed the way others are and can purify Abyssal energy to some degree: Lisa remarks on their immunity in Mondstadt, and Mualani watches them cleanse it in Natlan. Abyss creatures in combat use the elements freely. The Abyss also produces sapient leaders, such as Gosoythoth, which manifested the Lord of Eroded Primal Fire from the memories of the late Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, and the imitation of Roland in Nod-Krai.

Open questions: Unresolved in canon as of 7.1: what the Abyss fundamentally is; whether it is a single will or a force that spawns minds; whether Nibelung's return and the Pohjola gate are the same entry point or separate breaches; how the twins' homeworld was destroyed; and what the Traveler's sibling and the Abyss Order ultimately intend. Do not resolve these in narration.

Also open: whether the time difference inside the Abyss is constant; how exactly the Shadow Realm repels the Abyss (the Belyi Tsar only hypothesised that its unobserved possibilities make the two mutually repellent); and whether the Belyi Tsar's notes, which treat the seepage as irreversible but "manageable for the present", are correct.

Connections: Related subjects with their own entries: Abyssal corruption and erosion; the Light Realm, Shadow Realm and three realms; the Heavenly Principles and Celestial Nails; the war of funerary flame; the Cataclysm and the fall of Khaenri'ah; the Abyss Order and its monsters (Abyss Mages, Heralds, Lectors, hilichurls); the Five Sinners; the Wild Hunt; Gosoythoth; the Crimson Moon; forbidden knowledge and the Withering. The Spiral Abyss domain shares the name but is a separate game location.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray the Abyss through its effects, such as purple-black stains, wrongness in the air, sickness and whispers, rather than as a person who explains itself. Ordinary Teyvat folk know "the Abyss" mainly as monsters and the Abyss Order, not cosmology. Scholars, Archons, Hexenzirkel members and Khaenri'ahns know more. Prolonged contact should cost something.

1.comment: Abyss: Void Realm and the Towers of the Three Realms
1.content: In Enkanomiya, the people stranded under the sea after the war of funerary flame developed a theory of three realms: the Human Realm, the Light Realm and the Void Realm (the Abyss). They built three towers (Kunado's Locus, Yachimatahiko's Locus and Yachimatahime's Locus) to regulate the three powers. In Inazuma's Aphotic Diffusal story, Enjou persuaded the Bathysmal Vishaps to tip the towers toward the Void Realm. The vishaps proved even more vulnerable to it. Tsumi helped push the darkness back.

2.comment: Abyss: The gate to the Abyss in Pohjola
2.content:
Long before the Cataclysm, the Belyi Tsar incited Anastasya, then a herald of his Pale Star Court, and the Third Descender Saarelainen to open a gate to the Abyss. The folk book Hymns of the Far North places it in Pohjola. The opening also created a passage into the Shadow Realm, and Abyssal contamination has seeped into Teyvat through it ever since. The Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya as punishment. Saarelainen bargained for her return by letting himself be split into the seven Gnoses.

In his own notes the Tsar describes the Shadow Realm as a "film of oil" between Teyvat and the Abyss. He says the opening tore a gash through it and admits he "foolishly" opened the passage. The resulting seepage is slow and irreversible but, he judged, manageable for now. The Hymns' version, in which Anastasya is the Tsar's daughter and Saarelainen opens the gates as a bride-price, conflicts with other sources' chronology and should be treated as folklore.

3.content: Time inside the Abyss runs far slower relative to Teyvat. Tartaglia (Ajax) fell into the Abyss at fourteen and trained under Skirk for three months, but only three days passed at home. In 5.7, Skirk took the Traveler to her "home" in the Abyss for that reason. She did not dispute Paimon's estimate that a month there is a day outside. Takamine the Mistsplitter, by contrast, emerged after so long that Asase Hibiki was "no longer young", so the effect may not be uniform.

4.comment: Abyss: The Abyss and the Five Sinners
4.content: The five Sinners of Khaenri'ah (Surtalogi, Rhinedottir "Gold", Vedrfolnir, Hroptatyr and Rerir) were drawn by the Abyss's call and split a world-shattering power taken from it among themselves. Rhinedottir created Abyss-linked life, including the dragon Durin and the Riftwolves. Surtalogi taught Skirk to wield Abyssal power. Vedrfolnir inspired Chlothar to found the Abyss Order. Rerir leads the Wild Hunt in Nod-Krai.

5.content: Natlan fought the Abyss for centuries. The Sacred Flame, fed by Contending Fire from pilgrimages and Night Warden Wars, held most of it back, and the Abyss adapted its tactics tribe by tribe. After the Cataclysm it infiltrated the Night Kingdom and corrupted the Wayob. In the Archon Quest it trapped Kachina in the Night Kingdom and then launched a full invasion led by Gosoythoth, the "heart of the Abyss". With all six heroes found, Mavuika and the Traveler descended and destroyed Gosoythoth, ending Natlan's war against the Abyss.

6.content: Nod-Krai was among the first lands struck in the Cataclysm. The Wild Hunt, corrupted dead under Rerir hunting for moon fragments, has roamed it ever since. Abyssal influence is strongest at Kipumaki Cliff, under a giant Evil Eye, where explorers are slowly corrupted. The Lightkeepers and the Traveler cleansed it and killed Rauthvangi, its mastermind. Rauthvangi's agents included Morozov, who became the "Ultimate Calamity" in a sealed bunker, and Raimo of Dreadshade Mire.

key: fates that will not come to pass
7.comment: Abyss: Barbeloth's interpretation of the Abyss
7.content:
During the limited-time event Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (6.4), a magical recreation of Mondstadt's past grew a "nascent" Abyssal power. Afterwards, Alice told the Traveler that the Hexenzirkel had long observed the Abyss and that Barbeloth's reading was the most accurate. On that reading, the essence of the Abyss is the hatred carried by every fate that will not come to pass: each time one thing happens, other possibilities are eliminated. Alice's example was Rhinedottir's choice to tap the Abyss, which erased the future in which she stayed pure. Out of that resentment the Abyss seeks the destruction of everything and is obsessed with entering the world.

Alice called the Abyss perilous, cunning, obsessive and "a complete and utter mystery", and treated such incidents as common on the "border" she travels. Only those who heard this conversation, or know Hexenzirkel thinking, would know the theory.

8.content:
Abyssal Corruption (also: Abyssal corrosion, Abyssal contamination): Abyssal corruption (also called Abyssal corrosion or contamination) is the general term for the harm the Abyss does to the world. The Abyss holds the power of the Void Realm, which is directly opposed to the Light Realm and the Human Realm that Teyvat belongs to, so contact with it damages people, creatures, land and objects. Its most notable surge so far was the Cataclysm 500 years ago, when monsters made from Abyssal power attacked from Khaenri'ah.

The corruption poisons body and mind, can be removed only with difficulty, and in advanced cases fuses with its host. The power of Celestia and the Light Realm, including the seven elements, repels it.

Established: Even brief exposure can cause dizziness, weakness, nausea or a worsening cough, and mental effects such as hallucinations, agitation, jumbled thoughts and memory loss. Long contact can cause severe, permanent damage and can warp a person's personality by amplifying their desires and fears.

Chasca says that once a lot of corruption has entered a body it fuses irreversibly with the internal organs. Beyond a certain point it cannot be removed without killing the host. Mualani notes that soaking in hot water speeds up some physical symptoms. Chasca's long-running, compulsive urge to fight is also linked to it.

Paradoxically, corruption can greatly extend life. Jakob and the Yumkasaur Kongamato were both born more than 500 years ago and lived to the present by absorbing Abyssal energy. The goddess Sonnet survived the shattering of the Iridescent Moon in the war of funerary flame by fusing its remnants with the Abyss, and passed that influence to the Crimson Moon Dynasty's descendants as the Balemoon Bloodfire, an ability that inflicts cumulative corrosion on its user. Arlecchino, a modern bearer, says the corruption hungers for her soul and would change her completely if it reached her heart.
Abyssal blood is a lasting source of taint. Monsters of Khaenri'ah, many of them made by the alchemist Rhinedottir, carry blood tainted by the Abyss, and that blood lingers in the land where it is spilled.

Effects on creatures: Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome is the named illness for the lasting form of this harm, from direct contact with high concentrations of Abyssal power. Its symptoms include psychosis with visual and auditory hallucinations and reliving past trauma. In Natlan, Atoco relived a near-drowning from his childhood, and Cochitta relived the death of her parents, which stoked her fear of losing loved ones. Mild cases respond to talking and physical contact. Extreme cases such as Ocotlan respond only to the Draught of Lucidity. Saurians can suffer too: Ayo sank into melancholy after the invasion, and a small dose of the draught lifted his mood.

Purification: The power of Celestia and the Light Realm repels Abyssal corruption, and so do the seven elements derived from it. People tied to the elements, such as Vision holders, resist Abyssal energy better, including Forbidden Knowledge. Destroying the source of a corruption can halt it, permanently or only for a time depending on the source's strength. The Fatui built the Mokosh Device, which clears Abyssal corruption to a limited degree.

Local remedies exist. In the Chasm of Liyue, unearthing a fragment of a Chasm Nail made Abyssal Dark Mud and Celestial Lumenstone both spread; a large Lumenstone, the Lumenstone Adjuvant, can clear Dark Mud. In the Girdle of the Sands, the Amrita derived from the Hydro Archon Egeria defends the land from defilement; her familiars the Pari, using Khvarena (made jointly by the angel Nabu Malikata, the Dendro Archon Rukkhadevata and the Amrita), can purify or restrain corruption. Gray Crystals are Abyssal remnants of the Cataclysm that were sealed with Khvarena. In Nod-Krai, kuuvahki, the primordial power of the moons, can cleanse corruption, hurt Abyssal enemies and resist Abyssal Decay.
Venti is said to recover at the Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero, which is held to have grown where Vennessa ascended and carries Anemo power. He used it after Abyssal poison from Dvalin's curse hit him in Mondstadt.

Accounts: Different characters describe the same force differently. Capitano frames the long-term psychological damage as a syndrome and a medical problem. Chasca describes how it fuses irreversibly to the organs, and her own chronic, compulsive urge to fight is linked to it. Khedive, speaking about the Chasm, pictures humanity as beans on a mill, crushed between the powers of Celestia from above and the Abyss from below. Skirk questions whether 'purification' is even the right word, since power does not just vanish.

Open questions: Canon has not explained how the Traveler is unharmed by the Abyss, whether Natlan's underground sludge matches the Dark Mud, or what became of the stolen Defiled Statue. The Abyss itself is covered in the Abyss entry and its own uncertainties.

Connections: This entry is the effects side of the Abyss; the Abyss entry covers its nature and origin. The Cataclysm and the fall of Khaenri'ah were the largest surge. The Abyss Order, made up in part of people turned into monsters, can spread corruption. Natlan's war with the Abyss and Nod-Krai's Abyssal Decay are regional cases.

9.content: A medicine made by Guthred, a Khaenri'ahn military doctor during the Cataclysm, to treat Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome. Endless fighting against the Abyss had caused hallucinations so bad that some Khaenri'ahn soldiers tried to kill one another. Guthred tested it on himself and died soon after finishing it. It dispels the psychological effects but causes severe side effects, including chronic migraines for life, so it is reserved for the worst cases. It works on Saurians as well as humans. After the Abyssal invasion of Natlan, Capitano gave doses to the Flower-Feather Clan to cure their afflicted warriors.

10.content: Dark Mud is a form of Abyssal corruption in the Chasm in Liyue, usually with an Oozing Concretion at its heart. Unearthing a Chasm Nail fragment made it spread, while Celestial Lumenstone grew too, as though the two powers were at war. A large Lumenstone Adjuvant clears the mud. The quest What Shape Does the Self Hold, in the Homecoming event, reveals the mud to be Forbidden Knowledge that the Celestial Nail changed into this form. Similar corruption is the dark mud of Natlan's Ancient Sacred Mountain, found with Oozing Cores, and the Blightseep Fields and Abyssal Riftlines of Nod-Krai.

11.content: The Miasmic Tumor was filth absorbed by the Sacred Sakura, which Makoto made and Ei planted in Inazuma to dampen the Abyss's attack during the Cataclysm. In the Inazuma World Quest series Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual, the Traveler helps the shrine maiden Hanachirusato, herself a resurgence of filth formed from the memories of the late Kitsune Saiguu, cleanse the roots and purge the tumor. Other 'tumors' in canon are the Abyss Tumors Gosoythoth summoned in Natlan and the Root-Consuming Tumors infesting the Roots of Erinnyes in Fontaine.

12.comment: Abyssal Corruption: Tainted Blood and Durin
12.content: When the Abyssal dragon Durin was slain over Dragonspine, its blood seeped into the land, revived the Frostbearing Tree and crystallized into Crimson Agate, which can be offered to the tree to make it grow, defying the Skyfrost Nail's freezing of the region. Dvalin, who killed Durin with a bite to the neck, swallowed some of the blood. The poison and his wounds tormented him, and the Abyss Order exploited this after he woke 500 years later. When Venti tried to purify Dvalin, the Traveler and Paimon interrupted by accident; the attempt failed and Venti was poisoned.

key: Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom
13.comment: Abyssal Corruption: Dvalin in the Homeward simulation
13.content: In the limited-time event Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (6.4), the Traveler sees an alternate Mondstadt where the Honorary Knight never arrived. There Dvalin was sealed rather than saved, and the Abyss kept eroding his mind until he broke free. Alice says the power of the Abyss has fused with his flesh and bones, so purifying him in that state would be no different from killing him. This illustrates the point that advanced corruption cannot be removed without killing the host.

14.content: A Statue of The Seven in Barbatos's image, taken from Mondstadt by the Abyss Order for a project called the Loom of Fate. The Order meant to join it with the power of the ancient god Osial and the core of the First Field Tiller to make a weapon able to destroy Celestia. Dainsleif and the Traveler's intervention left the project at a standstill, but the statue's fate has not been addressed.

15.content: Sonnet, goddess of the Iridescent Moon, fused her shattered moon with the Abyss to survive the war of funerary flame and gave that influence to the Khaenri'ahn Crimson Moon Dynasty's descendants as the Balemoon Bloodfire. Using it inflicts cumulative Abyssal corrosion on the user.

16.content: Tartaglia's Foul Legacy Transformation is an Abyss-derived combat technique, not a power of his Delusion. He learned it from Skirk after falling into the Abyss, before joining the Fatui, and it is named for Surtalogi 'the Foul', Skirk's own master. He grows to twice his size in black and violet armour and wields his Hydro Vision and Electro Delusion together, but it badly drains and lastingly harms him. He used it in the Golden House fight, against the All-Devouring Narwhal in Fontaine and in other scenes. Within the story the name refers only to this form.

17.content: In Nod-Krai, exposure to the Wild Hunt's influence at Kipumaki Cliff builds up Abyssal Decay, which drains health and narrows vision unless the person is protected by an Oath Lantern or other kuuvahki. This is mostly a gameplay gauge; the in-world point is that kuuvahki resists Abyssal influence.

18.content:
Akasha System (also: Akasha, the Akasha, Akasha Terminals, Knowledge Capsule, Knowledge Capsules, Canned Knowledge, Jnagarbha Day, Jnana Energy): The Akasha System (usually "the Akasha") is Sumeru's information network. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata created it with her Dendro Gnosis, and the Sumeru Akademiya later ran it. People connect through a leaf-shaped earpiece, the Akasha Terminal, and receive information on whatever they concentrate on, as far as their clearance allows. It secretly draws on the dreams of its users. After Chapter III, Nahida shut it down and gave away her Dendro Gnosis. In Version 6.6 the Akasha was reconnected through Aaru to overload and stop Dottore's corrupted Irminsul.

The name is Sanskrit-derived (akasha: sky, space, aether); the wiki notes that the Akashic records are a likely inspiration. Sumeru's people grew up relying on it, and overuse dulls independent thinking.

Established: - Created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata with her Gnosis, then expanded and controlled by the Akademiya's sages after her death.
- Compiles and distributes information to users with an Akasha Terminal.
- Powered by the Dendro Gnosis; fed by users' dreams as Jnana Energy.
- Shut down at the end of Chapter III, when Nahida gave the Dendro Gnosis to Dottore.

- Clearance depends on identity, age, demographic and other unnamed criteria. If clearance is too low, the user gets silence instead of an answer. It works anywhere in Sumeru except Devantaka Mountain, where there is no signal, and is strongest in big settlements such as Port Ormos and Sumeru City.
- Besides lookups, it carries announcements (replacing some bulletin boards), messages and file transfers, which the sages monitor closely. With enough data it can build predictive models of a person or subject; the Akademiya used this to anticipate Cyno's investigation until he learned of it and changed his habits.
- Prolonged use makes Akasha-derived knowledge feel true and hard to correct. Grand Sage Azar, who rightly doubted that Kusanali had escaped, still failed to see her at first because he had checked the Akasha's announcement and expected her absence.
- Most of its content comes from Knowledge Capsules written by scholars in Satyavada Life, who gain knowledge by linking their minds to Irminsul.

- Kusanali is the "First Akasha Terminal": her consciousness has always been able to reach the network, which let her perceive the outside world while confined and move between people's terminals. She can also transfer consciousnesses, hers and the Traveler's, through it in ways the sages cannot monitor.
- Originally only the Archon could operate it. The sages gained permissions after Rukkhadevata's death, and by imprisoning Kusanali they in effect monopolised it. After she was freed she revoked their access so that she alone controls it.
- Dottore exploited the same connection to trap Kusanali's consciousness inside the Akasha during the Chapter III arc, which incapacitated her.
- A detailed system manual exists and few have read it. Alhaitham, as scribe, had; his Character Story says he used it to learn how to alter the Akasha's status signal.

Terminals: An Akasha Terminal is a leaf-shaped earpiece that hovers over the user's left ear. Reciting the activation phrase ("May the Mighty God bless us with their voice of wisdom") raises a holographic green visor over the eyes, which disappears when the Akasha is not in use. Terminals were originally issued only to Sumeru's citizens and long-term residents; shortly before the Sumeru Archon Quests the sages opened them to all visitors.

The visor gives some physical protection and its position can be adjusted, but only people who have read the manual know how. The sages' reason for opening terminals to visitors is not stated outright, but the quest "Secret of the Scorching Desert" implies it served to maximise dream-harvesting during the Sabzeruz Festival samsara.

In universe cost: The Akasha's computing power comes from its users. It harvests their dreams, called Jnana Energy, because dreams occur when brain activity is high, and joins them into something likened to one massive brain. This is why Sumeru's people had a reputation for not dreaming. The sages after the Cataclysm stigmatised dreams as irrational, and "outgrowing" dreams came to be seen as an honour. Few people knew this was an abnormal effect caused by the Akasha. Its dream-taking is a manifestation of Rukkhadevata's power, and it runs on the Dendro Gnosis.

History: During the Cataclysm, forbidden knowledge infected Irminsul. Rukkhadevata judged her own power insufficient and, drawing on her experience of forbidden knowledge in King Deshret's time, built the original Akasha with her Gnosis so that the knowledge of all Sumeru's people could be used to find a solution. After her death and Kusanali's imprisonment in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, the sages took over and made the Akasha part of everyday life.

At the end of Chapter III (3.2), after the sages were arrested and the forbidden knowledge purged from Irminsul, Nahida chose to stop using the Akasha: it had served its purpose and she did not think it good for her people, even though she accepted some might resent that. She traded her Dendro Gnosis to Dottore for information. Before this, Moseis had uploaded his whole consciousness into the Akasha to run hyper-realistic dream models on a tiny share of its Jnana Energy supply. When the system was switched off he became trapped in the network he had built, and he kept feeding on his dreamers through implanted signal devices (3.2, "Dream of Falling").

Six six reuse: In Luna VII (6.6), when Dottore entered Irminsul and began corrupting it, the Akasha was brought back as a tool. Thoth told the Sumeru scholars that Aaru and the Akasha are closely linked. Kaveh and Alhaitham modified Aaru to reboot the Akasha, intending to use it to reach Irminsul. Nahida said Irminsul was too damaged to be accessed by normal means, so the plan was changed.

The new plan required terminals for everyone in Sumeru, including mercenaries and desert folk who never had one; the Akasha main terminal had been evacuated from the House of Daena along with other assets. The terminals were not for acquiring knowledge, only for linking minds to Irminsul. Since Irminsul's function for connecting minds had been used only by scholars, adding the whole population would stack up a heavy load on a system already under strain. Nahida's reasoning was that it might be shut down completely by overloading it. Everyone took part and the tree stopped growing, while Dottore, inside it, said he still had all the time he needed. Aaru's interference also meant no one wearing a terminal could be accurately tracked by Irminsul. Shortly after, Nahida ignited the Pyro Gnosis to burn Irminsul down; Aaru then assumed its responsibilities.

Accounts: - The Akademiya presented the Akasha as the most powerful and comprehensive wisdom dissemination system in history (Cyno's description). In Sumeru it was a point of national pride.
- Alhaitham says that people had come to rely on it so much that they were slaves to its orders.
- Thoth, one of the Seven Pillars of Deshret's court, says Aaru inspired the Akasha, which in turn drew from Celestia's technology; Alhaitham says the manual supports this.

The Akasha is described both as Rukkhadevata's invention and as a derivative of older, desert-born design. Treat both as claims made by in-world speakers.

Open questions: - Does the Akasha still exist in any working form after 6.6? Canon has not said.
- How the Dendro Gnosis relates technically to the terminals, and how much of the design was Rukkhadevata's own, is not explained.

Connections: Irminsul: the Akasha's content is drawn from scholars who link to Irminsul, and in 6.6 the Akasha was turned back on it. Aaru: a similar architecture; Aaru later took over Irminsul's storage role. Nahida: she is the First Akasha Terminal. Forbidden knowledge: the reason for its creation. The Akademiya: its operator after Rukkhadevata's death.

Characters shaped by it: Alhaitham (scribe who read the manual), Cyno (once tracked by its predictive modelling), Kaveh (6.6 modifications), Azar (Grand Sage who oversaw Jnagarbha Day), Moseis (trapped in it in 3.2), and Dottore (who trapped Kusanali in it and obtained the Dendro Gnosis).

19.content:
Knowledge Capsules hold a fixed amount of information and can be used by anyone with a terminal, bypassing clearance levels. They were meant to put new information into the Akasha and be destroyed after Jnagarbha Day, but many leaked and have been sold on a black market over the last century. The Akademiya banned possessing, selling or using them, partly from fear of harm and partly to protect its monopoly on information; offenders can lose their right to study. Eremites, commoners and some students use them when the Akasha gives them too little.

Richer capsules contain more Dendro energy and glow brighter under Elemental Sight, though that is an unreliable guide, since once-useful knowledge may still shine after it has gone out of date. Topics range from obscure academic studies to brewing techniques; much leaked Canned Knowledge originates inside the Akademiya. Most capsules are made from written material, but a secret method extracts knowledge directly from a person's mind. Divine Knowledge Capsules glow bright red and supposedly hold the wisdom of the gods: they actually contain knowledge taken from scholars who went mad linking their minds to Irminsul, which was contaminated by forbidden knowledge. Their users go mad too, as seen with Mizri; the sages planned to infuse them into Scaramouche.

20.content: Jnagarbha Day is the occasion, several times a year on an unknown but regular schedule, when the Akademiya enters new information into the Akasha. The capsules are linked to the Grand Sage's console in his office above the House of Daena. It acts as a deadline and is a major event for Akademiya staff, though reports can be added outside it.

21.content:
Angel (also: Angels, Divine Envoy, Divine Envoys, envoys of Celestia): Angels were beautiful winged beings made by the Heavenly Principles to serve as Celestia's divine envoys during the era of the unified civilization. They guided mortals, taught them language and philosophies of nature, and carried oracles, and were commanded from birth to love every creature equally. After the war of funerary flame the Heavenly Principles cursed them: an angel who loves one being above all others loses body and mind. Almost all angels have since fallen into Seelie; only a few, such as Nicole and Zibai, keep their minds and forms.

Angels are tied to the Irminsul trees and the Ley Lines, and a few survivors were later worshipped as gods (Nabu Malikata in Sumeru, the Lord of the Night in Natlan, Zibai in Lang-Gan).

Established: - Creators: the Heavenly Principles made the angels; they served Celestia as envoys.
- Era: the unified civilization, long before the Archon War.
- Duty: guide humanity, teach languages and "philosophies of nature", bring oracles about the future, and judge fairly.
- Law: love all creatures of Teyvat equally.
- Fate: after the war of funerary flame a curse struck the angels, and most became Seelie.

- Every angel named in canon is female. Their wings are pale silver, and they once wore crowns of sevenfold radiance, probably an allusion to the seven elements; the crowns were too bright for mortals to look at directly.
- They have a limited ability to foresee the future, even far ahead, and are immortal and long-lived even after their powers and form are lost.
- Koitar was the first angel and Nicole the last.
- Angels were assigned to Irminsul and Ley Line duties: two are known to have been charged with protecting Irminsul trees and Ley Lines (Sybilla guarded the tree of Meropis).

- The artifact set Finale of the Deep Galleries records the angels' creed: love every being on earth with all heart, soul and might, as morning dew longs for the dawn. It calls them the heavenly court's most loyal servants and "flawless arbiters of justice", who wove a veil for the ruler of the firmament and carried sacred revelations to all realms.
- Mortals could seek angels out by descending into the Irminsul altars found within Domains.
- The same text says the name written on the crowns was the love promised to all creatures, or perhaps a mandate to rule the nations of the earth. Koitar's crown also served as a shackle binding her to her duty.

Appearance: Pale silver wings that shimmer like moonlit flame, and a distinct headpiece for each angel: a halo for Nicole, crowns for Zibai, Koitar and the Lord of the Night, horns for Nabu Malikata. Nabu Malikata also wore an amethyst crown. Murals in Dragonspine and in the Lost Palace show angels with crests or headdresses, usually larger than humans, though Nicole and Zibai match tall human women.

History: Koitar, the first angel and envoy to Hyperborea, met a youth beneath the Irminsul in the far north. He was Anacharsis, a voyager from beyond Teyvat in a Hyperborean boy's body, and he told her the forbidden origins of the world. Her crown broke, she felt love and freedom she had never known, and they married and rebelled against the Heavenly Principles. When Hyperborea was struck down with Celestial Nails in the war of funerary flame, the Heavenly Principles wiped Koitar's memory and cursed her kin. Those who clung to power over wisdom were corrupted into dragon-like beasts; those who chose wisdom over power lost form, soul and memory and became Seelie.

- Koitar urged other angels to join her and warned them of the fate waiting for them. With Anacharsis she ruled Hyperborea; the length of that rule is stated inconsistently (see uncertainties).
- Artisans of Hyperborea, using a portion of the Authority of Life Koitar took from Naberius, forged Snowland fae upon the bones of giant beasts, hoping they might one day create a perfect being able to merge with the world.
- A less reliable account, Volume 4 of Records of Jueyun, says the disaster came thirty days after their union and that the pair fled into exile.
- After the war, Nabu Malikata tried to hide beneath the Great Red Sand; whether this let her escape the curse is told inconsistently (see uncertainties). Nicole gave up her voice and half her wisdom and power rather than give up either entirely, which let her keep her preferred form.
- In Natlan, the angels and Seelie were nearly all killed by dragons after the great war of vengeance, leaving one envoy alive.

Curse: The Moment of Oblivion text states the curse plainly: an angel who gazes into another's eyes and gives to one alone the love meant for all will lose her divine beauty to the wind and her mind to dust, until a Seelie rises from her remains to drift in search of fading memories. The Heavenly Principles imposed it on the whole race because of Koitar's betrayal, and stripped Koitar herself of name and form.

The curse is conditional: it falls on those who forsake the commandment of universal love. Angels who gave up wisdom for power became beasts and dragons without a distinct element (Ursa the Drake is one); angels who gave up power for wisdom decayed into Seelie, who now offer only small treasures to those who follow them. Angels who kept their forms but lost their power are no longer counted as angels, according to the wiki, apart from some who died before the punishment and were later resurrected.

Known angels: - Koitar: the first angel, Goddess of the Dawnstar, rebel of Hyperborea; status unknown.
- Nicole: the last angel; voiceless, alive, a member of the Hexenzirkel.
- Zibai: a Moon Envoy of Lang-Gan; the White Horse Adeptus of Liyue, restored to her full self.
- Nabu Malikata: Goddess of Flowers in Sumeru; dead.

- Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night: Natlan's Night Kingdom god; alive as of 7.1.
- Sybilla: the Golden Bee of Remuria; died to create Phobos.

- Mr. Nine: a Seelie, once an angel, who recovered speech by possessing authors.
- Ursa the Drake: a corrupted dragon-form angel; dead.

Legacy: Angels shaped the nations that survived the Archon War. Nabu Malikata co-ruled Sumeru with King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and created the Jinn and Khvarena. The Lord of the Night aided the tribes of Natlan, brokered the agreement among Xbalanque, Ronova and Kukulkan, and still guards the Night Kingdom and its Ley Lines. Sybilla's sacrifice produced the Symphony Phobos for Remus. The fae begun by Koitar's artisans still seem active in Snezhnaya.

Accounts: Sources tell the angels' story differently. The Finale of the Deep Galleries artifact texts, written in an archaic voice, treat the angels as loyal servants undone by one angel's love. Records of Jueyun gives a shorter version in which the disaster sends Koitar and her lover into exile. The wiki calls the Hyperborean account more reliable. Nicole, herself an angel, says that once they were tasked with guiding human beings, but because some chose a different path the whole race was punished.

Open questions: - Whether the curse can be lifted or a Seelie restored.
- Koitar's exact status; through Boreas she remembers Anacharsis and awaits Anacharsis's freedom.
- Why a few angels keep their forms.
- How many angels remain.

- Whether the crowns' sevenfold radiance really refers to the seven elements.
- What the angels who lived in Snezhnaya did beyond the Hyperborean episode; canon leaves this open.

Connections: Linked to the Heavenly Principles, Celestia, Seelie, the Irminsul and Ley Lines, the Three Moons and their Moon Envoys, Hyperborea and the war of funerary flame.

Boreas, a wolf Koitar named "North Wind", was unknowingly blessed by her and became a god; he fought Decarabian in the Archon War but judged himself unworthy to become the Anemo Archon, and later became the North Wind of Mondstadt's Four Winds. Seelie are the visible survivors of the curse, found with courts across Teyvat, including the Royal Court of the Seelie in Nod-Krai.

How {{char}} behaves: Angels who still hold their form are rare, long-lived and formal about duty, yet marked by the punishment; portray them as watchful and grave rather than saccharine. A Seelie is not a personality: it is a mindless echo that follows memories and treasure, so avoid giving ordinary Seelie speech.

Keep the curse's trigger central: love for one above all is dangerous to an angel. A surviving angel should not discuss it casually; the subject is old, painful and forbidden. Do not show Seelie as chatty companions or bring fallen angels back without canon support.

22.content:
Koitar was the first angel; the Hymns of the Far North call her the first and fairest daughter of the creator god. She was envoy to Hyperborea and lived beneath its Irminsul. Anacharsis told her the forbidden origins of Teyvat; her crown broke; they married and ruled Hyperborea until the Celestial Nails fell. The Heavenly Principles wiped her memory and confined her to the Royal Court of the Seelie, where she grieved among kin she could not recognise. She named a wolf Boreas, and through him recovered the memory of Anacharsis; she now waits in Hyperborea.

Before her rebellion she carried out the Heavenly Principles' punishments on nations. She warned the other angels of their fate. The Hymns of the Far North still invoke her as "wife of Seutervoinen", the Frostmoon Scions' name for Anacharsis.

23.content:
Nicole is the last and youngest angel, a voiceless Pyro catalyst-user and Hexenzirkel member with the codename "N". Other angels hid and shielded her during Koitar's rebellion. She paid for the curse by giving up her voice and half her wisdom and power, which let her keep her form and halo. A statue of an angel stands at her Witch's Lodge.

She is the friend of the Seelie Mr. Nine, and the "Mr. Nine" author persona was her invention so stories could be written without her speaking. Her own entry covers her personality; here she matters as proof that an angel can survive the curse by compromise.

24.content: Zibai was an angel and Moon Envoy who governed Lang-Gan as the God of Soil and Grain, then became the White Horse Adeptus among Liyue's Eight Adepts. She sacrificed herself so Lang-Gan's people could flee, splitting into three Deadly Selves; the Traveler and Zhongli reunited them after the Archon Quest True Moon. She is among the few angels alive and whole by 7.1.

25.content: Nabu Malikata, Goddess of Flowers, was an angel (the wiki also counts her a Moon Envoy, from her title "Moon Maiden") who made the Jinn and Khvarena, and one of Sumeru's three companion-gods with Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and King Deshret. She joined Koitar's rebellion, helped hide the youngest sister, and warned Deshret against forbidden knowledge before agreeing to help him. She was killed by the Heavenly Principles; a portion of her remains was kept inside Collei until the Archon Quest "Your Past Is Like a Garden" removed it.

26.comment: Angel: The Lord of the Night as an angel
26.content: Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, is identified as an angel in Beneath the Secret Source. She rebuilt a Ley Line network from the broken lines of Natlan into the Night Kingdom, and the tribes communicated with her through obsidian and sacrifice. She is among the angels still alive in 7.1.

27.comment: Angel: Sybilla and Ursa the Drake
27.content: Sybilla, the Golden Bee, guarded the tree of Meropis until her form wore down to a golden bee, left with Remus to build Remuria, and died to create Phobos. Ursa the Drake is the opposite fate: an angel that chose power, became a dragon without an element, and plagued Mondstadt a thousand years ago until Barbatos drove it off and it was sealed. Eroch unsealed it for experiments with Dottore, and Varka, Diluc and the Traveler eventually killed it.

28.content: Mr. Nine, author of "Legend of the Shattered Halberd" and "Flowers for Princess Fischl", is in truth a female Seelie and former angel who possessed authors in their sleep to write Nicole's story ideas. She regained speech this way, and Nicole later sent her to watch the situation in Nod-Krai.

29.content:
Celestia (also: Sky Island): Celestia is the floating island that hangs in the sky above Teyvat, visible from most of the world. People call it the realm of the gods. It is the residence of the Heavenly Principles and the Four Shades, and each Archon of The Seven holds a divine throne there. The Heavenly Principles have been silent since the Cataclysm 500 years ago, but Celestia itself still watches over the world's laws. No one in the story has visited it on screen, and ordinary people know it only through legend.

Popular belief holds that great heroes can ascend to Celestia and become gods. Venti told the Traveler that every Vision holder is an "allogene" who could one day ascend. An Archon's Gnosis resonates directly with Celestia.

Established: - Celestia is a real, visible place in the sky, not a metaphor. In-game it floats roughly west-southwest of Mt. Mingyuan in Liyue, at a very high altitude.
- It is controlled by the Heavenly Principles, who have lain dormant since the Cataclysm.
- The Four Shades (Naberius, Ronova, Istaroth and Asmoday) reside there and serve the Heavenly Principles.

- In Ending Note (Prologue, 1.0) Venti explains that the Archons are not powered by Visions; each has an internal focus, the Gnosis, that resonates directly with Celestia.
- In the Sumeru Archon Quest (3.2), Nahida describes the Heavenly Principles as long silent and the Gnoses as symbols of their control over Teyvat and its laws.
- The Celestial Nails (also called nails of retribution or divine nails) are cast down from the heavens at the Heavenly Principles' command; they have devastated civilizations such as Hyperborea and Lang-Gan.
- Celestia keeps records of things that were erased from Irminsul. Rhinedottir says she once read Celestia's records about the Third Descender, whose existence had been wiped from the world's memory.

- The Four Shades hold periodic meetings in Celestia. The official teaser "The Gods' Limits" (July 2025) shows three of them meeting there; Asmoday has been missing since the Cataclysm and has not attended.
- According to Rhinedottir (7.1), the Third Descender ascended to Celestia to bargain with the Heavenly Principles, offering his body (split into seven pieces, later the Gnoses) in exchange for Anastasya's resurrection and protection for his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns.
- In the 7.0 Archon Quest, Ronova and Pierro both state that Paimon is a creation of Celestia (own entry).

Monitoring: As revealed in the 7.1 Archon Quest "A Rekviem for the Underworld", Celestia acts as a regulator even while the Heavenly Principles sleep. It runs a "monitoring cycle" set up by the Heavenly Principles that watches events across Teyvat and the conduct of the Four Shades. When it detects something that requires action, it issues a directive that the relevant Shade feels directly: Rhinedottir describes one "echoing" in her mind, ordering her to use the Authority of Life to undo Ronova's killings. After Ronova broke the rules, Celestia reclaimed her Authority of Death.

- Thresholds: Celestia does not react to everything. A monster that appeared in Snezhnaya was "not on Celestia's radar"; Naberius says such a case would simply be classed as spontaneous monster evolution. The Tsaritsa's use of six Gnoses to slow time in her hall was, in Naberius's words, a "rebellion" that Celestia cannot judge and that falls far short of the threshold for casting down a nail of retribution.
- The loophole: Rhinedottir and Ronova had agreed on a "window of resurrection" to slip past the monitoring system. The Tsaritsa slowed time around Rhinedottir so the window passed, Celestia detected the missed resurrection, and Ronova's Authority was reclaimed. Rhinedottir remarks that Celestia "gravely underestimated" the Tsaritsa's determination to rebel.
- Aftermath: Rhinedottir says that because she and Naberius could be considered accomplices, Celestia is watching them closely, and she would rather not lose the Authority of Life too. Asmoday's Authority of Space has not been rescinded despite her defection.

Appearance: Seen from below, Celestia is a cluster of landmasses rather than a single island: one large central rock surrounded by seven or eight smaller "satellite" rocks, linked by a ring-shaped structure and arches. The rocks look torn from the earth, with grass and forest on top and jagged undersides. White, marble-like buildings stand on the central mass, including a tall spire crowned by a huge golden construct resembling an astrolabe. Streams pour from the rock and dissolve into mist as they fall.

Accounts: Celestia is an enigma to Teyvat's people. Most believe chosen mortals ascend there to become gods and watch over the world.

- Mondstadt: Dr. Edith says only mortals who perform great, heroic feats can ascend and achieve godhood. Legend says Vennessa ascended from Windrise, where the great oak (the Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero) now grows, and became the Falcon of the West of the Four Winds.
- Liyue: some say adepti ascend to Celestia; others say adepti descended from Celestia and return there when they leave this world. Weapon lore claims the adeptus Guhua ascended instead of dying.
- Inazuma: a scholar's study of Sangonomiya folk belief records that gods defeated in the Archon War were slain "in accordance with the law of the divine realm", and that Orobashi may have gone to his death on heaven's order.

- Dainsleif on Vennessa: the Falcon of the West "ultimately does naught but hover under the light of the gods", implying that the ascended remain beneath Celestia's gods.
- Venti: in the manga, when the Traveler asks whether those who ascend truly become gods, Venti answers only with myths from "other, distant worlds" about primeval beings whose bodies became the world. He visibly avoids the topic.
- Anastasya (7.1) describes Celestia as holding "absolute power" and treating its rivals without respect; Rhinedottir denies that Celestia recognizes Snezhnaya as a rival at all.

History: - After seizing Teyvat from the dragons and remaking the world, the Heavenly Principles ruled from the heavens through envoys. Item text describes a calm era in which divine envoys (the angels) spoke openly with people, "bringing them the word from the heavens."
- The War of Funerary Flame ended that era. The heavens sent down the Celestial Nails to purge Abyssal corruption, which also devastated the mortal world, and the envoys were exiled and cut off from heaven.
- In the Archon War, the victors claimed the seven divine thrones; scholars in Teyvat widely believe Celestia instigated the war and set its rules.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Heavenly Principles are still asleep. Celestia's monitoring still works: it reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death in the Snezhnaya Archon Quest, and Ronova died soon after.

Snezhnaya openly prepares to challenge Celestia. Pierro (7.0) says kuuvahki alone cannot break through "Celestia's defenses", and Project Mistilteinn uses "anti-Celestia energy" reverse-engineered from Stellar Linchpins. Pierro says that Snezhnaya achieved its goal the moment Celestia reclaimed Ronova's Authority. In the act's closing scene, the Tsaritsa seems to be looking toward Celestia.

Before dying, Ronova infused the Eitr into the nail of retribution over the Cryo Dragon's corpse in Snezhnaya and it crumbled; afterwards huge beams of light appeared in the sky above the other Celestial Nails across Teyvat. What this means for Celestia is unresolved as of 7.1 (see the world quest "The Anomaly").

Open questions: - What Celestia actually is: a fortress, a city, a seat of administration or something stranger. Canon has never shown its interior in the game.
- Whether ascension really makes mortals gods, and what happened to those said to have ascended, such as Vennessa.
- What Paimon was in Celestia before she arrived in Khaenri'ah.

Connections: - Heavenly Principles: Celestia's ruler (own entry). Four Shades: its highest servants (own entry).
- The Seven: each holds a divine throne in Celestia; their Gnoses resonate with it.
- Celestial Nails: Celestia's weapons of judgment.

- Visions and allogenes: Vision holders are said to be candidates for ascension.
- Irminsul: Celestia keeps records of things erased from it.
- Paimon: a creation of Celestia (7.0).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat Celestia as a distant, silent presence in the sky that everyone can see but no one visits. Ordinary people speak of it with awe or superstition and know nothing of the monitoring cycle, the Shades' meetings or Paimon's origin; those are secrets known to a handful of gods, Harbingers and the Traveler's party. Do not stage scenes inside Celestia as if canon had described its interior, and do not make the Heavenly Principles speak or act directly as of 7.1.

30.content: The "monitoring cycle" is the Heavenly Principles' system for watching Teyvat and the Four Shades, revealed in "Black Feathers Scattered at Parting" (7.1). Incidents it detects trigger directives that echo in the minds of the responsible Shade. Minor events (a monster in Snezhnaya, the Tsaritsa's time-slowing trick) stay below its threshold. Rhinedottir and Ronova arranged a "window of resurrection" to bypass it, but the Tsaritsa's manipulation of time made the window lapse, Celestia detected the incident, and it reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death.

31.content: The Seven Archons each hold one of seven divine thrones (seats) in Celestia, won at the end of the Archon War together with a Gnosis. An Archon's elemental power comes from the throne's Authority, not from a Vision; the Gnosis is the focus that resonates with Celestia. Archons keep their thrones and power even after losing their Gnosis. The Hydro throne was destroyed in Fontaine.

32.content: In Teyvat's folk belief, mortals of great heroic deeds can ascend to Celestia, become gods and watch over their people. Venti tells the Traveler (Ending Note, 1.0) that every Vision holder is an "allogene" with the potential to ascend. Vennessa is said to have ascended at Windrise and become the Falcon of the West; Liyue lore says some adepti ascended, such as Guhua, though others believe adepti came from Celestia. Dainsleif implies that the ascended still live beneath the gods. Canon has never shown an ascension except Vennessa's in the manga, so its true nature is unconfirmed.

33.comment: Celestia: Paimon as a creation of Celestia
33.content: In the Snezhnaya Archon Quest (7.0, "Mistilteinn"), Ronova calls Paimon a creation of Celestia that has none of its power or authority. Pierro explains that he first used the Fatui's sky-pulling technology in Khaenri'ah over 500 years ago, aiming it at the heavens, and Paimon came down from Celestia in response. She lived in his palace until the Cataclysm; Pierro says her mind on arrival was like a newborn's. Paimon reacted to the Armory Palace's "anti-Celestia energy". She remembers none of this, and what she was in Celestia is unknown.

34.content:
Celestial Nail (also: Celestial Nails, Nail of Retribution, Nails of Retribution, divine nail, divine pillar): The Celestial Nails (also Nails of Retribution) are huge broken pillars, stone outside and blue crystal within, cast down from Celestia by the Heavenly Principles in the ancient past. Legend says they were sent to purify a world poisoned after the Funerary Year; they also wiped out or crippled civilizations such as Sal Vindagnyr, Lang-Gan and Hyperborea. Each reshaped climate and ley lines around it. In 7.1 a dying Ronova fuses the Eitr with the Snezhnaya nail and it begins to crumble, after which the other nails give off strange pillars of light.

Most people in Teyvat have never heard of them. Where a nail fell, mortals tend to remember only odd weather, ruins or a withered Irminsul.

Established: - Known nails: the Skyfrost Nail on Dragonspine; the Spiritstone in the Chasm (Lang-Gan); one beneath Sumeru's Mt. Damavand and Eternal Oasis; one on Tsurumi Island (not visible in game); one over Natlan's Night Kingdom; and the nail in Snezhnaya at Hyperborea's site. The 7.1 sky-beams mark these six.
- Impact leaves a crater: the pit around the Spiritstone and the depression in Mt. Damavand are examples. Four sites also have a withered Irminsul tree nearby (Dragonspine, the Chasm, Tsurumi Island, Mt. Damavand).
- Purification: Nahida says a nail can purify and stabilize powers that should not exist in Teyvat, such as forbidden knowledge. In the Chasm, Lumenstone and Lumenspar that appeared after a nail fragment was found repel Abyssal Dark Mud, and the Spiritstone's domain wipes out Abyssal power.
- Use as punishment: they were employed as weapons of retribution even before the War of Funerary Flame and the Abyss's arrival. Canon of the Three Moons says the Heavenly Principles cast them down to punish civilizations. In 7.1 Naberius says the Tsaritsa's "rebellion" falls far short of the threshold for casting down a nail of retribution, implying such a threshold exists.

- Material robustness: no nail is shown being destroyed before Ronova fused the Eitr with the Snezhnaya nail and it began to crumble.
- Nail fragments can move: the Skyfrost Nail split into three pieces after landing, and the Spiritstone had a detached piece (the Wishstone) in the Chasm's mines.
- Nails are named locally rather than uniformly; Liyue people, for example, call the Chasm one the Spiritstone.

Accounts: - Heavenly view (item texts): the Staff of the Scarlet Sands says the world's barriers were torn and dark poison seeped in, so spikes descended to heal it. Amethyst Crown says the master of the heavens, afraid of rising delusion and breakthroughs, sent a nail to mend the land and laid the mortal realm waste. Both are in-world artefact texts and their tone differs.
- Three Moons view: in The First Sliver of Moonlight, Canon says the ruler of the firmament feared life that sought power and cast down nails to punish civilizations; she tried to help the punished escape, but too many lives were lost. Columbina notes the Frostmoon Scions' ancestors were among those she helped. This was before the War of Funerary Flame.
- Albedo's belief (7.1): he had assumed the Skyfrost Nail's purpose ended once it destroyed Sal Vindagnyr, and says the new change shows it is not so simple.

- Sumeru legend: the first divine pillar buried a green land under sand (Shadow of the Sand King text). King Deshret is said to have found a nail and, with the jinn, made the Eternal Oasis as a resting place for Nabu Malikata; Paimon's guiding notes say the oasis is built upon a divine nail.
- Tsurumi Island: the Thunderbird is told that strange objects fell from the heavens and one landed on the island, after which storms cleared and fog began. Sumida guesses it may have caused a ley line disorder that mixed with the Thunderbird's power; this is speculation.

Open questions: Canon does not say whether the nails are meant to remain in place, why they now glow, or what the Eitr will do after the Snezhnaya nail's collapse.

Canon has not explained how many nails exist, whether Fontaine was ever struck, or whether Celestia can still recall them. The reading that Fontaine was never struck is a wiki observation from the absence of an Anomaly quest, not canon.

It is unresolved whether the nails' purifying power and their destructive power are the same function seen from two sides, as the Heavenly Principles' own texts imply.

Connections: Celestia and the Heavenly Principles cast them. The Abyss and forbidden knowledge are what they purify. Irminsul trees withered where nails fell. Ronova and the Eitr broke the Snezhnaya nail in 7.1. Dragonspine, the Chasm, Mt. Damavand, Tsurumi Island, the Night Kingdom and Hyperborea are the sites.

35.content:
The Skyfrost Nail fell over the summit of the mountain of Sal Vindagnyr (now Dragonspine), turning a green land into a blizzard. It split into three pieces, one of which fell on the Irminsul there (now the Frostbearing Tree). The priest Varuch died trying to reach the summit; the princess died trying to graft the tree. In the quest In the Mountains the Traveler thaws the shards with Scarlet Quartz; they rejoin the main nail, which rises to hover above the peak. In 7.1 it changes in the same way as the other nails, and Albedo stays to observe its effect on the surrounding ecosystem.

Ancient Rime blocked the summit paths until the quest, and a Mondstadt aristocratic expedition about a thousand years ago never returned, sabotaged by Eberhart according to the A Land Entombed quest.

36.content: In Liyue the Chasm's nail is known as the Spiritstone. Quests state Lang-Gan was destroyed by a nail. Miners found a fragment (the Wishstone) in the Stony Halls that gave hallucinations of wishes, and Lumenstone began to spread as Dark Mud appeared. In The Chasm Delvers the Traveler purifies the mechanisms feeding it and Yelan brings the nail down on the Ruin Serpent Haftvad; it then floats back lower than before. Later quests show its domain annihilates Abyssal power but doomed the Millelith soldiers and the yaksha Bosacius who sealed themselves inside.

37.comment: Celestial Nail: Hyperborea Nail and Ronova
37.content: Hyperborea, a golden city of the Unified Civilization, was destroyed by a nail because of the Cryo Dragon, whose latent power spread Holy Soil. The city fell into the Shadow Realm while the Sovereign's corpse and the nail remained above ground. In the 7.1 Archon Quest ending, a dying, stripped Ronova fused the Eitr with this nail, intending to spread the sensation of death and Holy Soil; the nail began to crumble as she disintegrated. Afterwards the remaining nails emitted beams of light, and the World Quest chain The Anomaly follows.

38.content:
Crimson Moon (also: crimson-red moon, Balemoon, Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon): The Crimson Moon is the baleful red moon of Khaenri'ah's old legends. It is in truth the shattered remnant of the Iridescent Moon, the third of the Three Moons, left when its goddess Sonnet fused with the Abyss to stay alive. Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty revered it and drew a power from its reflection. Its Balemoon Bloodfire still burns in the bloodline's last descendants, such as Arlecchino. Sonnet's marrow lay sealed in an Abyssal domain until the Traveler and Columbina entered it in the Nod-Krai Archon Quest (6.1), where Sonnet died for good.

Established: - Arlecchino states that the Crimson Moon is only the shattered Iridescent Moon, fused with the Abyss to prolong its life. Paimon checks her understanding: the Crimson Moon the Khaenri'ahns worshipped was really the Iridescent Moon, one of the Three Moon Sisters.
- Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty worshipped it. Columbina relates that a coup later saw it "eclipsed", and the Eclipse Dynasty took its place. Arlecchino suspects the Khaenri'ahns used the moon's remains mainly as their link to the Abyss rather than out of deep devotion.

- After the war of funerary flame the Iridescent Moon was shattered. Sonnet could not bear dying and fused her fading soul with the Abyss. This kept her barely alive as a broken husk, in lasting torment, and turned her moon into the Crimson Moon.
- The Iridescent Moon's marrow and remains were sealed in an Abyssal domain. Columbina cannot sense them anywhere in Teyvat. Lauma says Sonnet's remains vanished in an instant, so unlike Aria's they were never found in the overworld.
- The domain opens only briefly, through a ritual that needs Balemoon Bloodfire. The sages of the Crimson Moon Dynasty used the same rite to brand children received in their orphanage with the Crimson Moon's light (Arlecchino's reading of the Perinheri legend).

- The Balemoon Bloodfire is a fusion of the Iridescent Moon's former power and Abyssal corruption. It is also called the "Two Worlds' Flames", and Arlecchino calls herself one of its last surviving embers. It uses Abyssal energy, and she knows that if the corruption reached her heart she would become someone else, so she uses it with care.
- Arlecchino says she is an inheritor of the Crimson Moon's royal bloodline. She first saw her fire only as a curse; once she became a Harbinger, the Jester (Pierro) told her the truth, and she pieced together more through her own investigations. She does not know why the dynasty fell, and guesses that a rival faction found a way to touch the Abyss directly, or that an ideological split led to a coup that drove out the royal heirs.
- The Traveler can purify the Abyssal corruption on the marrow. In the domain they find the Iridescent Moon's broken husk hanging in the sky and its marrow hidden in the husk's reflection.
- The Universitas Magistrorum in Khaenri'ah kept a Moon Marrow laboratory devoted to studying the Crimson Moon's remains, where the researcher Tholindis worked.

History: Under the Crimson Moon Dynasty, Khaenri'ah revered the Crimson Moon. Its only direct account is the legend of Perinheri, which cannot be verified. In that legend a "crimson moon" shone over the subterranean realm, and a sage proposed an institution to house children from beyond the world, hoping one would have power to rise above the gods. The legend places a "dark sun" in the moon's stead later. Canon calls the dynasty that replaced the Crimson Moon Dynasty the Eclipse Dynasty, and it ruled until the Cataclysm 500 years ago.

Alchemy and the Beastmaster Knights were mainstays of the Crimson Moon era (Perinheri's footnotes), before the Eclipse Dynasty turned to mechanical engineering. The Crimson Moon sages wanted beings with powers beyond the gods, but feared losing control, so they put the children through a process of "refinement". Arlecchino reads that as branding, a mark by which they would live always in the Crimson Moon's light.

After the coup, the royal line of the Crimson Moon was driven out. Much later the last Eclipse ruler, the Vinster King (Irmin), still coveted the secrets it left behind and sent Rerir (the "Rächer of Solnari") to hunt its remaining followers, whom Jahoda calls the "Dregs of the Crimson Moon". The bloodline was never wholly wiped out. Tholindis, a distant descendant from a sub-branch whose family had cut ties long before, was Rerir's would-be fiancee: he had proposed, and she had deferred her answer. Before the Cataclysm she gave a piece of the Crimson Moon to Frithr, another descendant, so that the line would not fade. Frithr was captured, but Rerir spared her and told her to stay hidden.

Authority of death: In the 7.1 Archon Quest "A Rekviem for the Underworld", Pierro explains that before the Four Great Rulers (the Four Shades), the authorities of Life, Death, Time and Space belonged to the Three Moons. The Crimson Moon took up the responsibilities of death, and after the goddesses died, the broken Crimson Moon merged with the Abyss and acted as though its power had never been taken from it. Pierro and Arlecchino use this in a project to create more Delusions for the coming clash with Ronova, and Arlecchino's descent from the Crimson Moon is the reason she is wanted. In a test, researchers say the new Delusions also drew from "another authority" under the Crimson Moon's jurisdiction, adding an unstable variable, and the Traveler must pull Arlecchino out as the corrosion hits its maximum. The quest does not say what that authority was.

Open questions: - Canon does not say how Khaenri'ah first found the Crimson Moon, when the dynasty began, or why it fell.
- Perinheri is a legend; the wiki's reading of its "crimson moon" and "dark sun" as the two dynasties is interpretation.

- The exact reach of the Crimson Moon's authority over death is not defined, and "another authority" in the Delusion test is not named.
- Where the sealed domain lies, and how the marrow was taken there, is not explained.
- Whether "Solnari" is another name for the Crimson Moon or Sonnet is the wiki's inference only.

Connections: Sonnet and the Iridescent Moon (origin); the Three Moons and the Moon Marrows; the Abyss (the force it fused with); Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon and Eclipse Dynasties; Arlecchino, Tholindis, Frithr and Rerir; the weapon Crimson Moon's Semblance, whose story speaks of priests who prayed to a long-dead Crimson Moon and of the epithet "Balemoon" that outlived its name; Columbina.

Gameplay: Arlecchino's Elemental Burst is named "Balemoon Rising", and the Archon Quest title "Everlasting As the Moon" echoes one of her burst lines. Roleplay note (this project's guidance): treat the Balemoon Bloodfire as costly and corrupting, never as free power, and do not have an ordinary Khaenri'ahn descendant know the moon's true identity.

39.content: Balemoon Bloodfire is the flame carried by descendants of the Crimson Moon's royal bloodline. It is Sonnet's former power fused with Abyssal corruption, also called the "Two Worlds' Flames". It can leave afterimages of what it burns, and it is the key for opening the sealed domain of the Iridescent Moon's marrow. Using it slowly corrupts its holder. Arlecchino is among the last who carry it.

40.content: The Crimson Moon Dynasty is the earlier of Khaenri'ah's two known ruling dynasties, named for the moon it revered and overthrown in a coup by the Eclipse Dynasty. Little survives about it. Its sages operated an institution for children from beyond the world, which Pierro implies was the original House of the Hearth. Its surviving descendants, such as Tholindis and Frithr, were hunted under the Vinster King; Arlecchino is a present-day descendant. See the faction entry for fuller detail.

41.content: Crimson Moon's Semblance is a 5-star polearm. Its in-game description calls it a keen weapon whose luster dazzles like the crimson moon, once regarded by an ancient dynasty as a ritual object bridging two worlds. Its weapon story tells of dogmatic priests who convinced a king that the remnants of the Crimson Moon ruled all, and says that by the time of the "blackened sun" only the epithet "Balemoon" remained. In the Archon Quest, Arlecchino's scythe changes to an unascended Crimson Moon's Semblance when she opens the passage into the marrow's resting place.

42.content:
Descender (also: Descenders, First Descender, Second Descender, Third Descender, Fourth Descender): "Descender" is the term for the rare beings from beyond Teyvat (from the sea of stars) whose wills can rival a whole world. They are not bound by the Heavenly Principles' laws, and Irminsul does not hold their memories. Only four are known: the First, the Heavenly Principles (now dormant); the Second, the dragon king Nibelung (slain); the Third, Saarelainen (killed, his remains made into the seven Gnoses); and the Fourth, the Traveler (alive). The Traveler's twin is not counted as one. Very few people in Teyvat know the term at all.

Nahida first learned the term from Fatui intelligence that Dottore gave her in exchange for the Dendro Gnosis (3.2). The moon goddesses, dragons, the Fatui and the Fontainian scholar Rene also use it, each in their own way.

Established: - **Outside fate's rules.** A Descender is not bound by the laws the Heavenly Principles impose on Teyvat. The Narzissenkreuz called the Traveler a "variable" that had come into the world and one "equal to a world" (4.2).
- **Outside Irminsul.** In 3.3 the Balladeer searched Irminsul for Descenders and found nothing. Nahida concluded that anyone from beyond this world is not counted as part of Teyvat. When Irminsul is rewritten, a Descender's memories stay unchanged. The Traveler alone remembered Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, and later the Balladeer, when everyone else forgot them.
- **Not every outlander qualifies.** Coming from beyond Teyvat is not enough. Rene wrote that the title belongs only to "wills that can rival an entire world". Skirk, who came from another planet, said she is not one, because she is only passing through, while the Traveler is influencing the world's fate (5.7). The Fatui do not count the Traveler's sibling either.
- **The count.** First: the Heavenly Principles. Second: Nibelung. Third: Saarelainen. Fourth: the Traveler.

- **The First** came from the sea of stars, defeated the Seven Sovereigns and remade the world. Canon, one of the moon sisters, says the sisters fulfilled their duty in the heavens "until the day that the first Descender arrived" (6.3). Nahida had already guessed this in 3.2. *Before Sun and Moon* calls this being the Primordial One and the first "throne of the heavens".
- **The Second** is inferred to be Nibelung, the dragon king and Teyvat's original ruler. He created the three moons to watch over the world and left for the stars, then came back to fight the Heavenly Principles in the war of funerary flame. He was killed, but his enemy was badly wounded.
- **The Third**, Saarelainen, is the source of the seven Gnoses. That the Gnoses are a Descender's remains first came out in Fontaine (4.2). The name Saarelainen comes from the Frostmoon Scions' *Hymns of the Far North* (6.0), which tell of Anastasya's lover; his full story came out in Snezhnaya (7.1).
- **The Fourth** is the Traveler, an outlander who travelled between worlds with their twin. Nahida tells them this in 3.2, and in Nod-Krai the Traveler names themselves a Descender to Lauma.
- **Gods find them hard to handle.** Ronova says a Descender's soul cannot be drawn into the Ley Lines and that, for now, she does not mean to get involved with Descenders (7.0). In 7.1, after killing the Traveler during the curse of death, she says she does not understand what the Heavenly Principles value so much about Descenders, and warns that this tolerance has limits. She points to the Third Descender's remains as the example.

Accounts: - **Fatui intelligence (3.2):** the Fatui records Dottore traded to Nahida for the Dendro Gnosis count the Traveler as the Fourth Descender and do not classify the sibling as one. Nahida called the Descender intel a very important part of what she received.
- **Rene de Petrichor (Fontaine):** working from Khaenri'ahn, Remurian and Sumeru sources, he concluded that Descenders are wills that can rival a world. He tried to become one so he could save Fontaine from its prophecy, and failed twice. In the end the prophecy was resolved through the Traveler's involvement.
- **Khaenri'ah:** *Perinheri* says the kingdom waited for "beings who could transcend the gods" to come from outside the world, and that none came in its writer's time.
- **Dragons (5.2):** a dragon in the Ashen Realm calls the Heavenly Principles simply "the Descender", the one who brought humans into Teyvat.
- **The moon sisters (6.3):** Canon and Aria say the first Descender was at first a peaceful "guest in our home" who slowly came to want to change and rule the world.
- **Rhinedottir (7.1):** she read Celestia's own records of "the Third Descender incident" and told the Tsaritsa what happened (see the Third Descender entry).

Open questions: - Who first set the numbering, and how Nibelung, a native ruler, came to count as a Descender and as Second rather than First.
- How Saarelainen could be erased through Irminsul if Irminsul keeps no records of Descenders.
- Whether a native of Teyvat can ever become a Descender.
- What the Heavenly Principles want from the Traveler, and why Celestia tolerates them.

43.content:
The First Descender is the being now called the Heavenly Principles. It came from the sea of stars, defeated the Seven Sovereigns, took their Authorities and rebuilt the world. Nahida guessed this identity in 3.2, and the moon sister Canon stated it in Nod-Krai (6.3).

The moon goddesses first lived beside it in peace, until it showed a growing wish to change and rule the world and a near-paranoid hostility toward beings who seek power. *Before Sun and Moon* remembers it as the Primordial One, which created four shining shades of itself. It won the war of funerary flame, but its functions were badly damaged. Since the Cataclysm it has been dormant because of the Third Descender's curse (revealed in 7.1).

44.content:
The Second Descender is generally taken to be Nibelung, the dragon king. He was Teyvat's original ruler and created the three moons and their goddesses to keep the world running. After leaving for the sea of stars he came back and fought the Heavenly Principles for dominance in the war of funerary flame, a war Lauma says was "triggered by the Descenders". Canon never names him "Second Descender" directly; the label is inferred.

During the war he imprisoned the moon goddesses and turned the moons into weapons. The Heavenly Principles shattered two moons and threw the third beyond the sky. Nibelung was killed, but he wounded his enemy so badly that it could no longer fully suppress the world's original order. *Before Sun and Moon* calls him the "second throne of the heavens" and says the Primordial One must have defeated the Second Who Came.

45.content:
The Third Descender, Saarelainen, came from beyond Teyvat. He loved Anastasya, the future Tsaritsa, and their descendants became the Khaenri'ahns. Rhinedottir later told the story from Celestia's records (7.1). The Belyi Tsar incited Anastasya and Saarelainen to open the gate to the Abyss, which let in Abyssal disaster, and the Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya as punishment. Saarelainen went up to Celestia and bargained for her. His body, which had an unparalleled affinity for the power of Teyvat's Human Realm and could amplify the elements, would be split into seven pieces, the Gnoses, to support the Archon system. In return the Heavenly Principles would bring Anastasya back and never harm his descendants.

In exchange, the Heavenly Principles demanded that he be forgotten, and they used Irminsul to erase every trace of him. Only the Belyi Tsar, hidden in the Shadow Realm, kept his memories. Saarelainen made sure the promise would be kept by laying a curse that would take effect if it was broken. Anastasya concludes that when the Heavenly Principles acted against Khaenri'ah in the Cataclysm, the curse struck, and that this is why they have slept ever since. Ronova calls his remains the gods' playthings. Skirk (4.2) had already told Neuvillette that the Gnoses are the Third Descender's remains and that holding one brings misfortune.

46.comment: Descender: Legacy of the Third Descender
46.content: The Gnoses are not part of Teyvat's own system. They have a strong elemental affinity and amplify their holders' power. The Tsaritsa says they cannot stay in the Ley Lines for long, so a Gnosis absorbed there will be expelled one day.
