The Third Descender, Saarelainen, then traded his body to become the seven Gnoses. In return it restored her and promised never to harm his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. Its price was that it wiped him from all memory through Irminsul. He bound the promise with a curse that would strike if it was broken, and Anastasya concludes that this curse is why it has slept since the Cataclysm.

The Belyi Tsar had incited Anastasya and Saarelainen to open the gate, and Saarelainen made the deal in person in Celestia. Anastasya concluded that harming Khaenri'ah in the Cataclysm triggered the curse, and Rhinedottir did not dispute it. Neuvillette's Vision text tells it from the other side: the wounded "usurper" and "one who came after" made the Gnoses together to keep the world's resentment under control.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is still asleep. Celestia's monitoring cycle keeps watching Teyvat and the Shades, and in 7.1 it reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death.

The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses and is preparing to face it. The Traveler's sibling says it will certainly wake.

Pierro's Project Mistilteinn is a weapon meant for that confrontation. In 7.1 Pulcinella explains that a notebook was sealed away for fear that Snezhnaya might become a "Second Khaenri'ah" by drawing the attention of the Heavenly Principles and its sustainer. Earlier upheavals did not wake it: the end of the Hydro throne (4.2) and Nahida burning Irminsul (6.6). In Sumeru, Nahida had wondered whether destroying a Gnosis might wake it. See the separate entry on its dormancy.

Accounts: - Moon goddesses (Aria, Canon, Sonnet; 6.3): a guest who turned conqueror, whose rules brought order at too high a price.
- Dragons (Neuvillette, Apep): "First Usurper", "Usurper-King", "usurper from beyond the heavens". They say its stolen dragon power became the Archons' Authorities (Neuvillette, 4.1). Apep says dragons once believed only forbidden knowledge could beat it.
- Enkanomiya historians (Before Sun and Moon): the reverently named Primordial One, true lord and creator.
- Frostmoon Scions (Hymns of the Far North): Pitkamoonen, Lord of the Seven Calamities, a god to be placated, not invoked.
- Celestia's servants: Ronova was titled its Arbiter, and Asmoday called herself the Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles.
- Nicole (6.2): the moon goddesses could not challenge it, but it tolerated them because they kept the planet alive. It may never have known that Nibelung had imprisoned them, and so treated the moons' weaponisation as a breach of peace.
- Furina (4.2): its will "will have its way". Pierro calls every divine rule, even a god's love for humanity, a curse.

Open questions: - When it will wake, and what it will do to Snezhnaya when it does.
- Why it values Descenders such as the Traveler.
- What Saarelainen sealed beneath Zapolyarny Palace.
- How far it intended the Archon War, and what it did in person in the Cataclysm.
- Whether it is the "creator who has not yet returned" in the Traveler's profile (fan inference only).

Connections: Its seat is Celestia. The Four Shades are its parts, and The Seven sit on its thrones. Its works include the Gnoses, Visions (through the Archon system), the false sky, a refashioned Irminsul, the nails and fate. Its foes are Nibelung, the Abyss, Khaenri'ah, the Tsaritsa, the Abyss Order and Apep.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation): keep it offstage. It is asleep, has no present-day voice, and has never been shown speaking. Show it through Celestia's directives, the Shades, the nails and people's reluctance to name it. Commoners know "Celestia" and "the gods", not this history.

Do not reduce it to pure evil or pure good. Canon shows both its "deep love" for humanity and its brutality toward civilisations that test its rules.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): - The "unknown god" who separated the twins is Asmoday, "Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles", not the Heavenly Principles itself.
- "The Second Who Came" in Before Sun and Moon means Nibelung.
- It is not an Archon, and it is dormant, not dead. Do not give it a fixed gender, a face or dialogue.

89.comment: Heavenly Principles: Before Sun and Moon on the Primordial One
89.content:
Before Sun and Moon, a banned history in The Byakuyakoku Collection, is the fullest in-world account of the Primordial One. When the "eternal throne of the heavens" came, it fought the seven dragon-lords and made four shining Shades of itself. After forty years the Sovereigns fell and the nations submitted. Four hundred years after "the Held Branches", it and one Shade created animals, plants and humans, who made a covenant with it and entered a new age. The author suggests the Primordial One "may have been Phanes", a winged, crowned, androgynous being born from an egg, who used the eggshell to separate the universe from the "microcosm of the world".

The book records that in the Funerary Year the "second throne" came and war returned, and that after Enkanomiya fell into the depths the Primordial One and three Shades did not hear its prayers. Later a ban from the "first throne" blocked the road home, so the author reasons it must have defeated "the Second Who Came". Possessing the book was forbidden after Orobashi's death.

90.comment: Heavenly Principles: The covenant and the Unified Civilization
90.content: Under the covenant, the heavens answered hunger with food and rain, poverty with riches and sorrow with their voices, and the one taboo was temptation. Angels walked among humans as its envoys. Artifact text (Tiara of Frost, Tiara of Flame) says it also set a hidden rule of "cyclical eternity" under which civilisations flourish and are remade, and that humans who asked the angels about it met only silence.

91.comment: Heavenly Principles: Saarelainen's curse on the Heavenly Principles
91.content: Saarelainen's curse was the safeguard on his bargain with the Heavenly Principles: it would strike if the promise to spare his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns, was broken. Anastasya concluded in 7.1 that the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah triggered it, and that this is why the Heavenly Principles sleeps. His body became the seven Gnoses, and the Heavenly Principles erased all memory of him through Irminsul.

92.content: The Heavenly Principles set up a "monitoring cycle" through which Celestia watches events in Teyvat and the conduct of the Four Shades, even while the Heavenly Principles sleeps. In 7.1, Ronova and Rhinedottir tried to schedule a resurrection inside a gap in it. The Tsaritsa used her Cryo power and the six Gnoses to slow time in her hall so the window passed, and Celestia reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death. A directive then "echoed" in Rhinedottir's mind ordering her to undo Ronova's killings. Naberius judged that this act of rebellion fell short of what would warrant a nail.

93.comment: Heavenly Principles: Epithets of the Heavenly Principles
93.content: The Heavenly Principles has many titles in different sources: Usurper-King and First Usurper (Neuvillette), All-Plunderer (the quest Sealed Site of Sacrifice), Master of Fortuna and Master of the Four Shades (artifact texts), Lord of Hosts and Lord of the Eternal Heavens (moon-related artifact texts), Great Judge (a noble's notes) and King of Light (General History of Snezhnaya), Winged One (Scroll of Streaming Song and artifact text), Sovereign of the Firmament (the quest For a Green Island...) and great ruler of the firmament (the moon goddesses). Pitkamoonen, Lord of the Seven Calamities and Lord of the Sky are Frostmoon Scion names. Its Chinese name 天理 means "heaven's law" or natural order.

94.content:
Holy Soil (also: Holy Soil phenomenon, hallowing of soil, Holy Soil of primordial ice): Holy Soil is land that holds a high concentration of the primordial elemental power of the three realms. Dragons can thrive in it; humans cannot live or farm on it. The process of land becoming Holy Soil is called the Holy Soil phenomenon. Canon shows it on Watatsumi Island, in ancient Natlan and across ancient Snezhnaya, and at the end of Version 7.1 Ronova tries to give it to the whole world.

The term is used by different speakers for different places, so a character should say which land they mean. It is a lore term, not a gameplay status or zone.

Established: - Watatsumi: local folklore says the island's spirit hears the call of Enkanomiya and sinks toward its depths. The Sangonomiya Shrine sends someone to Enkanomiya every few centuries to fetch a Bloodbranch Coral left by Orobashi to seal the vishaps, then performs the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri to make the sunken spirit return.
- What the ritual really does (Tsumi, in the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event): it awakens Orobashi's second familiars, the Sangacorallia, creatures that break the Light Realm's primitive elemental energy down into the milder energy of the Human Realm.
- During the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event (Version 2.5) the ritual did not reverse the phenomenon but only stopped it, which Kokomi says had never happened before. Investigation showed the Void Realm had invaded Enkanomiya and suppressed interaction between the Light Realm and the Human Realm. The matter was resolved, but the source of the Bloodbranch Coral was cut off when the vishaps rescued their sealed kin.
- Natlan: the speaker the wiki identifies as Kukulkan says that, in an earlier eon, the Heavenly Principles regarded the phlogiston-rich soil that sustained Natlan as Holy Soil and cast sky-nails down to destroy the land. Dragons, being adaptable, were forced to devolve to survive in the new Natlan and became the saurians, though their bloodline did not change.
- Snezhnaya: Aksinya, citing record fragments from the Shadow Realm, says that when Hyperborea tried to make the Primordial Human from the Cryo Dragon Sovereign's corpse, the experiment ran out of control, and the corpse's unchecked authority turned the whole of Snezhnaya into the Holy Soil of primordial ice. Ley lines there became veins of pure crystal. The Heavenly Principles then sent a nail down on Hyperborea, which sank into the Shadow Realm.

- Dragons and the vishaps belong to the Light Realm, the realm of pure primordial elemental beings, so land close to its power suits them.
- Eboshi (The Three Great Martial Trials) tells the Traveler that the phenomenon is the expansion of the Bathysmal Vishaps' habitat, meaning primordial power is growing stronger, and that only Watatsumi Omikami's life force awakening a second servant lets the Sangonomiya convert this raw power.
- Version 7.1: Ronova, dying and stripped of her authority, fuses the Eitr with the nail above the Cryo Dragon's corpse. The cutscene text of her last words describes giving the feeling of death and the hallowing of soil to the world. The nail crumbles and light rises from the other nails (see Celestial Nail).

Accounts: - Folklore: Enkanomiya's depths draw away Watatsumi's spirit, bleaching the soil.
- Tsuyuko (a shrine maiden who attended the Sumeru Akademiya): seawater leaches nutrients; Orobashi's Jade Coral Branch replenishes the missing elements and holds off the bleaching.
- Eboshi: the soil is the vishaps' habitat growing, a sign that primordial power is strengthening.
- Kokomi: the Matsuri is meant to reverse the process; during the limited-time 2.5 event it only paused it, and once she learned how the Bloodbranch Coral works she said she may need to think of a new way to counteract the phenomenon.

- Kukulkan (Natlan) and Aksinya (Snezhnaya) both describe the Heavenly Principles as ending Holy Soil with a nail, each from their own side of events; the heavenly motive is never given in the Principles' own words.

Open questions: Canon does not say what Holy Soil is at a physical level, or whether the nails cure or merely suppress it.

It is unresolved whether the Holy Soil Ronova meant to release in 7.1 is actually spreading, whether it helps or harms living dragons and vishaps, and what it would do to farmland.

Whether the Watatsumi bleaching and the nail-ended cases are the same process is never stated; the shared name is the only direct link in canon.

Connections: The three realms and the Light Realm supply the power. Celestial nails and the Heavenly Principles are the response in Natlan and Snezhnaya. Dragons, vishaps and saurians are the beings tied to it. Watatsumi Island, the Sangonomiya Shrine, Enkanomiya, Hyperborea, the Cryo Dragon, the Eitr and Ronova are the places and figures involved.

95.comment: Holy Soil: Holy Soil on Watatsumi Island
95.content: Watatsumi's soil is bleaching and losing nutrients. In The Moon-Bathed Deep, Tsuyuko explains that a Jade Coral Branch left by the Omikami must be retrieved from Enkanomiya for the shrine's ritual (called the Watatsumi Mitama Omatsuri in that quest). Tsuyuko privately attributes the bleaching to seawater leaching nutrients from the soil.

96.comment: Holy Soil: Holy Soil and the Three Realms Gateway Offering
96.content: During the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event (Version 2.5), Kokomi's Bloodbranch Coral ritual only paused the Holy Soil phenomenon instead of reversing it, which she says had never happened before. Tsumi explains that the ritual really awakens the Sangacorallia, which convert raw primordial energy into the milder energy of the Human Realm, and that darkness from the Void Realm was stalling them. The problem was resolved, but the coral supply ended, and Kokomi says she may need a new way to counteract the phenomenon.

97.comment: Holy Soil: Holy Soil in Natlan and Snezhnaya
97.content: Kukulkan says a nail was cast on phlogiston-rich Natlan and forced the dragons there to devolve into saurians. Aksinya says the Cryo Dragon's corpse turned Snezhnaya into the Holy Soil of primordial ice until a nail struck Hyperborea. At the end of 7.1 Ronova breaks the Snezhnaya nail with the Eitr, meaning to give the world the feeling of death and the hallowing of soil.

98.content:
Iridescent Moon (also: Sonnet's moon, moon of Sonnet): The Iridescent Moon was the third and smallest of the Three Moons, raised by the Dragon King Nibelung and governed by Sonnet, the youngest of the Three Moon Sisters. Its light was the faintest of the three, barely visible to the naked eye, but it produced fleeting halos when it shone. The Heavenly Principles shattered it in the war of funerary flame. Sonnet, in agony over her broken moon, fused her fading soul with the Abyss to stay alive, and the Iridescent Moon became the baleful Crimson Moon. Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty later worshipped it as a source of Abyssal power. Its husk and Abyss-corrupted Moon Marrow were hidden in an otherworldly domain, which the Traveler and Columbina entered in the Nod-Krai Archon Quest (6.1).

Established: - Smallest and last-made of the Three Moons; its goddess was Sonnet.
- Faint light, fleeting halos.
- Shattered, then fused with the Abyss as the Crimson Moon.

- Nibelung made the moons with Secret Source technology and raised them from the planet's crust at what is now Nod-Krai.
- Sonnet shared sovereignty of the night sky with her sisters, one at a time, riding in a silver carriage. The English text says they switched about three times a month; the Chinese uses the looser unit xun.
- When the moon fell, the sisters' carriage was overturned and the palace of the stars ransacked, according to the Liyue book Moonlit Bamboo Forest.

- Sonnet is shown as a tall, fair woman with long pink hair and pink eyes, in white robes lined with purple and pink, with a pink crescent behind her and a laurel-like circlet. Everlasting As the Moon also gives her the title "Mistress of the Seven Hues".
- Sonnet was the one sister who spoke against the Heavenly Principles' new order, though she deferred when Aria and Canon chose to watch and wait.
- The dragons treated the sisters as traitors and cheered the moons' destruction.

History: Nibelung left, the sisters kept Teyvat for him, and then the Heavenly Principles arrived and were received as guests. After Nibelung returned and imprisoned the sisters, the Heavenly Principles shattered the moon. Sonnet fused the remains with the Abyss.

Sonnet was horrified at the Heavenly Principles' treatment of anyone who challenged them, and thought it excessive for the offences. After the Heavenly Principles overthrew the Seven Sovereigns, the sisters entered a precarious peace with them, which the dragons saw as betrayal. When Nibelung returned from the Abyss, the sisters disagreed about whether to take sides. He took it for disloyalty, sealed them in the moon's reflection and made their moons into weapons. The Heavenly Principles shattered the Iridescent and Eternal Moons and threw the Frost Moon beyond the false sky.

Sonnet stayed imprisoned in the reflection after her moon was shattered, ignorant of the war. In True Moon (6.3) a future Columbina reached her, and the truth shocked her. Of the three sisters she feared death most and looked to the others for comfort as the prison began to wear down her body. The sisters gave Columbina the authority of all three moons and asked to be sent back to Teyvat, mortal, where history records they died.

Leaving the prison meant death, because a moon goddess cannot live without her moon. Seeing the shattered Iridescent Moon was an agony and a terror for Sonnet. To prolong her life she fused her fading soul with the Abyss (A Nation That Doesn't Exist). This kept her barely alive, in perpetual torment, and turned her into the Crimson Moon. Light Realm power and Abyssal power were mixed in her.

Her Marrow and the moon's husk then ended up sealed in an Abyssal domain, by means canon does not explain, so unlike Aria's remains they were never found in the overworld. Lauma says Sonnet's remains vanished in an instant.

Crimson moon era: Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty found the Crimson Moon and used it as a conduit to the Abyss. The domain holding its Marrow was sealed and could be opened only temporarily by a ritual. The dynasty's sages used the ritual in an induction ceremony in their otherworldly orphanage, branding the children with the Crimson Moon's light. Its power appears in the royal bloodline as the Balemoon Bloodfire, which is Sonnet's former power fused with Abyssal energies and can leave afterimages of whoever it burns. Hence the name "Two Worlds' Flames".

Everlasting as the moon: About 500 years after the Cataclysm, Columbina and the Traveler wanted the Iridescent Moon Marrow to restore Columbina's kuuvahki against the revived Rerir in Nod-Krai. Arlecchino, one of the last descendants of the Crimson Moon bloodline, used her Balemoon Bloodfire to open the path to the moon's burial grounds. Inside they found the broken husk hanging in the sky and the Abyss-corrupted Marrow in its reflection. The Traveler absorbed the Abyssal power and restored the Marrow to its pure essence.

Present day: As of 7.1 the Iridescent Moon is a broken husk in a sealed Abyssal domain, Sonnet is dead, and its Marrow is held by Arlecchino. The shadowmoon illusion is gone and only the Frost Moon, returned under the false sky, lights the night.

Accounts: - Liyue books say the sisters died fighting each other, or that only two died and the moon in the sky is one of their corpses. Treat these as folk memory.
- Dragon-side accounts treat the sisters as traitors to Nibelung.

- The Mitternachts Waltz text says two of three bright moons were "shredded by a sword".

Open questions: - Who or what sealed the Marrow in the Abyssal domain, and when.
- What the dark presence in the domain was. Canon does not say.

- Whether "Solnari" on the teaser note is another name for Sonnet or her moon.
- Whether the Balemoon Bloodfire survives now that Sonnet is gone.

Connections: Sonnet (its goddess); Nibelung (creator); the Heavenly Principles (destroyers); the Abyss (what it fused with); the Crimson Moon, the Crimson Moon Dynasty and Khaenri'ah; Arlecchino and the Balemoon Bloodfire; Columbina, Dottore and the Traveler; the Frost Moon and the Eternal Moon (siblings).

99.content: The Iridescent Moon Marrow was sealed in the Crimson Moon's domain, corrupted by the Abyss. The Traveler cleansed it (6.1) and Columbina gave it to Arlecchino. Dottore stole it, and after his defeat Columbina returned it to her again.

100.content: The Balemoon Bloodfire is the form the Crimson Moon's power takes in the bloodline of Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty: Sonnet's old power mixed with Abyssal energy, able to leave afterimages of what it burns. Arlecchino used it to open the way to the moon's burial grounds.

101.content:
Irminsul (also: World Tree, Sarva, Irminsul tree, Irminsul trees, silver-white tree): Irminsul is the primordial silver-white world tree of Teyvat. It grows downward in a vast cavern deep underground, and the Ley Lines are its roots. Through them it gathered the world's memories into one repository. The Dendro Archon's consciousness is bound to it, and outsiders such as the Traveler have no records in it. In Version 6.6, after Dottore hijacked and corrupted it, Nahida burned Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis, and Aaru took over its role.

Irminsul is older than the Heavenly Principles. They took it over and remade it into a recorder of all information and an anchor for the world's fate.

Established: Tighnari (3.0) says the Dendro Archon is called the God of Wisdom because of this link, and that her power is said to be a manifestation of Irminsul.

Silver-white trees with glowing blue streaks, known as "withered trees", Petrified Trees or Irminsul trees, are parts of Irminsul across Teyvat. Domains, Ley Line Outcrops and Ley Line Blossoms belong to the same network. A mind can connect to Irminsul: the Dendro Archon does so by nature, and the Traveler briefly did in Chronic Illness. Fate is written into the tree; Nahida says the Fontaine prophecy was "carved into Irminsul long ago".

- Original Resin text says the silver-white trees and blossoms intertwine in the deepest place in the earth, and that the pattern of their roots defines the Ley Lines.
- Scholars also connect to Irminsul to produce the Akasha's Knowledge Capsules. Some forest dwellers, such as Haypasia, try through meditation and Spirit Borneol, but many who attempt such a connection go mad.
- The innermost region is made only of torrents of information. Small saplings sprout there as packets of data; touching one carries a visitor elsewhere in the space. It is easy to get lost. The "heart" is a huge glowing tree whose branches look like circuitry (The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call, 3.3).
- The Raiden Shogun said that as long as the Ley Lines flow, the erosion of time never stops. Wiki analysis links Irminsul to that flow.
- Lisa's voice-over about Mona mentions that the Hexenzirkel go on Irminsul expeditions.

Origins: Apep (6.6) says the Heavenly Principles did not plant Irminsul. It existed in the age of the dragons, looked and worked very differently, and its Ley Lines carried the power of the Light Realm. The Heavenly Principles took it over, made it serve humanity and used it to anchor fate.

Apep adds that in the end humanity failed to protect it. The Worldspan Fern item says the first fern sprouted in Apep's verdant court and that later plants came from those first fronds; the wiki identifies that first frond as Irminsul. In the 6.6 Archon Quest, Istaroth calls Irminsul "the original tree of Teyvat" and the means by which the Heavenly Principles maintain fate.

Memory and erasure: Purging information from Irminsul takes power on the level of a god. A purge rewrites everything recorded about its subject, including memories, books and letters. The events and their consequences remain, but people remember different causes or different actors. Natives of Teyvat never notice the change, Archons and Paimon included. Only beings with no records, such as the Traveler, keep the original memories.

A being cannot fully erase itself: Scaramouche erased his past (3.3) but went on existing as the Wanderer. Erased information can be kept if it is abstracted so that it still resonates with what Irminsul records. Nahida gave Scaramouche a memory block for this purpose. Once restored, information does not vanish again. The wiki notes that Weapon and Artifact descriptions never change after a purge.

History: - About 6,000 years ago (per item text), Celestia's Skyfrost Nail shattered an Irminsul tree on Dragonspine. Durin's blood later revived it as the Frostbearing Tree.
- In the distant past, the Heavenly Principles used Irminsul to erase the Third Descender, Saarelainen (revealed 7.1).
- Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who died about 500 years ago, was polluted by forbidden knowledge. Through her link she went on polluting Irminsul after her death, and the Withering was a sign of that corruption.
- 3.2: Nahida removed Rukkhadevata from Irminsul. With the Traveler, she erased the forbidden knowledge. Nahida's Irminsul search found records of the Traveler's sibling, which is unexpected for an outsider, and they grow fuzzy near the end of the sibling's journey.
- 3.3: Scaramouche tried to erase himself.
- 6.2: In Nod-Krai, the Wanderer says he was built from a branch once connected to the main Irminsul tree.
- 6.6: Dottore hijacked Irminsul, and Nahida burned it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Irminsul is destroyed; only its underground parts remain. Aaru, King Deshret's unfinished afterlife, was rebuilt to collect and store the world's information in its place.

Nahida says the fire burned for seven days and nights, and most of Teyvat's vital information was saved. Nicole moved Nahida's connection to Aaru, so the loss did her no harm. With Irminsul burned, Nahida says, fate "now carries many more possibilities." The Pyro Gnosis vanished in the fire.

Accounts: - Tighnari's ancestors learned from Rukkhadevata's familiars that Irminsul was sick, but even those creatures knew no cure.
- Apep says the tree is older than the Heavenly Principles, who usurped it. Istaroth says it is how they maintain fate. Nahida says it exists to protect humanity and can therefore be sacrificed for humanity.
- The Belyi Tsar's notes say the Goddess of Flowers in Sumeru sought to build a system independent of the Ley Lines and Heimarmene.
- Albedo says Truly Ancient Petrified Trees grow one or two miles high, with a large spider living around their roots.

Open questions: Canon leaves several things open: where the main tree stood relative to the Abyss (Prototype Crescent mentions Irminsul branches brought back from the abyss); why the Traveler's sibling was recorded; whether the silver-white trees across Teyvat changed after the burning; where the Pyro Gnosis went; and how far the Heavenly Principles' hold on fate has loosened.

Connections: Ley Lines (its roots), Nahida, Aaru (its successor), the Heavenly Principles and fate.

Also the Akasha, Descenders (who are not recorded), the Withering and forbidden knowledge (its corruption), Dottore (who hijacked it), the Wanderer (made from one of its branches) and the domains.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): after 6.6, Irminsul is gone and Aaru holds the world's memory. Natives must not remember erased people or events, such as Greater Lord Rukkhadevata or Scaramouche's original history; only the Traveler, other outsiders and those whose records were restored know the old versions.

Outside Sumeru, most people know at most about the crisis and the sealed border. Silver-white trees, Ley Line Blossoms and domains are still part of the landscape; canon has not said they changed. Treat a mind link to the world's memory as dangerous for anyone but a Dendro Archon.

102.content:
In Version 6.6 (Song of the Welkin Moon, Acts IX and X), Nahida fell into a coma, chaos spread through Sumeru from the Ley Lines, and finally a giant Irminsul tree rose in Sumeru City. Dottore had entered Irminsul through death, a route Nahida could have closed only by cutting every soul off from the Ley Lines. Once he was inside, her authority was quickly restricted, and Pantalone had placed Dottore's last backup in the Ley Lines. Sumeru's defenders overloaded Irminsul with the Akasha to stop its growth. Wanderer and the Traveler went inside while the world's information was moved into Aaru. Nahida invoked her "supreme authority as the keeper of Irminsul" and lit the Pyro Gnosis, which Mavuika had given her. Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius consented, and the flames burned the tree and Dottore with it.

Ronova asked whether Nahida would really abandon what she had always fought for. Nahida answered that Irminsul exists to protect humanity, so humanity, and she as one of its protectors, come first. Naberius replied that since she had become "a great tree" herself, she need not fear losing another. Dottore tried to drag the Traveler into the flames, but the Segments he had deleted dragged him down instead.

103.content: The Heavenly Principles set a rule: if Irminsul is in grave danger, part of its power seals off Sumeru to protect the rest of Teyvat. Pollution alone never set it off; Dottore's direct invasion in 6.6 did. The barrier cut Sumeru off and stopped trade with Natlan. Only the Traveler, who has no record in Irminsul, could walk through it. They absorbed Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis with their Pyro mastery and carried it in. The meeting was held so that Irminsul could not record it.

104.comment: Irminsul: Aaru as the new Irminsul
104.content: King Deshret built Aaru with illicit celestial technology as an unfinished afterlife, and it once held three of his Seven Pillars prisoner. In 6.6 Sumeru's scholars reprogrammed it, and during the battle the world's information was moved into it out of Irminsul. Aaru now collects and stores what the Ley Lines carry. Nahida calls it the new Irminsul, and her own existence is now bound to it.

105.content: Known erasures: the Third Descender Saarelainen, erased by the Heavenly Principles long ago (revealed 7.1); Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, removed by Nahida in 3.2; Scaramouche's past, erased by himself in 3.3; and forbidden knowledge, erased by Nahida and the Traveler. Each time, natives' memories and records were rewritten while the consequences remained. Memory of Saarelainen survived only with the Belyi Tsar, who was hiding in the Shadow Realm at the time, and in Celestia's own records, which Rhinedottir says she has read.

106.content: Silver-white trees with glowing blue streaks stand across Teyvat as parts or root-ends of Irminsul: on Dragonspine (the Frostbearing Tree, plus one on a small island further east), in The Chasm, on Tsurumi Island near the "Boatman", and in the Orchard of Pairidaeza on Mt. Damavand. Ley Line disorders warp the land around them. The wiki notes that they stand where Celestial Nails are thought to have struck. The Dragon-Queller, the Sacred Sakura and the Weeping Willow of the Lake have similar streaks but brown bark, and are not counted as Irminsul trees.

107.content: On Dragonspine stands the sprout of an ancient Irminsul tree that Sal Vindagnyr revered. Item text says the kingdom's last princess was born under it. Celestia's Skyfrost Nail shattered and froze the old tree, and the princess failed to save it by grafting a branch. Five hundred years ago, the dragon Durin's blood seeped into the Ley Lines there. It revived the tree with red streaks in place of blue and a "thirst for more power". Fed with Crimson Agates, the tree bears a single fruit, the catalyst Frostbearer.

108.content: "Sarva" is the Aranara's word for Irminsul. They speak of returning to Sarva when someone dies, but also of coming from, returning from and travelling through it. After Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's removal, Araja said Sarva no longer remembers Marana, the Aranara name for the Withering.

109.content:
Irminsul Modifications (also: Irminsul purge, Irminsul erasure, erased from Irminsul, purged from Irminsul, history rewriting): Irminsul, the silver-white tree that stores Teyvat's information, can be edited. A god-level power can purge a person or fact from it, and memories, books and records across Teyvat then change to match, while the events themselves still happened and their results remain. Three purges are known: the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (by Nahida, 3.2), Scaramouche (by himself, 3.3) and the Third Descender Saarelainen (by the Heavenly Principles, revealed 7.1). In 6.6 Dottore hijacked Irminsul and Nahida had it burned down.

The edits touch people's memories and physical records (books, letters, item and character texts), but not the underlying events, so rainforests Rukkhadevata grew, or crimes Scaramouche committed, remain and are simply remembered with other causes or actors. People native to Teyvat, including gods, do not notice they were altered. Descenders and other outlanders have no records in Irminsul and so keep their memories.

Established: Irminsul collects the world's information through the Ley Lines and acts as the record of Teyvat, so removing something there removes it from the shared understanding of the world. Rewriting changes whatever counts as Teyvat's information: what people remember and what books and letters say. Natives, including the Archons, do not notice. Paimon is affected too, while the Traveler is not. Removal appears to happen only once: information that natives of Teyvat preserve or retrieve afterward does not disappear again, though retrieval is presumably hard without the help of someone who never lost it, such as the Traveler.

Weapon and artifact descriptions are not changed by these edits, which is why some texts still name Rukkhadevata or Scaramouche. Ordinary item descriptions and books are changed. Natives can sometimes shield their memory: according to Rhinedottir, the Belyi Tsar fled into the Shadow Realm and so was the only one to retain some memories of Saarelainen. Information can also be stored in a form that still resonates with what Irminsul holds, which let Scaramouche's past be recovered later. Irminsul can also refuse an entity: Andersdotter's Durin was at first rejected by Irminsul and, once he physically entered Teyvat, scripted toward the fate of Rhinedottir's earlier Durin, until steps taken by the Hexenzirkel and the Traveler let Irminsul accept him as a different entity.

Accounts: Rukkhadevata: In Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies Nahida removes the Greater Lord, whose existence had been contaminated by forbidden knowledge and kept polluting Irminsul after her death. Afterward Nahida believes she was always the original Dendro Archon who lost her memories fighting the darkness in the cataclysm. The other Archons and the people of Sumeru remember only Lesser Lord Kusanali (in the voice-overs of Venti, Zhongli and Ei, "Buer"), and the Akademiya's reasons for confining Nahida change to disappointment in her weakness.

Scaramouche: In The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call (Interlude Chapter, Inversion of Genesis) Scaramouche erased his own past from Irminsul. He could not erase himself entirely and continued to exist as the Wanderer, but he lost the memory of his earlier identities. Records elsewhere were rewritten: Ei and Yae Miko lose their Kunikuzushi voice-overs and Tartaglia his Balladeer voice-over, Fatui NPC lines are changed, and Inazuma's account of Tatarasuna and the fall of the Raiden Gokaden is retold without him.

Saarelainen: In the 7.1 Archon Quest (Black Feathers Scattered at Parting) Rhinedottir, who says she read Celestia's records of the incident, tells Anastasya that Anastasya was first erased by the Heavenly Principles as punishment after the Belyi Tsar incited her and Saarelainen to open the gate to the Abyss. Saarelainen then ascended to Celestia to bargain for her return, offering his own life. The Heavenly Principles agreed on condition that everything about him be forgotten: they erased him and all related memories from Anastasya's mind and used Irminsul to erase every trace of the Third Descender from the world.

Other changes: Sumeru NPC dialogue that named the Greater Lord now names Lesser Lord Kusanali or the Dendro Archon; Aranara and Aranyaka voice-lines that named Queen Aranyani now say "Dendro Archon" or "Lord of Verdure"; the descriptions of Kalpalata Lotus, Rukkhashava Mushrooms, Harra Fruit and The Boon of the Elder Tree, and the book The Folio of Foliage, are rewritten. Nahida's Character Details and Character Stories 1 and 3, and Zhongli's Character Story 5, are altered. Weapons and artifacts such as Viridescent Venerer's Determination and Fruit of Fulfillment keep references to her. The Traveler's voice-over about Rukkhadevata disappears after A Toast to Victory, since Paimon no longer remembers her.

Tatarasuna: the swordsmith Niwa Hisahide is remembered as dying with another smith in the furnace to purify Tatarasuna, rather than being murdered by Dottore, who in the original history took his heart to power a device. Aqaba's report names a mechanic from Fontaine (Dottore as Escher) instead of a puppet. The fall of the Futsu, Hyakume and Senju schools is blamed on a murder spree by the head of the Hyakume clan, and Kaedehara Yoshinori's letter is altered accordingly. The Traveler checks many of these changes in A Dance of Destruction. Nahida's own Balladeer voice-over is not removed.

Saarelainen was not completely erased: the Frostmoon Scions kept some of his tales as hymns, though these are unreliable because they were written under the modified record (they claim Anastasya was the Belyi Tsar's daughter, which is shown to be false). Objects tied to him, such as a Gnosis, a Stellar Linchpin and a prism that stores memories independently of Irminsul, remain, and the Belyi Tsar retained some memories of him because he had fled into the Shadow Realm.

Open questions: Canon does not explain how the purge power works in detail, why self-purging fails, how much else the Heavenly Principles have edited without anyone noticing, or why the Traveler's sibling has records in Irminsul while the Traveler has none.

Because anything that happened before the Traveler's arrival could have been edited with nobody (except other Descenders) remembering, canon invites caution about claiming a record is original. Do not invent additional purges or say who else has been erased.

Connections: Irminsul, the Heavenly Principles, the Ley Lines, the Akasha System and Aaru, Descenders, Fate, the Shades, and the destruction of Irminsul in 6.6 are the neighbouring entries. Characters most affected are Nahida, the Wanderer, Dottore, the Belyi Tsar and the Traveler.

110.content:
Nahida removed the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from Irminsul in Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies to cleanse the pollution of forbidden knowledge. Gods, mortals and Nahida herself now remember only Lesser Lord Kusanali, who believes she lost her memories in the cataclysm. The forests she grew and Sumeru's traditions remain.

Traces: the throne inscription RUKDVTA in the Orchard of Pairidaeza, a Geoshroom's distorted memory, and the artifact set Viridescent Venerer's Determination and weapon Fruit of Fulfillment. After the purge the Rukkhashava Mushrooms archive text says people take "Rukkhadevata" to be the name of a giant tree that once stood in Sumeru.

111.content:
Scaramouche tried to remove himself from Irminsul in the Interlude Chapter and succeeded in erasing nearly all records of his past, but he could not remove himself and lives on as the Wanderer, no longer recalling his earlier identities. Before this, Nahida had prepared a memory block that would remind him of his past regardless of changes to Irminsul, and gave it to him after the Traveler recognised his new identity as Wanderer.

Effects included Tatarasuna and Raiden Gokaden histories rewritten (see main entry), and Fatui NPC dialogue about him altered to mention Tartaglia or Signora. Weapons and artifacts keep references to him (Surpassing Cup, Husk of Opulent Dreams, Kagura's Verity, Kagotsurube Isshin). The Shakkei Pavilion domain description lost its reference in 3.3 for everyone.

112.content:
According to Rhinedottir in the 7.1 Archon Quest, Saarelainen ascended to Celestia and traded his own life to have Anastasya restored; the Heavenly Principles' condition was that everything about him be forgotten, and they used Irminsul to erase every trace of him. Memories of him were wiped and records altered, but traces remain.

Survivors: hymns of the Frostmoon Scions (unreliable), his Gnosis, a Stellar Linchpin, and a memory-storing prism. The Belyi Tsar kept some memories of him by fleeing into the Shadow Realm.

113.content:
After the Doctor's Nod-Krai half was destroyed, part of his Omega Build stored in Northland Bank infiltrated Irminsul and overrode Nahida's authority for a time. It produced red mist that drove people mad, unusual Ley Line blossoms, and a giant Irminsul tree in Sumeru City that Nahida described as a sign of unchecked greed.

With the Seven Pillars of King Deshret helping them take control of Aaru, Nahida's allies merged Aaru with the Akasha System and used it to overload Irminsul. Nahida diverted its stored data to Aaru and used the Pyro Gnosis, which Mavuika had handed over to her through the Traveler, inside Irminsul. The Heavenly Principles had reserved enough of its power to isolate Sumeru if Irminsul were lost.

114.content:
Nahida, within Irminsul, invoked her right as its keeper and faced the Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius, who asked whether she was certain she wished to use her authority to destroy Irminsul, the tree through which the Heavenly Principles maintain fate. She said humanity's survival came before Irminsul. They allowed it, and the Pyro Gnosis burned the tree; the Doctor died, dragged into the flames by the Segments he had deleted. Aaru took over Irminsul's role and Nicole's reliance on Irminsul was transplanted there.

The burning lasted seven days and nights, and afterward the Pyro Gnosis vanished without a trace, which Mavuika accepted. See the dedicated entry for the destruction of Irminsul for fuller detail.

115.comment: Irminsul Modifications: Additions and Records of Outlanders
115.content: Additions are rarer. Nahida arranged for Dottore's recorded memory of killing Niwa Hisahide to be preserved and findable when Scaramouche searched for Descender records, and admitted to the Wanderer in As Though Morning Dew that she planned this deliberately. Beings not from Teyvat, such as Descenders, do not normally appear in Irminsul, but the Traveler's sibling has records there, which characters link to Khaenri'ah.

116.content:
Kuuvahki (also: blessing of the Moon Goddess, polar kuuvahki): Kuuvahki is a moon-power found only in Nod-Krai: a pure, primordial form of elemental energy belonging to the Light Realm, comparable to phlogiston. It flows through Nod-Krai's air, land, plants and animals. The Frostmoon Scions call it "the blessing of the Moon Goddess"; Snezhnograd researchers named it "kuuvahki." It powers Moon Wheels, Lunar Reactions and Nod-Krai machines.

Ineffa also compares it to the Primordial Sea. The Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest (6.3) reveals that kuuvahki is the body of Columbina, the Moon Goddess, poured out over Nod-Krai about 6,000 years ago.

Established: - It is linked to the Three Moons and is strongest when the Frost Moon comes closest to Teyvat. Many creatures grow stronger or weaker with its tides.
- Kuuvahki strong enough can counter the Abyss and even turn Abyssal power into something usable.

- It has two opposite polarities, red and blue: like colours repel, opposite colours attract. Where it is very strong, "the rules by which objects move and operate" change.
- It drives Aino's "Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Energy Cannon" over Nasha Town, which fires when the Wild Hunt threat gets too high, and the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle, a source of new technology and weapons.
- Radiant Beasts are ordinary animals warped over ages by kuuvahki into stronger, element-attuned creatures. Some plants store kuuvahki.

- The Frostmoon Scions hold it sacred. Lauma says their statues of rare Lunasoul Stone brim with kuuvahki, which drew the Fatui's interest, and the Fatui's efforts to use kuuvahki have worsened tensions between the two groups.
- Abyssal power can also win. Flins observes that when kuuvahki and Abyssal energy meet, the stronger one suppresses the weaker; a strong enough Abyssal source consumes and changes the kuuvahki.
- Under the influence of the Pillar of Embla in northern Nod-Krai, kuuvahki exists in a "pure energetic form" that has no polarity and spreads as waves (kuuvahki currents). These waves can purify Abyssal contamination and melt Lunar Conflux Barriers, the barriers that form when pure kuuvahki condenses.
- Bodily sensitivity varies. Overexposure can cause nosebleeds, dizziness, headaches, nausea or full-body itching. People with chronic, severe symptoms have congenital kuuvahki sensitivity, which worsens if untreated. Snezhnayan doctors created a medicine for it generations ago, but some Frostmoon Scions refuse Fatui-linked help. In Where the Moon Rises (6.0), Lauma treats a flare-up suffered by Kaarina, whose family distrusts the Snezhnayan doctors in Nasha Town. Powdered lakkaberries ease symptoms for a while. The silver blood of Frostmoon Scions with strong Hyperborean ancestry, such as Lauma, can counter them.

Accounts: Before the truth came out, locals explained kuuvahki either as the power of the moons that Nibelung raised from Nod-Krai, or as the remains of two shattered moons whose fragments fell on Nod-Krai.

Ineffa says geological surveys and meteorite studies support the legend that the moon once rose from Nod-Krai. Lauma tells the shattered-moon version: the fragments rained down "like stardust", which is why kuuvahki is so plentiful there. Frostmoon legend also credits the immense kuuvahki of the Eternal Moon, the largest moon, with creating the ocean tides. Hyperborean survivors on Hiisi Island are said to have received hereditary gifts from the Moon Goddess Canon, including kuuvahki sensitivity, silver blood, animal speech and white antlers.

Origin: In The First Sliver of Moonlight (6.3), Columbina, fleeing Dottore through the "moon's reflection", travels back to the War of Funerary Flame and meets the Moon Sisters Aria, Canon and Sonnet. They tell her kuuvahki did not exist in their time: it is simply her power. Made Trilune Goddess by their authorities, she turns her body into moonlight poured over Nod-Krai alone, and that moonlight becomes kuuvahki. It answers her because it is her.

The reflection could hold divinity and authority but not a body, which is why she gave up her body. She left her soul in the reflection, anchored to the present by a Luonnotar, and hid her Trilune Authority within the Frost Moon. Because the Heavenly Principles destroyed the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and banished the Frost Moon in the same era, later generations believed kuuvahki came from the shattered moons. To close the loop, Columbina willed herself to be reborn about 500 years before the present, with no memory except a lullaby.

Moon wheels and reactions: Moon Wheels, the Vision-like gems of Ineffa, Lauma, Flins and others, channel kuuvahki instead of ordinary elemental energy. Lunar Reactions also harness kuuvahki.

The Lunar Reactions are Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom and Lunar-Crystallize. Zibai of Liyue is the only known Moon Wheel user from outside Nod-Krai; Istaroth gave her hers.

Ineffa's Moon Wheel character story records an ancient researcher's notes describing the Moon Wheel as a ritual item from Nephilheim: a "plaything" the "traitors" (the Moon Goddesses) gave their human followers so the goddesses could communicate with them. Like the wisdom of the researcher's Sovereign, it relies on "a purer form of power" rather than elemental energy, which the notes call tainted by the usurper (the Heavenly Principles). Later canon says the Heavenly Principles and the Three Moon Sisters made the Moon Wheels.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): kuuvahki is Nod-Krai's main exploration mechanic. Kuuvahki plants, red or blue kuuhenki and similar sources give a red or blue "empowered state" for lifting, throwing and smashing objects, disabling Fatui machines and riding Moonlanes.

Other sources are struck Atapetra Conches, some bots and Strong Kuuvahki Environments (such as Thunderclap Reef), which keep the player empowered. The player carries one object at a time and can also disable Fatui Oprichniki, Landcruisers and Recon Bots and use Unipolar Fields. Unipolar objects respond to one colour, bipolar ones to both. Near kuuvahki plants the player can briefly turn into a kuuhenki to move quickly along the ground. In co-op, a guest cannot use the empowered state or kuuvahki currents. In combat, Lunar Reactions need a Moon Wheel holder or Columbina in the party, whose Moonsign Benediction passive enables them, and unlike ordinary reactions they can CRIT. Radiant Beasts can trap the party in a draining Radiant Cocoon.

Open questions: - How kuuvahki relates to ordinary elemental energy, and how Zibai's Moon Wheel works outside Nod-Krai, are not explained.

- In The First Sliver of Moonlight, Varka mentions Albedo's theory that elemental energy can dilute the Light Realm's power, but its consequences for kuuvahki are not spelled out.
- Canon has not stated how kuuvahki changed after Columbina's three parts were reunited and the Frost Moon was brought within the False Sky at the end of Descending Moon.

Connections: Related topics: Nod-Krai; the Three Moons and Columbina (Kuutar); the Light Realm, phlogiston and the Primordial Sea; Moon Wheels and Lunar Reactions; the Frostmoon Scions and the Fatui; Archaeolune Energy on the Frost Moon; the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau; Radiant Beasts; the Abyss and the Wild Hunt; the War of Funerary Flame.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): in Nod-Krai kuuvahki is part of the landscape. Plants glow or lean toward passers-by, animals are livelier or more sluggish with its tides, and red or blue glows suit polarity effects.

Ordinary Nod-Krai people still believe the shattered-moon or "moon rose from Nod-Krai" explanations. Only those close to the Song of the Welkin Moon events, such as the Traveler and Columbina's companions, know kuuvahki is Columbina's body, so keep that knowledge limited. Frostmoon Scions speak of it reverently as the Moon Goddess's blessing; Fatui researchers and Nasha Town engineers treat it as an energy resource. A local might casually mention a neighbour's kuuvahki sensitivity or nosebleeds. Do not give kuuvahki powers outside Nod-Krai without a canon reason.

117.content: Kuuvahki sensitivity is how strongly a person's body reacts to kuuvahki. Overexposure brings nosebleeds, dizziness, headaches, nausea or full-body itching. Congenital kuuvahki sensitivity is a chronic, worsening form diagnosed in people with severe symptoms. Treatments are a Snezhnayan medicine developed generations ago (some Frostmoon Scions refuse it out of distrust of the Fatui), powdered lakkaberries for short-term relief, and the silver blood of Frostmoon Scions with strong Hyperborean lineage, such as Lauma. Verna's protective suit and Czcibor's unexplained recovery after vanishing in Barrowmoss Barrens are known cases.

118.content: In northern Nod-Krai (Voidsea Outlook, Wavechaser Plain, Ashveil Peak), under the influence of the Pillar of Embla, kuuvahki exists in a pure energetic form without polarity and spreads as waves. Glimmerfruit, Mandragoras, Slothsheep and Spireblooms give off these currents, which suffuse Mandragoras, Slothsheep and Spirit Blooms, light Oath Lanterns, melt Lunar Conflux Barriers and purify Abyssal contamination. Mandragoras are plant-like organisms that live in symbiosis with pure kuuvahki.

119.content:
Ley Line Disorder (also: Ley Line Disorders, Ley Line Disturbance): Ley Line Disorder is the in-game term for the odd conditions inside Domains and some Spiral Abyss chambers. Depending on the place, the surroundings may hurt or hinder fighters (falling icicles, lightning, a creeping cold, drained energy) or boost them (stronger reactions, higher damage). It sits on the border between game rule and setting: Domains are said to stand on Ley Lines, but canon never explains each effect as a story event.

Treat it mainly as a gameplay label with an in-world flavour: Domains are built on the Ley Lines, and energy surging through the Petrified Tree at a Domain's heart is how the Ley Lines entry accounts for such effects. The same word is also used for a few Trounce Domains that replay old battles as "Memories".

Established: - The wiki defines Ley Line Disorders as effects inside the Spiral Abyss and certain Domains that help or hinder characters, separate from enemy auras and elemental nodes. It has existed since 1.0.
- Domains are tied to the Ley Lines: item and loading text say Domains stand on Ley Lines around Petrified Trees (see the Ley Lines entry).

- Hazards and debuffs seen in Domains include Sheer Cold (a temperature bar that drains HP), periodic lightning bolts that drain Energy, falling icicles, longer Frozen duration, unstable High-Energy Crystal Cores dropped by defeated foes, a spreading Plasma Field, a pursuing Chaos Cluster, enemy Attendants that bolster a leader, and alternating Energy Tides.
- Four elemental debuffs exist: Smoldering Flames (Pyro damage over time), Slowing Water (longer skill cooldowns), Engulfing Storm (draining Energy), and Condensed Ice (higher Stamina use). Each lasts while the matching element stays on the character and can be cleansed by applying a self-aura of an element that dispels it.
- Beneficial Disorders include raised elemental damage, boosted reactions (Overloaded, Electro-Charged, Swirl, Superconduct), HP-threshold bonuses, CRIT damage, Plunging Attack, melee and ranged buffs, Shield and Elemental Mastery buffs, and shockwaves that trigger on certain actions.

- Trounce Domains that carry a Ley Line Disorder include Beneath the Dragon-Queller, Narukami Island: Tenshukaku, End of the Oneiric Euthymia, Joururi Workshop, The Realm of Beginnings, Shadow of Another World and Scattered Ruins. Several are "Memories" challenges whose in-game text invites the player to relive an earlier battle, for example the sealed dragon Azhdaha in Beneath the Dragon-Queller and the duel with the Knave (Arlecchino) in Scattered Ruins.
- Damage from Disorders such as icicles, lightning and blasts scales with the Domain's level and the target's resistances. Specific values vary by Domain and are mechanics, not lore.

Accounts: - Game text: the Ley Lines entry records loading-screen lines saying some characters are "recognised" by disturbed Ley Lines and boosted in Disorder Domains, and that those touching disturbed Ley Lines may be carried to hidden Domains where foes from their memories appear. That is a rule-of-play description, not a witnessed event.
- Story quests: separate Ley Line disturbances (Abyss Order tampering in 3.5, corruption in Sumeru in 6.6) are narrated as real events in the Ley Lines entry. None of them names a "Ley Line Disorder" in the Domain sense.

- Characters such as Dainsleif, Nahida, Nicole and Thoth treat the Ley Lines as a real network. In Caribert (3.5) Dainsleif says the Abyss had interfered with the Ley Lines in Avidya Forest and that he repaired it. No one in canon says Domain Disorders are a deliberate act.

Open questions: - Whether the hazards in Domains are natural properties of the Ley Lines beneath them, a product of their builders, or only a gameplay abstraction.
- Whether "Memories" Domains are the Ley Lines replaying recorded events; their descriptions suggest it, but canon does not state a mechanism.

Connections: Ley Lines, Irminsul and its Petrified Trees, Domains, the Spiral Abyss, elemental reactions and auras.

Ley Line Blossoms and Outcrops are the open-world counterpart. Disorder effects draw on the elements and reactions, so they connect to the element and reaction entries.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): in Domains and Abyss chambers, Disorders are the environmental rule set for the challenge. A Domain can show one or several, and values differ by Domain and difficulty. Elemental debuffs apply to each party member independently (Smoldering Flames affects only the active character), pulse on a fixed interval, and are shortened by artifacts and elemental resonance when the Domain applies them. Some self-applied auras can cleanse them.

Examples of tuning in the wiki: Cryo icicles and Electro lightning bolts deal damage scaled by Domain level, and the Energy Blast and Powerful Blast types depend on reactions.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): characters can describe a Domain's strange cold, lightning or surging energy as the Ley Lines acting up beneath it. Most travellers would treat it as a known hazard of Domains, not a mystery. Do not have a character explain its cause as settled fact; canon does not.

Keep it separate from story-level Ley Line trouble such as the 6.6 Sumeru crisis. The words overlap but canon never joins them.

120.content:
Ley Line (also: Ley Lines, leyline, leylines, Earth Veins): The Ley Lines are a hidden network that links all of Teyvat. Elemental energy flows through them, and they carry the memories of everything that happens in the world, from the surface to the deepest depths. They were tied to Irminsul, the world tree, which stored what they gathered. Disturbed Ley Lines can make people see memories that are not their own.

Ley Lines existed in the age of the dragons, but the Heavenly Principles refashioned them, along with Irminsul, into a defence for the world against the Abyss and an anchor for fate. Natlan is the great exception: its own Ley Lines were destroyed in an ancient war, and the Night Kingdom serves in their place.

Since the end of the Sumeru crisis in 6.6, Irminsul has been burned away, and Aaru now stores the information carried by the Ley Lines.

Established: - Elemental energy flows through the Ley Lines, and loading-screen lore says they "remember all things" that happen in the world.
- Tighnari compares them to the roots of Irminsul. They reach up to the surface from a vast cavern deep underground, and they keep absorbing the world's memories and funnelling them into the tree.
- Where the flow of energy is blocked, deposits form at the surface and Ley Line Blossoms bloom. All Domains are said to be built on Ley Lines, around silver-white Petrified Trees that are parts of the Irminsul root system.

- Original Resin item text says the roots of all the Irminsul trees and blossoms intertwine at the deepest, most hidden place in the earth, and that the pattern they make defines the Ley Lines. Condensed Resin text says these trees are connected to Ley Lines that have become blocked over time, and that resin energy can purify the blockage.
- Disturbances carry memories. In the Interlude act Caribert (3.5), the Abyss Order tampered with the Ley Lines near Avidya Forest, and the Traveler fell unconscious and saw their sibling's memories from centuries before. Dainsleif later observed that Abyss Order activity is usually followed by Ley Line trouble.
- The Ley Lines are linked to erosion. The Raiden Shogun says that as long as they flow, the relentless erosion of time will never stop (Farewell to the Past, 2.5).

- Souls and the dead. In Nod-Krai (To the Lighthouse, 6.0), Flins describes ghosts as the echoes of living souls whose thoughts and memories failed to enter the Ley Lines at the moment of death and so linger on the surface. In time they fade and return to the Ley Lines. Ei likewise calls ghosts "disembodied memories held in the Ley Lines."
- Not everyone is recorded. The Traveler is not recorded in the Ley Lines, and in 7.0 Ronova says that a Descender's soul cannot be brought into them.
- Damage and healing. In Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX (6.6), Cyno explains that overloading and the Withering both harm the Ley Lines' vitality and can do irreversible damage, but that the Ley Lines heal well once blockages or pollution are dealt with. His teacher Cyrus says Ley Line Blossoms bloom from openings in the Ley Lines and signal some anomaly; dissecting anomalous blossoms let scholars judge the state of Irminsul.

Origins: Before the Heavenly Principles arrived, the Ley Lines and Irminsul already existed. According to Apep (6.6), the Ley Lines then carried an abundant, primitive form of elemental energy: the power of the Light Realm. The Heavenly Principles usurped and refashioned Irminsul, made it serve humanity and used it to anchor the fate of the world. The Light Realm's power was diluted into the elemental energy of the human world.

The Lord of the Night (5.3) says the Heavenly Principles modified the Ley Lines to help counter the Abyss, which is why their stability mattered above all. Kukulkan, the ancient Natlan ruler, once hoped to learn how "the one seated upon heaven's throne" had turned the Ley Lines into "a girdle that defends the planet" (A Finale Emberforged, 5.5). According to the Lord of the Night, the ancient dragons once tried to strengthen the Ley Lines with the Source Mechanism, a device under Natlan, but failed because they could not navigate the Ley Lines' intricate structure; that structure has since completely changed.

Accounts: - Mavuika (5.3): the forces of the Abyss always seek to corrode Teyvat; the Ley Lines were created by the Heavenly Principles, and only their protection lets Teyvat nurture life.
- Apep (6.6) and Kukulkan (5.5): the Heavenly Principles took an existing network and converted it, rather than making it from nothing.

- Caribert (4.7): Teyvat's Ley Line system is deeply entrenched in the planet, so new Ley Lines can neither replace nor extend the existing ones.
- Layla (3.6) wonders, without evidence, whether the Ley Lines follow fixed courses like the orbits of celestial bodies and are reflections of the stars upon the earth.

Natlan and the night kingdom: Natlan lacks stable Ley Lines of the ordinary kind. Mavuika (5.1) says its Ley Lines took the worst damage in the ancient war between the Descender and the dragons, which let the Abyss in. Guided by Ronova, the angel Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, rebuilt a similar network from the fragments: the Night Kingdom, which functions as Natlan's Ley Lines.

Because of the rules needed for the Ode of Resurrection, Natlan's network could not be reconnected to the other nations' Ley Lines, so memories made in Natlan and elsewhere do not mix. Capitano at first sought to "reconstruct" the Ley Lines through the Source Mechanism (5.1), which would have cost the Lord of the Night her existence and wiped the memories in the old network. In 5.3 the Ley Lines were instead restored after the war against the Abyss: Capitano died in Mavuika's place and merged with the Lord of the Night to change the rules, letting the Khaenri'ahn souls he carried enter. The Night Kingdom has since been open to the souls of outlanders who die in Natlan.

Sumeru crisis 6 6: In Song of the Welkin Moon Acts IX and X (6.6), Dottore's corruption of Irminsul spread a red mist of corrupted Ley Lines over central Sumeru. Apep sensed the disorder from afar, and strange, never-before-seen Ley Line Blossoms appeared. Dottore had entered Irminsul through death; Nahida says her only possible safeguard would have been to block every soul's free access to the Ley Lines. Pantalone placed Dottore's last backup into the Ley Lines. To stop him, Nahida and her allies moved the world's information out of Irminsul and redirected it to Aaru. Nahida then burned Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis, with the permission of the Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius. The burning took seven days and nights. The reconfigured Aaru now collects and stores the Ley Lines' information.

Open questions: - Whether the Ley Lines and Irminsul's roots are literally the same structure, or two linked systems.
- Why the Traveler and Descenders are not recorded.

- What changes now that Aaru, a system designed outside the Heavenly Principles' plan, holds the Ley Lines' records instead of Irminsul. Canon has not shown this as of 7.1.
- Where and how the sibling intends to lay down the Ley Lines of "New Khaenri'ah".

Connections: Irminsul (the memory store), the Heavenly Principles (who refashioned the network), the Abyss (which it protects against), Domains and Ley Line Blossoms (surface outlets) and Ley Line Disorders (unstable energy in Domains).

Erosion and fate both flow through this network. Natlan's Night Kingdom is a stand-in network, and Aaru is the repository since 6.6.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Ley Line Outcrops are open-world challenges. Defeating the enemies reveals a Ley Line Blossom (a Blossom of Revelation for character EXP materials, or of Wealth for Mora), claimed with Original Resin. Domains and their Petrified Trees and Ley Line Disorder effects are tied to the Ley Lines in the same way.

Loading screens describe a "recognition" by the Ley Lines that boosts some characters in Ley Line Disturbance domains, and say that disturbed Ley Lines can carry those who touch them to hidden Domains where foes from their memories appear.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Ley Lines as an unseen, underground current. Most people only know them through Domains, blossoms, scholars' talk or strange memories and ghosts. A disturbance can plausibly cause dizziness, disorientation, odd elemental behaviour or flashes of another person's memory.

Experts such as Spantamad scholars, Sumeru forest rangers, Natlan shamans like Citlali, Dainsleif or the Lord of the Night can sense or reason about Ley Lines. Ordinary people cannot read them at will. Nobody can simply create new Ley Lines from nothing: even the Lord of the Night only reassembled intact fragments, and the Loom of Fate is a unique Khaenri'ahn device.

121.content:
The Loom of Fate is a Khaenri'ahn device made by Caribert and the Abyss Order that can weave Ley Lines. In its incomplete form it could only create and implant memories. According to Caribert (Bedtime Story, 4.7), once complete it gains the power to weave real Ley Lines and loses its lesser power over memories. He also said new Ley Lines can neither replace nor extend Teyvat's existing ones.

In A Space and Time for You (5.7), the Iniquitous Baptist Haden claimed that the Traveler's sibling had used the Loom to re-weave Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines; he later admitted he was bluffing about Khaenri'ah's revival being complete, since the Order still needed memories of Khaenri'ah. The sibling explained that the Abyss Order's attack on Natlan was a feint to reach the Lord of the Night. She gave them space to weave new Ley Lines, which were superimposed on Natlan; according to Citlali, she agreed once assured that Natlan would not be affected, and set another condition she did not reveal. The result is the "Atlas of the New World", holding New Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines, which still needs a place to be laid down; the sibling sees this as necessary to face the Heavenly Principles as equals.

122.comment: Ley Line: Ley Line Blossoms and Petrified Trees
122.content:
Ley Line Blossoms grow from deposits where the flow of elemental energy is impeded, at the ends of the Ley Lines. They are said to take root in people's wills: a "Revelation" blossom answers a desire for battle, a "Wealth" blossom a desire for money. Petrified Trees, silver-white extensions of Irminsul, stand at the heart of Domains and channel the Ley Lines; the surge of energy through them causes Ley Line Disorders. Both can be revitalised with resin.

Scholars treat blossoms as diagnostic. In 6.6, Cyrus taught that they bloom from openings in the Ley Lines and signal an anomaly, and anomalous blossoms helped Sumeru judge Irminsul's condition during Dottore's corruption.

123.comment: Ley Line: Ley Lines and the dead
123.content: Several sources tie the dead to the Ley Lines. Flins (Nod-Krai, 6.0) says ghosts are fragments of souls that failed to enter the Ley Lines at death and will slowly fade back into them. Ei calls ghosts memories held in the Ley Lines. In 6.6 Nahida says the only defence against Dottore's entry through death would have been closing the Ley Lines to all souls. In Wraith's Nocturne (7.0), Ronova explains that the angels' renovation of the Korolevskiy Theater's Ley Lines hampers her soul-ferrying and allows only two deaths a day there, and that a Descender's soul cannot be brought into the Ley Lines. Natlan's dead go to the Night Kingdom instead.

124.content:
Light Realm (also: realm of the elements, Vishap Realm): The Light Realm, also called the realm of the elements or the Vishap Realm, is one of Teyvat's three realms. It is the home and origin of pure, primordial elemental beings, above all dragons and elemental lifeforms, and the raw source from which the seven elements were later drawn. It stands directly opposed to the Void Realm (the Abyss) and is not naturally compatible with the Human Realm.

Canon treats it as the elemental energy of the world before it was divided, like white light before it is split into seven colours. Its energy vanquishes the Void Realm's darkness. Modern Elemental Energy is a narrowed, more easily controlled and human-compatible form of it.

Established: - The Light Realm hosts creatures that wield pure, raw elements. Dragons and elemental lifeforms are its best-known inhabitants.
- It is diametrically opposed to the Void Realm and incompatible with the Human Realm unless adjustments are made.

- Its dragons were ruled by the Seven Sovereigns under the Dragon King Nibelung, who were later succeeded in rulership by the Three Moons.
- When the Heavenly Principles arrived, it and its shades defeated the Seven Sovereigns, founded the Human Realm and narrowed and refracted the Light Realm into the seven elements (per the banned book "Before Sun and Moon").
- It then used phlogiston as inspiration to modify the Light Realm's power into modern Elemental Energy, easier for humans to control and better suited to fight the Abyss (Beneath the Secret Source, as relayed by the wiki).
- The Human Realm was at some point interposed between the Light and Void Realms (The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent).
- Realm-crossing adaptations exist: vishaps were modified to accept Orobashi's Bloodbranch Coral, Sangacorallia break the Light Realm's pure elemental energy into something the Human Realm can bear, and Natlan's Holy Soil was similarly rendered tolerable with Grainfruit and the Essence of Sacrifice. The Void Realm, by contrast, is incompatible with both and dangerous to both.

- Descriptions of its nature: the "Notes by a Certain Noble Individual" in the Pale Crown Palace call the light from the genesis of the world "undissipated hope itself", able to "illuminate the entire cosmos", and say the never-refracted light signified "a boundless array of possibilities in its pure whiteness" until man confined it to a narrower band of hues in the name of certainty. The same notes say that whenever we lay an anchor into fate, the Abyss lays an anchor into us at the end of time.
- In An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, Aksinya names Nibelung the master of the Light Realm's power at the very beginning, relays the Belyi Tsar's vision of a world where all love one another "as in the very beginning", and calls that "love" a kind of spiritual overflow that runs dry under sorrow.
- Neuvillette's Vision story says the Heavenly Principles, crippled in the war of vengeance, created the Gnoses to keep subduing "the resentments and loathing of the world". The wiki reads these sources together as meaning that narrowing the Light Realm and anchoring Fate turned the primordial "love" into envy, hatred and selfish desire; that link is the wiki's synthesis, not a single canon statement.
- Apep, a being of the Light Realm, adapted to abyssal forbidden knowledge after consuming the corrupted corpse of King Deshret, but suffered great infirmity for millennia.

Accounts: - The banned book "Before Sun and Moon" presents the Heavenly Principles' refraction as founding the Human Realm. The Pale Crown Palace noble's notes present the same narrowing as a loss: boundless possibility confined in the name of certainty. Both are in-world views; canon does not name one the whole truth.

Event accounts: - During the limited-time 2.4 event Three Realms Gateway Offering, Tsumi, the Snake-Masked Shrine Maiden, describes the three realms' analogous currents (ley lines for the Human Realm, elemental currents for the Light Realm, dark currents for the Void Realm) and says the Light Realm's energy vanquishes the Void Realm's darkness.

- In the same event, Enjou had tricked the vishaps into disrupting the balance of the three realms in Enkanomiya. Afterwards the vishaps, despite their hatred of humanity, lent humans aid against the encroaching Void Realm (Three Realms Gateway Offering: Aftermath; also stated on the Light Realm loading screen).

Open questions: Canon does not say what the Light Realm physically is, where it lies, or how its currents work. The three realms appear to be concurrent facets of the world rather than separate places, with some areas dominated by one realm's power.

Fan theories connect the Light Realm to the Abyss or to the Shadow Realm. They are speculation only. Treat them as unresolved.

Connections: Three realms: cosmology.three-realms. Abyss (Void Realm): cosmology.abyss. Rulers and inhabitants: Seven Sovereigns, Nibelung, dragons, vishaps, elemental lifeforms. Refraction into elements: Heavenly Principles, system.elements, system.phlogiston. Regional forms: kuuvahki and the Three Moons in Nod-Krai (see also Archaeolune Energy on the Frost Moon), phlogiston in Natlan. Enkanomiya: Enjou's trick and the Three Realms Gateway Offering.

How {{char}} behaves: This section is the project's suggested narrative handling, not canon. Most characters will not know the term "Light Realm"; scholars, dragons, vishaps and those close to the Heavenly Principles or Fatui research might. Keep it mysterious, and do not state fan theories as fact.

125.content: The Light Realm (realm of the elements, Vishap Realm) is the primordial source of pure elemental energy and the home of dragons and elemental beings. Opposed to the Void Realm and incompatible with the Human Realm without adaptation. The Heavenly Principles defeated its Seven Sovereigns and narrowed it into the seven elements.

126.content: Teyvat's three realms are the Light Realm, the Void Realm and the Human Realm made by the Heavenly Principles. They appear to coexist as facets of the same world rather than separate places. The Light Realm's energy overcomes the Void Realm's darkness. The Void Realm threatens both others.

127.content:
Moon Envoys (also: Moon Envoy, Lunar Envoy, Lunar Envoys, Envoy of the Lunar Palace, envoys of the moon): Moon Envoys were servants of the Three Moons who lived in the Lunar Palace during the era of the unified civilization. The name is a title, not a species: an angel or someone who was not one could hold it. Known examples are Zibai, Thoth and, by inference, Nabu Malikata. After the war of funerary flame killed the moon goddesses, the office lost its purpose.

The envoys carried out many divine duties. Some laboured across the moons to guide humanity and weave the threads of fate for living things, while others came down to the mortal realm to bless nations with good harvests. They could take animal forms and travelled by lunar chariot.

Players mostly meet the concept through Zibai (6.3), Thoth (6.1) and the Nod-Krai moon story; most of what is known comes from a handful of quests, character stories and item texts, so the picture is partial and several memberships are inferred.

Established: - After the Three Moons accepted the Heavenly Principles' divine plan, the new masters sent subordinates to share the sisters' work, and Moon Envoys were assigned to assist each goddess. In a remembered scene, Sonnet says the work can simply be left to the Moon Envoys.
- Envoys lived in the Lunar Palace above the clouds.
- Souls of the dead once followed the Moon Envoys' trail to the cities on the moons, where they rested.

- The title could be held by any individual, angel or not. Zibai, an angel who guided Lang-Gan, became an envoy when Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, gave her a crest bearing the sigil of the moons; her character story says she never fully accepted it. The crest is her Moon Wheel.
- Duties varied. The furnishing text for the Moon Envoy of Silver Radiance says some envoys toil across the three moons to guide ignorant mortals, others descend to bless a nation with bountiful harvests, and that the title does not name one specific person.
- Envoys could change shape into animal forms and used a lunar chariot to travel, for example between the Lunar Palace and Lang-Gan, according to the wiki's summary of Zibai's quests.
- The Lunar Palace is also called the Moon Capital; boatmen such as Diotima and Euthyphro ferried souls toward it, and Diotima says the souls followed the envoys' trail.

- Thoth, later the Ibis King of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, is described by the Guiding Notes and by Zibai's memories as a former Moon Envoy and her colleague. Zibai recalls a colleague who liked to take ibis form.
- Zibai was killed after trying to save Lang-Gan from the Celestial Nail against the Heavenly Principles' will; Istaroth froze the moment of her death and held her soul in fragments, which the Traveler and Zhongli reunited during Lantern Rite (6.3 event).
- The end of the office: the Eternal and Iridescent Moons were destroyed and the Frost Moon was banished beyond the false sky in the war of funerary flame, killing their goddesses. The wiki states the envoys were then no longer needed and that souls were afterwards deposited into the ley lines instead.

Accounts: - Official wiki synthesis: envoys were a staffing arrangement made after the Heavenly Principles arrived, with each goddess given assistants.
- Zibai's character story: she was handed a moon crest by the shade of Time without explanation, wondered whether it was part of the plan, and began travelling between the morning stars, the moons and her garden, without accepting the crest.
- Thoth, as quoted by Nefer: he boasted that he laboured across three moons to guide mortals and weave fate so that life could sprout anew in cycles. Nefer judged it a liar's pitch, though other sources support that he really was an envoy.
- Boatman hymn (Euthyphro): a boatman prays to the goddess Prusmene to be spared from the coming order of the Primordial One and speaks of ushering souls to the Lunar Palace above the clouds. This is a believer's account, not a statement about envoys.

Open questions: - Whether boatmen and Moon Envoys were one role or two.
- Which moon each named envoy served; only Zibai's link to Sonnet is argued, and from indirect evidence.
- Whether Nabu Malikata and the Mistress of Chenyu Vale were envoys; both are inferences.

- How many envoys there were and what happened to most of them. Only Zibai (restored) and Thoth (freed in 6.6) are known to have survived; Nabu Malikata is dead.
- Why Istaroth chose Zibai, and whether her gift was part of Time's own intentions; Zibai herself asks this in her story.
- Do not resolve these. Treat anyone not named in canon as unknown.
