Connections: Three Moons and their goddesses Aria, Canon and Sonnet; the Heavenly Principles and angels; the unified civilization; the war of funerary flame; the shadowmoon that hid the moons' fate; Istaroth; Zibai, Thoth, Nabu Malikata; the Moon Wheel; Lang-Gan; the afterlife systems of the moons and, later, the ley lines and Irminsul.

Moon Wheels were originally made by the Heavenly Principles and the moon sisters and given to human followers so the goddesses could communicate with them in rituals, per the wiki; Zibai's wheel differs in design because Istaroth gave it to her directly as the symbol of her envoy status. In Nod-Krai the wheels later underlie the Moonsign and Lunar reaction mechanics, which are game systems and not part of the envoy office.

128.comment: Moon Envoys: Zibai as a Moon Envoy
128.content: Zibai was an angel who guided the nation of Lang-Gan and was later made a Moon Envoy when Istaroth gave her a crest of the moons. In the wiki's reading she was assigned to Sonnet of the Iridescent Moon, who left much of her work to her. She travelled between Lang-Gan and the Lunar Palace by lunar chariot. She died defying the Heavenly Principles over the Celestial Nail, and was restored in the Lantern Rite event story (6.3). Her own entry carries the detail.

129.comment: Moon Envoys: Thoth the Moon Envoy
129.content: Thoth, the Ibis King and Lord of Lies, is described as a former Moon Envoy of the Lunar Palace and a colleague of Zibai. He later served King Deshret as a Seven Pillar. His claim of laboring across the three moons to guide mortals comes from Nefer's recollection of him, and she doubted it, but other texts back the envoy role.

130.comment: Moon Envoys: Souls and the moons
130.content: In the unified-civilization era the dead were said to follow the Moon Envoys to cities on the moons and sleep there. Boatmen ferried souls toward the Lunar Palace above the clouds; Diotima of Meropis was one, and Euthyphro of Arcadia wrote the hymn found at the Golden Hall. After the moons fell the wiki says souls went into the ley lines. The hymn suggests this afterlife existed alongside the Irminsul.

131.content:
Moon Marrow (also: Moon Marrows, Eternal Moon Marrow, Iridescent Moon Marrow, Artificial Moon Marrow, Marrow of the Eternal Moon, Marrow of the Iridescent Moon): A Moon Marrow is a divine artifact: an energy core formed from a Moon Goddess's remains after her death. Moonchanters in Nod-Krai long sensed a divine presence in the Eternal one and named it the Marrow. It exists in three forms: the Eternal Moon Marrow (Aria), the Iridescent Moon Marrow (Sonnet, corrupted by the Abyss) and an Artificial Marrow that Fatui Harbinger Dottore made himself. Columbina compares the Marrow to an Archon's Gnosis, and it can only form once a goddess is dead.

Established: - Formed from the remains of a dead Moon Goddess; it holds her power and divine imprint.
- Eternal Moon Marrow: from Aria, a miniature moon ringed with debris. Sealed away by the Frostmoon Scions and able to show past events.
- Iridescent Moon Marrow: from Sonnet, a red crescent wreathed in crimson flame when uncorrupted. Corrupted by the Abyss.
- Artificial Marrow: made by Dottore, a light-blue mechanical sphere with esoteric patterns.

- Columbina, the living Frost Moon goddess, says a Marrow can only form after the goddess is dead, so she does not carry one herself. She compares it to a Gnosis, which was formed from the body of the Third Descender; a god who bears a Gnosis is an Archon.
- A Marrow is a source of primordial Light Realm energy that predates the Heavenly Principles.
- Each Marrow belongs to its own goddess. Columbina says the three moons are not one and the same and that, as the Frost Moon goddess, she cannot wield the others' powers. She also says one body cannot contain the Marrows of two moons.
- A goddess can still restore her own strength by drawing kuuvahki from a Marrow. Columbina does this with the Eternal Marrow, saying moonlight blends and each moon can reflect the others' glow.
- Dottore's Artificial Marrow counted as a genuine article for completing the Trilune.

- The Marrows came into being after the war of funerary flame, once the Three Moons were destroyed or exiled and their goddesses had died.
- Canon's death is confirmed but no Marrow of hers is attested. Her circumstances differed: her moon was banished beyond the false sky rather than shattered, and a new goddess (Columbina) was born to succeed her. Whether a Frost Moon Marrow exists is not stated in canon.

Accounts: Eternal Moon Marrow: it coalesced from Aria's remains and was found and kept as a sacred relic by the Frostmoon Scions. They sealed it in a secret chamber that opens only once a year, on Moon-Prayer Night, when the moon is nearest Teyvat and kuuvahki in Nod-Krai peaks. Its power can reveal past events, especially when a Moon Goddess wields it.

Iridescent Moon Marrow: it came from Sonnet. At the moment of death she was overcome by fear and surrendered to the Abyss to prolong her life, which left her suspended in agony and her Marrow corrupted with Abyssal energy. That corruption shows as the Balemoon Bloodfire, an accursed flame that leaves ghostly images of those it burns. As the Iridescent Moon sank into the Abyss it became the Crimson Moon, venerated by Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty. They hid the Marrow in a domain reachable only for brief periods through a ritual that uses Bloodfire. Later Khaenri'ahn dynasties kept researching the Crimson Moon, and the Universitas Magistrorum had a Moon Marrow laboratory devoted to its powers.

Artificial Marrow: Dottore made it much later in his False Moon Institute in Nod-Krai, using the other two Marrows as a substrate (per the wiki). Arlecchino says his contact with Hyperborean phantoms gave him knowledge of the moons and Hyperborean technology, which he used to fashion it as a replacement for the Frost Moon. Dottore boasts that his artificial moon is not rejected by Teyvat, unlike Columbina, whose Old World identity and lineage kept her from integrating into Teyvat.

History: The Traveler came to Nod-Krai and, wanting to recover memories of their spaceship, sought the Eternal Marrow's ability to glimpse the past through the Frostmoon Scions. Dottore wanted it to gain the Three Moons' power and become a god. The resurrected Sinner Rerir wanted it to reunite with his lover in the moon's reflection. Rerir broke into the Scions' secret chamber alongside the Traveler, disguised as the Traveler's sibling. Before the Traveler could take the Marrow, Vilemina stole it and brought it to Sandrone, who later returned it to the Scions after a fight with Rerir at the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. Lauma then used a secret rite to store the Marrow in the Traveler's body, which took it easily because the Traveler is a Descender, and the Traveler became more sensitive to kuuvahki. Once friends with Columbina, the Traveler let her draw on it from within; even a single ray of its moonlight greatly restored her strength.

Present day: As of the end of the Song of the Welkin Moon finale (6.3), the Eternal Moon Marrow is in Lauma's keeping, in the Frostmoon Scions' secret chamber. The Iridescent Moon Marrow, purified of its corruption, is held by Arlecchino. The Artificial Marrow was destroyed with Dottore's defeat. This section follows the wiki's account; later 6.x or 7.x events that moved the Marrows were not found.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat a Marrow as a sacred relic, not a trinket. Nod-Krai residents and the Scions regard the Eternal one with reverence. Only characters who were present for the Song of the Welkin Moon should know the details of Sonnet's purification, Dottore's artificial Marrow or Columbina's role.

132.content: The remains of Aria, goddess of the Eternal Moon, condensed into a miniature moon ringed with debris. The Frostmoon Scions kept it as a sacred relic in a chamber that opens once a year, on Moon-Prayer Night. It can show past events, especially in a goddess's hands. Lauma stored it in the Traveler for a time, and after Dottore's defeat she restored it to the chamber.

133.content: Sonnet's Marrow, a red crescent in flames when uncorrupted. Abyssal energy twisted it into the Balemoon Bloodfire and the Crimson Moon Dynasty hid it in a domain opened only by a Bloodfire ritual. The Traveler freed and purified it during the 6.1 story, and Arlecchino now holds it.

134.content: Dottore's creation, a light-blue mechanical sphere with esoteric patterns, built in the False Moon Institute. It stood in for Columbina's strength after she banished herself and let him control the Trilune power. It was destroyed when he was defeated.

135.content:
Ode of Resurrection (also: Rite of Resurrection, Rite of Rekindling): The Ode of Resurrection is the ceremony, held at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in Natlan, that revives warriors bearing an Ancient Name who have died fighting the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars. An officiator recites a eulogy, the Pyro Archon walks into the Sacred Flame to find the fallen and their Name in the Night Kingdom, and the crowd sings until the Archon steps out again with the revived. It only works if the warrior's team won. It is the reason Natlan could send its best into endless war.

It is also called the Rite of Resurrection, and Mavuika's character stories call it the Rite of Rekindling. It heals only the fatal wound, not injuries gathered earlier in the battle or existing illness. After the Abyss was defeated in 5.3 the ceremony was discontinued.

Established: - Who qualifies: only Ancient Name bearers. For that reason warriors without a Name were not sent to the Night Warden Wars.
- Condition: at least one member of the fallen warrior's team must return victorious. If an entire team falls, none can be restored.
- Where: at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, through the Sacred Flame, a conduit to the Night Kingdom.

- Those not brought back are stranded in the Night Kingdom, and their Ancient Names are eventually forgotten and lost. Natlan's saying is that the victors burn bright while the losers turn to ash.
- The healing applies only to fatal injuries. It does not mend wounds accumulated during a long battle or pre-existing ailments (Mavuika's character story).
- Warriors who are never lost to the Night Kingdom eventually retire from age or injury, die normally, and their Ancient Name passes to another warrior, so the Names carry Natlan's history across generations.
- Natlanese who die otherwise enter the Night Kingdom, slowly lose their sense of self in the sea of souls, and are in time reborn in Natlan in other forms. The Ode is the exception for bearers who fell in victorious battle.

- The Ode's power does not belong to the Pyro Archon. Quest text states it comes from Ronova, the Ruler of Death, who let the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, borrow it.
- The Night Kingdom typically records only the memories and experiences of Natlanese people, which is why Ancient Names are seen as a Natlanese matter and a bearer's Name is sought there. Its Ley Lines could not take in souls from outside Natlan until Capitano's merger in 5.3; the Traveler's Ancient Name, Tumaini, was a special case forged for them.

Ceremony: An officiator opens with a eulogy addressed to the warriors of Natlan, calling on them to heed the call of life as inheritors of memory and legend and naming Natlan's fire as the nation's lifeblood. The Pyro Archon then steps into the Sacred Flame to seek the dead and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom. Meanwhile the crowd in the stadium bows its head and sings in Swahili.

The song's refrain is that the tale continues on: glory passes through generations, courage lights sky and earth, victory will again herald Natlan's path, and the living will wait and sing until the heroes come back and burn bright once more. The melody and lyrics are an excerpt of the Natlan soundtrack, sung in Swahili. At the end the Archon emerges from the flame with the resurrected person. Mualani describes this as the usual sequence before Kachina's Ode, and later recalls Kachina humming the song during training breaks.

Because the ceremony is a public rite, the crowd is part of it. Natlanese treat it as a victory celebration rather than a funeral; Mavuika's character story says she thought of it, as a child, as akin to a victory feast.

History: Natlan's tradition holds that the Ode was made possible when Xbalanque borrowed power from Ronova. Through the Pilgrimage the strongest Ancient Name bearers were chosen and sent to fight the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars, and the Ode let them fight knowing they could be brought back.

In Mavuika's character story, her father won the Pilgrimage and went to war. After a three-day battle in which three of seven warriors fell, he was revived by the Ode but came out of the flame covered with the wounds of the long fight and unable to stand. That was the first time young Mavuika felt the gaze of death, which she saw as something to respect and fear even with the Ode available. Her father told her that everyone fears death, but some still step forward because they have something to protect.

In the final war: Once the six Heroes of Natlan were gathered during the Abyss's invasion, Mavuika awakened the power of the divine throne to extend the Ode's blessings to every Natlanese warrior, whether or not they bore an Ancient Name; later quest dialogue (Citlali, Ronova) treats this as use of Ronova's borrowed power, for which death was owed as the price. From then on, casualties fell effectively to zero, and the Abyss was repelled from the overworld.

Open questions: - Canon shows the borrowed power but not how Ronova and Xbalanque drew up their terms; do not invent the details of the bargain.
- Canon does not say whether the Ode could be performed again, or what happens to the souls that were never recovered by it.

Connections: Sacred Flame and Night Kingdom (the ceremony's means and destination), Night Warden Wars and Pilgrimage (the system it supports), Ancient Name (who may be revived), Mavuika (the Archon who performs it), Kachina (its failure and the final use).

The Ode also links to Ronova's role as Ruler of Death in Natlan's history, to the Wayob who keep the dead in the Night Kingdom, and to the Archon Quest act Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (5.3).

136.comment: Ode of Resurrection: Ode of Resurrection
136.content:
The Ode of Resurrection is Natlan's rite for reviving Ancient Name bearers who fell fighting the Abyss, provided at least one of their team returned victorious. At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame an officiator speaks a eulogy, the Pyro Archon walks into the flame to find the fallen and their Name in the Night Kingdom, and the crowd sings that the tale continues on. It heals only the fatal wound. Its power was borrowed from Ronova, Ruler of Death, by Xbalanque.

In 5.0 the Ode failed for Kachina because the Abyss was disrupting the Night Kingdom, and Mavuika suspended the Pilgrimage. During the 5.1 invasion she extended the rite to every Natlanese warrior. In 5.3 Kachina led the Stadium in the Ode to strengthen the Traveler and Mavuika in the final battle, and afterwards it was discontinued.

137.comment: Ode of Resurrection: Kachina's Failed Ode
137.content:
Kachina's Ode was led by Mavuika with Ntotila as officiator. Mavuika returned from the Sacred Flame alone, saying neither Kachina nor her Name could be found. Some in the crowd, led by Tepexpan and Tamuin, doubted Kachina's worth; Mavuika declared her a hero. She suspended the Pilgrimage and began investigating. She later said the Abyss's unrest in the Night Kingdom had blocked her.

Mavuika told the Traveler, Paimon, Mualani, Iansan, Chasca and Kinich that without working Odes Natlan would fall to the Abyss, and that suspending the Pilgrimage at least meant no more warriors went to a war they could not return from.

138.comment: Ode of Resurrection: Ronova and the Borrowed Power
138.content: Quest text says the Ode's power comes from Ronova, the Ruler of Death, who let Xbalanque borrow it. In 5.3 Ronova required the Archon's life as the price for the power used in the war. The Lord of the Night held back the blow, and Capitano merged his life force with the Lord of the Night instead.

139.content:
Primordial Human (also: Narayana, Proto-Man, Primordial Humans, Ruler of Elysium, King of Elysium, Svarod, Velikan of Light): The Primordial Human, also called Narayana, is a title: the ruler of Teyvat in "the court of the stars". Nibelung, the dragon king, held it before the Heavenly Principles destroyed him, and the seat has been vacant since. Later efforts tried to create a new bearer: the Hyperboreans' project that produced the Belyi Tsar, the Frostmoon Scions' Sacred Heir Project, and Rhinedottir's Primordial Human Project, which produced Albedo.

In 7.0 the Pale Crown Palace quest line shows Aksinya's attempt to complete the Belyi Tsar's ascension to the title at the cost of the world as it is. The term also appears in a Nicole voice-over, where in another possibility Albedo was the "Primordial Human" who traveled through worlds "recording and creating all".

The term gathers several separate efforts under one name, and canon never defines it in one place. Treat it as a title whose meaning is shown by what people tried to do to obtain it.

Established: - Narayana is another name for the title (Aksinya, 7.0). An artifact text speaks of a "vacant seat in the court of the stars", which the wiki identifies with it.
- Nibelung, called "the One" by Aksinya, is tied to the seat; after his destruction it has sat empty.
- Hyperborea tried to produce a new bearer from the remains of the Cryo Dragon. The result, born about a thousand years after the experiment, was the Belyi Tsar, the first Cryo Archon.

- Because Nibelung was still alive when Hyperborea ran its experiment, notes in the Pale Crown Palace say the seat was still occupied and the experiment could not reach its goal.
- The experiment ran out of control. The Cryo Dragon's unchecked authority turned the land into the Holy Soil of primordial ice, and the Heavenly Principles dropped a nail on it, which sank Hyperborea into the Shadow Realm.
- Aksinya says the Belyi Tsar knew he was the failed product of that project, yet accepted it, and with the Hvergelmir institute set out to become the true Primordial Human. The Eye of Graeae was the "Proto-Man" built to complete this.
- In the world quest An Ark That Used to Be a Soul (7.0) the Traveler stops Aksinya's plan to open the Court of Bliss, in which the Tsar would ascend and a "Courtyard of Carefree Light" would replace the world.

- Aksinya describes the intended outcome as covering Snezhnaya, then the whole world, in the Shadow Realm so that love stays unchanging. The Eye of Graeae says the authority of the Primordial Human is like a poison to humans and fae, who carry mixed desires, and that completing it would mean the world was about to undergo an inexorable revolution.
- Nibelung is the only past bearer canon points to. According to the wiki, Aksinya and the Belyi Tsar describe the Light Realm's overflow from him as hope and love, which the Heavenly Principles later distorted.

Accounts: - **Aksinya (7.0):** the seat of Primordial Human, or Narayana, has been empty since Nibelung's destruction, and the Belyi Tsar was meant to fill it.
- **Artifact text (Disenchantment in Deep Shadow):** the Snow-King, burdened by sin and remorse, assembled the Hvergelmir to seek the stairway to the vacant seat in the court of the stars.
- **Nicole (voice-over, About Albedo):** in another converged possibility, Albedo was the "Primordial Human" who traveled through worlds, "recording and creating all". She adds that once that journey ended, no one could guarantee whether he would choose destruction or salvation. The wiki generalises this into a description of Primordial Humans.

- **The Eye of Graeae (7.0):** it says it persuaded Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis to stop Aksinya and asked to be divided, because it feared both the title's power and the world it would produce.
- **Hyperborea's notes:** the seat was described as occupied while Nibelung lived, so the experiment could never have succeeded in his lifetime.

Open questions: - Whether the office has any holder now. No canon says it does.
- Whether Nibelung's title and Narayana's seat in "the court of the stars" are the same idea as being a Descender.

- What authority the title grants beyond being equal to the One, and why the Heavenly Principles would have treated a new bearer as a threat.
- What the Courtyard of Carefree Light would have done to the world, beyond what Aksinya and the Eye of Graeae say.

Connections: Related entries: Nibelung and the Descenders; the Belyi Tsar, Aksinya, the Hvergelmir institute and the Eye of Graeae; Hyperborea, the Cryo Dragon and the Shadow Realm; the Frostmoon Scions' Sacred Heir Project and Avrelian; Rhinedottir, Albedo and Subject Two.

140.comment: Primordial Human: Nibelung and the vacant seat
140.content:
Aksinya calls Nibelung "the One": a will born alongside Teyvat, master of the Light Realm's power in the beginning and king of the Dragon Lords. She says the place of Primordial Human, or Narayana, has been vacant since his destruction. The wiki, citing the same quest, lists "Primordial Human" among his titles. His rank as Second Descender rests on the war of funerary flame, covered in the Descenders entry.

Per the wiki's summary of the Pale Crown Palace notes, his seat was still held while he lived, which is why the Hyperborean experiment could not give anyone the title.

141.comment: Primordial Human: Hyperborea's project and the Belyi Tsar
141.content:
Hyperborea tried to forge a new Primordial Human from the flesh and blood of the Cryo Dragon. The experiment went out of control and the land became the Holy Soil of primordial ice; the Heavenly Principles dropped a nail on the region, and Hyperborea sank into the Shadow Realm. A thousand years later the Belyi Tsar awoke from the remains. Unaware of what he was, he led the Snowland Fae, later learned his origin and, as Cryo Archon, chose to pursue the goal set for him.

He founded the Hvergelmir institute to help. Aksinya and the Hvergelmir built the Eye of Graeae to complete his transformation. The Tsar fell fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, and Anastasya succeeded him as the Tsaritsa.

142.comment: Primordial Human: The Eye of Graeae as Proto-Man
142.content:
Aksinya describes the Eye of Graeae as the "Proto-Man" created through countless experiments, the key that would let the Belyi Tsar become the Primordial Human; its face was modelled on the Tsar's human form. It is the quest NPC Paimon calls Goggles, found by the Traveler in an abandoned train in Chapter VII (7.0). Before the final fight it asked the Traveler what they would do if their sibling had become a different person; the Traveler answered that they would learn to love them again.

Before the Cataclysm it was divided into three parts and persuaded Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis to stop Aksinya. Once the Traveler recovers its three fragments, Aksinya transfers it into the Tsar's remains, and its consciousness becomes the core of the being fought as the Primordial Human in the Court of Eternal Bliss. After the fight, it and Aksinya fall into the Shadow Realm together.

143.comment: Primordial Human: The Sacred Heir Project and Avrelian
143.content:
The Frostmoon Scions, Hyperborean survivors, ran a Sacred Heir Project instead of the Seed of Life Project: breeding to purify moon-blessed blood until a Maiden bore a being able to wield the Light Realm's energy at will. The prophesied child was called the Ruler or King of Elysium. The wiki lists Avrelian, the first Reed Miller, as the failed outcome: his mother fled the role, and he became a legendary thief and founder of the Treasure Hoarders, executed 500 years ago.

Lovia, the last Archpriestess, tried again with the twins Aila and Alia. Both rebelled, and Aila, as the new Moonchanter, ended the project. The link between this project and the title Primordial Human is the wiki's reading of item texts.

144.comment: Primordial Human: Rhinedottir's Primordial Human Project
144.content:
Rhinedottir's Primordial Human Project aimed to create a human through alchemy. It first produced failures such as Subject Two, who took Albedo's form and was discarded in Durin's stomach, and finally the "perfect" Albedo, whom she classed as Cretaceus. Nicole says that in another converged possibility Albedo was the Primordial Human who traveled through worlds.

Nicole adds that she cannot observe how that version ended, and that the journey now is the player's own.

145.content:
Primordial Sea (also: Primordial Seawater, Water from the Primordial Sea, Primordial Water, primordial ocean): The Primordial Sea is an ancient sea hidden beneath Fontaine. Most life in Teyvat first arose in it, and it once lay on the surface of the world. Its water gives life, and it can also take it away: the people of Fontaine were made from Oceanids using its water, so pure Primordial Seawater dissolved them back into water. This was the root of Fontaine's "original sin" and of the prophecy that a rising flood would dissolve every Fontainian. In the 4.2 Archon Quest, Neuvillette, restored as the Hydro Sovereign, made Fontainians true humans. The flood came, but it no longer dissolved them.

The main known entrance lies beneath the Fortress of Meropide, behind a sluice gate in its Forbidden Zone. Smaller passages and pools exist in other underground places, such as beneath the Tower of Ipsissimus and in an underwater Sinthe production base. People from other nations are not dissolved by it; it only makes them more sensitive to Hydro.

Established: - Pure Primordial Seawater dissolves a Fontainian of Egeria's era or later into water, and their memories merge into the sea. Non-Fontainians are not dissolved.
- Diluted water does not dissolve people but still harms them. Exposed Fontainians show flushed skin, hyperventilation and exhaustion.
- Since Neuvillette's absolution (4.2), Fontainians are no longer dissolved by it.

- Water from the sea is described as having "higher quality and density" than ordinary seawater, and it can be weakened by mixing or dilution.
- In the 4.0 Archon Quest, Neuvillette says the Primordial Sea no longer exists on Teyvat's surface.
- Ordinary people cannot normally enter the sea; Childe reached its depths only after following a voice out of Meropide.
- Sigewinne can diagnose Primordial Seawater exposure from its symptoms (she did so for Freminet, and later testified about Furina).

- The dissolved are not simply erased. Their consciousness seems to keep some individuality: an "Oceanid" took shape in the Fountain of Lucine from Vigneire and Vacher's later victims, whose dissolved remains flowed back there with the water used on them.
- After the prophecy was fulfilled, much less Primordial Water remained on the surface, and what remained seems to be impure. Vacher's old gang still tries to exploit it while the Fontainian authorities pursue them.

History: Before the Archons, the sea's "heart" was the first Hydro Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns. After the Heavenly Principles removed it, the Hydro Archon Egeria became the sea's new heart. Egeria used the sea's water to give her Oceanids human bodies. The Heavenly Principles judged this a sin, and the Fontaine prophecy followed.

Egeria's people became the tribes of Fontaine. In her reign, repentant exiles were sent below the waves to guard her secret, the entrance to the sea. They built the first Fortress of Meropide over it, and later wardens added gauges to monitor the water level. In time most of the prison's inmates forgot what the gate was for. The Remurian god-king Remus received a goblet of water from Egeria at the sea and used it to build Remuria (see the Ichor entry).

Present day, in the 4.x Fontaine Archon Quest:
- 4.0: Marcel, whose real name is Vacher, has been dissolving young women for about twenty years in experiments to bring back his dissolved lover, and has framed others each time. The court learns that water from the sea can dissolve Fontainians.
- 4.1: For about a year Wriothesley had watched the gauges in Meropide's Forbidden Zone climb. Freminet collapses after swimming through diluted Primordial Seawater along Childe's route, and Clorinde rescues him. The sluice gate bursts. Wriothesley and Clorinde hold the water back until Neuvillette arrives, pushes it back and reseals the gate. Childe, meanwhile, wakes in the depths of the sea facing a colossal narwhal-like beast.
- 4.2: The water rises at Poisson after a tremor, and people there dissolve, including Navia's attendants Melus and Silver. Navia nearly dissolves in a flooded ruin; Melus and Silver, their consciousness now formed into Oceanids, shield her from the other victims for the few seconds Neuvillette needs to save her. The narwhal surfaces at the Opera Epiclese to devour Fontainians. Focalors's death on the Oratrice returns the Hydro Authority to Neuvillette. He absolves Fontainians of their sin and turns the sea-derived "blood" in their bodies into real blood. With the Traveler he subdues the beast inside the sea, and Skirk sends it, with the unconscious Tartaglia, back into the Abyss. The energy the beast had consumed returns to the sea, which floods Fontaine. No one dissolves, and the water then recedes.

Accounts: - Hydro Vishaps (glider text, which itself calls them unreliable): the first sea was like blood, and life within it was not separate individuals. Creatures that moved onto land or into the sky grew blood vessels to carry the sea inside them, and the first Hydro Dragon was its beating heart.
- Oceanid tales (same text): when that heart was removed, Celestia's envoy, the leader charged with creating life, came to the sea and made another heart, Egeria. She had a dragon's nobility without its form and a god's majesty without a divine duty, and her compassion led her into the sins that beings of pure water must beware.
- Remurian legend (Dross of Pure Sacred Dewdrop): the dense primordial sea is the purest origin of all things and will one day swallow all life; whatever did not arise from it will be filtered out as floating detritus.

- The Remurian Harmost Boethius (Sublimation of Pure Sacred Dewdrop): life born of the sea is fated to return to it, but humans have endless ways to transcend, and even the sea cannot fully dissolve them.
- Hyperborean prayer preserved in Nod-Krai (Hymns of the Far North): the hymn to Maadteraahka, Mother of Life, praises her as the "mother of the waters" who birthed a heart for "the roaring primordial ocean"; the wiki identifies Maadteraahka as Naberius, Ruler of Life, and the heart as Egeria.

Open questions: - Who, if anyone, now acts as the sea's "heart"? Canon says only that Neuvillette, fully restored, could command it.
- Is the Amrita Pool, Egeria's body in Sumeru, made of the same water? The question is unresolved.

- Is Fontemer, Fontaine's sea and its aberrant creatures, the same thing as the Primordial Sea? The names suggest a link that the English text never states.
- What does the Remurian prophecy mean by "detritus", things not born of the sea that will be filtered out? Boethius posed this question to Remus; the item text records no answer.

Connections: Prophecy of Fontaine (the flood it caused); Egeria, Focalors and Furina (the Hydro Archon's role); Neuvillette and the Hydro Dragon (the sea's original sovereign); Oceanids and the tribes of Fontaine (the people it shaped); the Fortress of Meropide (built to guard its entrance); Remuria (built on water refined from it).

The All-Devouring Narwhal fed on the sea's energy. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo studied it. The Sea of Stars and Nibelung appear in the moon-age lore that the sea predates.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): after 4.2 the sea is no longer a danger to Fontainians, so a modern scene should not show Fontainians dissolving. Primordial Water can still be shown as a rare, illicit substance tied to Vacher's remnant gang. Before 4.2 it is lethal to Fontainians and almost unknown to the public; most people learned of its power only from Marcel's trial.

Ordinary people cannot visit the sea. Its only known gates are sealed: Meropide's sluice gate and the Tower of Ipsissimus, which Ann resealed. Do not have non-Fontainians dissolve, and do not treat the sea as a place where the dissolved can be revived; Vacher never succeeded.

146.comment: Primordial Sea: Primordial Seawater and Sinthe
146.content:
Water from the Primordial Sea dissolves Fontainians whose bodies came from it. Diluted, it does not dissolve them. Vacher (Marcel) found that weakened water made Sinthe, an addictive drink that brings euphoria. He sold it through dealers in Poisson to fund his research. Long use leaves people unable to focus or control their emotions, and withdrawal brings paranoia, anxiety and severe fatigue. Callas banned it in Poisson. Vacher also used the water to dissolve a man after a shooting, leaving Callas to be blamed. Callas kept silent to protect his daughter Navia, and later died in a duel with Clorinde.

Cowell, a conspirator against the House of the Hearth, hid a balloon of the water in Lyney's magic box to dissolve the woman posing as Halsey. She was really Liliane, a thief from Mondstadt, so the water did not affect her. At Furina's trial, a deliberately diluted sample produced the same symptoms in her as in other humans, which supported the charge that she was human.

147.content: Deep in the Fortress of Meropide's Forbidden Zone, a sluice gate seals the largest known passage from the Primordial Sea to the surface. Only the warden and trusted people knew of it. Wriothesley worked out that its gauges measured Primordial Water, and that the prison existed to stop the sea from engulfing Fontaine. When the gate burst in 4.1, Neuvillette pushed the water back and resealed it.

148.comment: Primordial Sea: Original sin of Fontaine
148.content: Egeria's Oceanids longed to live as humans, so she poured Primordial Seawater into their "blood vessels" as a substitute for blood, giving them human bodies. Creating human life was beyond her authority, and the Heavenly Principles branded her and her people with an original sin. The decree followed: the waters would rise, every Fontainian would dissolve, and only the Archon would remain, weeping on her throne. Neuvillette's absolution in 4.2 replaced that substitute blood with real blood.

149.content: Legend says that when Remus came to the Primordial Sea, Egeria gave him a goblet of water. He refined it into golden Ichor, which he hoped would replace the sea itself. He mixed the insoluble Ichor with pure water, believing it could hold memories and wisdom, so that his subjects could leave their bodies and live forever in golem bodies that the sea could not dissolve. Item text says ordinary life cannot bear the separation of soul and body. The torn souls turned the Ichor black, and the attempt helped destroy Remuria.

150.comment: Primordial Sea: Narzissenkreuz in the Primordial Sea
150.content: In the world quest series "Ann of the Narzissenkreuz", the Ordo's Master, Narzissenkreuz (Rene de Petrichor), waited in the Primordial Sea to give birth to a new world of his own design. He had foreseen an apocalypse and meant to escape it this way. The Traveler, Ann, Seymour and Caterpillar forged the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz and defeated his follower Jakob Ingold at the Tower of Ipsissimus. When the tower collapsed into the sea, it broke a seal leading to the Primordial Sea. Inside, the Traveler and Ann defeated the Master, who lost control of the sea, accepted that his world-formula was wrong and left with them. Ann then resealed the waters so they would not flood Fontaine.

151.content:
Realm of Consciousness (also: realms of consciousness, consciousness realm, space of consciousness): A realm of consciousness is an abstract space built on a person's mind. It lies outside the world of Teyvat, yet what happens inside it can change the outside world. Its entrance takes a shape tied to its owner, and its interior is coloured by the owner's memories. The Traveler visits three: Makoto's (Inazuma), Lesser Lord Kusanali's and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's (Sumeru). Canon says very little about how they work.

A realm can outlast its owner's body: the owner keeps a sense of self after death, but cannot perceive the outside world or the passage of time, and the realm cannot be preserved forever. Yae Miko calls the whole idea "very abstract" and surrounded by chaos.

Established: - It is a domain built on one person's consciousness, separate from Teyvat.
- Events inside can affect the real world.
- The entrance takes a form related to its owner: a torii gate for Makoto, a newly sprouted tree branch for Kusanali, a Knowledge Capsule for Rukkhadevata.
- Its interior is shaped by the owner's memories.

- A realm can exist after the owner's body dies, and the owner can keep their sense of self; but the owner cannot sense the outside world or time passing, and the realm cannot be kept indefinitely.
- Someone else may seal or open the entrance: Ei sealed Makoto's, and the Shogun later unlocked it; Kusanali opened Rukkhadevata's with the Electro Gnosis.
- A realm can be closed from within by a living owner: Kusanali shut hers to keep Il Dottore from reaching her mind through the Akasha.

- Makoto deliberately used hers as a place to show Ei her vision of Eternity, with a seed of the Sacred Sakura waiting to be given to Ei once she understood. Ei did not know this.
- The Dream Sakura the Traveler took from Makoto's realm persists afterwards in a quasi-physical form that can be seen but not touched.

Accounts: - Yae Miko (Radiant Sakura) gives the only general description: a very abstract concept, surrounded by chaos.
- Kusanali treated Rukkhadevata's realm as a preserved image of Irminsul as it was five hundred years earlier; this is her belief at the time, stated in the quest.

- The wiki's overview of how a realm is accessed and what it contains is a summary of these three cases rather than a statement by any one character.

Open questions: Canon does not explain the mechanics of realms of consciousness, who can make one, or what happens to a realm once its owner's consciousness is gone. It does not say whether Focalors' and Furina's spaces in The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur are realms of consciousness; they merely resemble them in how time behaves. Do not state either as fact.

Whether realms of consciousness differ from Ei's Plane of Euthymia only in how they are made is also unstated; the wiki merely notes that they are different.

Connections: Related to Ei's Plane of Euthymia (a mind-world she placed in the blade Musou Isshin), to the Sacred Sakura and Inazuma's cataclysm cleansing, to Irminsul and forbidden knowledge in Sumeru, and to the Akasha system that Dottore used against Kusanali. Adepti personal abodes (sub-space creation) are a separate technique.

Makoto's realm links to the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual and the Dream Sakura; Rukkhadevata's links to the erasure of Eleazar and the healing of Irminsul.

How {{char}} behaves: Use as a narrative device, clearly dreamlike and personal: the entrance looks like something the owner would make, the inside echoes their memories, and time outside need not match time inside. Keep explanations vague, as in canon. (This is the archive's suggested use, not a canon rule.)

152.comment: Realm of Consciousness: Makoto's realm of consciousness
152.content:
After Makoto died in the cataclysm, Ei preserved her realm of consciousness; its entrance is a torii gate. Ei sealed it, but the Shogun unlocked it when their wills opposed each other so they could fight at full strength, Ei having no body of her own. Makoto had prepared the realm so that Ei could eventually grasp her vision of Eternity, after which Makoto's remaining consciousness in Musou Isshin would give Ei the seed of the Sacred Sakura. Ei planted it in the realm, where it took root in Inazuma's past and absorbed the filth of the cataclysm. Makoto's strength and consciousness were then spent and the realm vanished. The Dream Sakura it yielded remains, visible but intangible.

Quests: Farewell to the Past and Radiant Sakura (Transient Dreams, Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, version 2.5).

153.comment: Realm of Consciousness: Kusanali's realm of consciousness
153.content: While Lesser Lord Kusanali was imprisoned in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, she closed off her consciousness so Il Dottore could not read her mind through the Akasha. As part of the plan to free her, the Traveler entered her realm of consciousness; the entrance appeared as a newly sprouted tree branch (quest Jnagarbha Day, Archon Quest Chapter III Act V).

154.comment: Realm of Consciousness: Rukkhadevata's realm of consciousness
154.content: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's realm was left behind when she died in the cataclysm. Its entrance was a Knowledge Capsule, opened when Kusanali used the Electro Gnosis, which also shielded her somewhat from the forbidden knowledge that had corrupted Rukkhadevata's remaining consciousness. Because Rukkhadevata had been contaminated and was bound to Irminsul, Irminsul could not heal while her memory lasted. Kusanali erased Rukkhadevata's existence and remaining consciousness; the realm, which Kusanali took to be Irminsul as of five hundred years earlier, disappeared. Irminsul was healed and things caused by its contamination, such as Eleazar, vanished (quest Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies, version 3.2).

155.content:
Sacred Flame (also: K'ahk', Natlan's Sacred Flame): The Sacred Flame is the fire that never stops burning above the arena of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Natlan's central landmark. It is the conduit to the Night Kingdom, the realm of the dead and of the Wayob, and the means of speaking with the Wayob. Mavuika calls it the foundation of Natlan's resistance against the Abyss. Battles between Natlanese warriors produce Contending Fire, which fuels it. The Pyro Archon steps into it during the Ode of Resurrection to bring fallen heroes back.

Its main outlet, the column of fire above the arena, can be seen from far outside the Stadium. A second outlet is the large fire pit in the Speaker's Chamber, where the tribal chiefs meet under the Archon's eye. Mavuika put her life into the flame at the end of the Cataclysm 500 years ago and returned from it in the present day.

Established: - The flame is a continuous fire at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and a conduit to the Night Kingdom and the Wayob.
- Contending Fire, produced only in combat between people of Natlan, keeps it burning. Cival explains that Natlan is safe from the Abyss only while the flame burns eternal.
- The Pyro Archon performs the Ode of Resurrection through it.

- When a new Pyro Archon ascends the divine throne, their "inner flame" awakens, and the Sacred Flame grants them broad knowledge and memory of Natlan. Mavuika says this is how she knows the history of Natlan's rules (Echoes of Life, 5.0). In a scene from Mavuika's past shown in A Fuel Named "Fate" (5.1), her friend Wanjiru repeats the idea and worries that inheriting the flame's knowledge can change a person's personality.
- Objects carried into battle by Natlanese heroes slowly become imbued with Contending Fire. Burning them releases that fire as fuel, though crudely and all at once.
- Mavuika says that no one but her could sustain the flame, and that it "must never go out": it frightens the Abyss and is "the pillar of Natlan's stability".

- Smaller flames split from the Sacred Flame are carried to braziers for the Turnfire Night ritual of the Scions of the Canopy. A tutorial describes them as holding a blessed power that dispels darkness and scatters the Abyss's power.
- Ochkanatlan-era bulletins call the flame K'ahk' and give the tyrant Och-Kan the title "Guardian of the Sacred Flame" (Yajaw K'ahk').

Ode: In the Ode of Resurrection, an officiator recites a eulogy, the Pyro Archon walks into the flame to seek the fallen warrior and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom, and the crowd bows and sings until the Archon walks back out with the revived warrior.

Only Ancient Name bearers who fell in the Night Warden Wars qualify, and only if their unit "achieved victory", meaning at least one member came back victorious. The rite reverses only the fatal wound; injuries built up earlier in the battle and existing illnesses remain. Mavuika's character stories call the return a "Rite of Rekindling", treated like a victory feast. As a child she watched her father come back through the flame alive but so badly wounded he could not stand.

The power behind the Ode traces back to Ronova, the Shade of Death, who let the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, borrow her power on condition that he keep the bargain secret. See the Ode of Resurrection's own entry for the full rite.

History: Mavuika was Pyro Archon during the Cataclysm. After the war against the Abyss she placed her remaining life inside the Sacred Flame so that she could reawaken 500 years later and oversee her plan to drive the Abyss out of Natlan. She woke some years before the Traveler arrived and won the Pilgrimage to become Archon again.

In the Natlan Archon Quest (5.0), the Ode for Kachina failed: Mavuika came out of the flame alone, unable to find her or her Ancient Name, because the Abyss had invaded the Night Kingdom and blocked communication between the flame and the Wayob. Mavuika suspended the Pilgrimage, even though fewer battles meant less Contending Fire. Since Contending Fire alone was "far from sufficient", she then transferred her own power into the flame to keep it alight, giving up, among other things, the ability to turn her hair to flame. To reach Kachina and the Traveler in the Night Kingdom, she burned the keepsakes of past heroes stored in the Speaker's Chamber, using their Contending Fire to open the boundary between the worlds.

During the Abyss's full invasion (Archon Quest Act III, 5.1), the manifestation of the Abyssal being Gosoythoth put the flame out. Mavuika used the might of the Pyro Gnosis to reignite it and hold the incursion back, and refugees fell back to the Stadium because the flame repels the Abyss. At the flame the Traveler witnessed a scene from the distant past in which Ronova and Xbalanque struck their bargain. Once the six heroes were gathered, Mavuika borrowed the Lord of the Night's power to extend the Ode's protection to every Natlanese warrior, with or without an Ancient Name.

Accounts: - Mavuika (Echoes of Life): the first Pyro Archon, a mortal with no special power, used the divine throne to borrow power from the heavens (Ronova) and set "the rules" of Natlan, a framework through which ordinary people can become Archon. The flame's gift of memory is part of that framework.
- A material description: the first human to ascend "arose from the throne to enter the Sacred Flame" while the world waited for a successor; Och-Kan then seized power and founded Ochkanatlan.
- A Thousand Blazing Suns (weapon text): Xbalanque reached for "the primal flame" in the ineffable city. Under the name "Haborym", the divine name Pyro Archons bear, "life had become the sacred flame unquenchable" and the rules became an ever-blazing divine throne. The text also credits an artisan and the Scarlet-Eyed Youth, the second Pyro Archon, with ensuring that the Sacred Flame would endure. Its closing line is "So long as the flame does not die, there shall still be 'hope.'"
- Mavuika's own imagery (Character Story 5): in meditation she pictured her plan as a long road toward a high tower with the Sacred Flame burning at its summit.

Open questions: - How the flame came into being. The poetic weapon text ties it to Xbalanque and the name Haborym, but no literal account exists.
- What sustains it now that the Abyss war is over, and whether Contending Fire is still collected for it.
- How the knowledge passed to new Archons is stored, and whether it really changes the inheritor (Wanjiru's worry in Mavuika's memories, not a confirmed fact).
- Whether the flame outlet in the Night Kingdom is a true exit as well as an entrance.

Connections: The Night Kingdom, which stands in for Ley Lines in Natlan, lies on the other side of the flame. The flame is not itself a Ley Line.

- Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame: the tournament that produced Contending Fire, chose heroes for the Night Warden Wars and chose the Archon.
- Ode of Resurrection and Ancient Names: the rite performed through the flame, and the names it restores.
- The Pyro Archon (Mavuika as of 7.1) is responsible for protecting and fuelling the flame. The Pyro Gnosis rekindled it in 5.1.
- Ronova and the Lord of the Night are the powers behind Natlan's rules of resurrection. Capitano's later sacrifice, which merged his life force with the Lord of the Night, rewrote the rules of the Ley Lines; canon frames that through the Night Kingdom rather than the flame.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): during the 5.1 Archon Quest defence, Pyro DMG is increased within the light of the Sacred Flame. Lit braziers carrying split-off Sacred Flame grant protection that lets the player light other braziers during Turnfire Night content. In the final 5.3 boss fight, "the Sacred Flame will ignite your will to persevere", fully restoring Mavuika and the Traveler instead of letting them fall. The Pyro Traveler's sixth constellation is named "The Sacred Flame Imperishable".

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the flame as Natlan's civic and spiritual heart. Crowds face it during the Ode, chiefs negotiate beside its fire pit, and warriors speak of feeding it through honourable combat. Outlanders could not fight in the old Pilgrimage because their battles produce no Contending Fire.
Only the Pyro Archon walks into the flame in canon, apart from the Traveler at Mavuika's side. Do not let ordinary characters step through it to the Night Kingdom. Set after 5.3, the war is won and the Ode is no longer performed; a scene showing a resurrection rite as current should be set in the past.

156.content: Contending Fire is the energy produced when people of Natlan fight one another, and the fuel of the Sacred Flame. The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame existed largely to generate it, which is why outlanders were barred: their participation would hinder its production. Items carried in battle by heroes absorb some of it over time. Mavuika burned such keepsakes in 5.0 to force open the way into the Night Kingdom, and their power was spent in an instant.

157.comment: Sacred Flame: Mavuika's sleep in the Sacred Flame
157.content: After the Cataclysm, Natlan was ruined and its tribes broken. The Archon and the tribal heroes agreed on a 500-year plan to rebuild the tribes until each Wayob could choose a new hero. Because Natlan had no gods able to extend a human life, Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame, dying before her time so that she could wake again when the plan matured. She revealed this in Past and Future (5.0).

158.comment: Sacred Flame: Guardian of the Sacred Flame (K'ahk')
158.content: In Ochkanatlan-era Ancient Bulletins found in the Old Core of Chu'ulel, the Sacred Flame is called K'ahk', and Och-Kan, the Holy Sovereign of the Eternal Empire, is styled Yajaw K'ahk', "Guardian of the Sacred Flame". One bulletin uses that title to seal off a "cursed land". The title shows how Ochkanatlan's ruler claimed the flame's authority after Xbalanque entered it.

159.content:
Sea of Stars (also: the universe beyond Teyvat): The Sea of Stars is the universe beyond Teyvat: thousands of planets, stars and civilisations lying past the false sky and the Dark Sea. Canon describes it as a dangerous "black forest". The Heavenly Principles, Saarelainen and the Traveler all came from it, and unknown threats and cosmic calamities such as Surtalogi, the All-Devouring Narwhal and the Abyss reside there. Teyvat is one planet among them.

Most Teyvatians cannot see it at all, because the false sky hides the cosmos from the planet. It is not an accessible location in the game and appears in animated shorts, weapon and book text and character stories.

Established: - Teyvat's planet sits on the edge of a spiral arm of an unnamed galaxy in the sea of stars.
- Three of the four Descenders came from beyond Teyvat (the wiki counts the Heavenly Principles as the first Descender, Saarelainen as the third and the Traveler as the fourth). The Abyss is counted among the cosmic calamities that reside there.
- Unknown cosmic calamities live there too.

- In the Old World, Nibelung made the Eternal, Frost and Iridescent Moons from the planet's crust to govern it while he travelled the sea of stars. During his absence the Heavenly Principles descended on Teyvat, took control and raised the false sky, which kept the universe hidden.
- During the Funerary Year Nibelung returned, brought the Abyss to the world and fought the Heavenly Principles, who won and still rule Teyvat. The Eternal and Iridescent Moons were shattered, and the Frost Moon was thrown out beyond the false sky into the sea of stars. By the Archon Quest "True Moon" it had been revitalised and drawn back inside the false sky.
- After the Cataclysm, Surtalogi brought Skirk to Teyvat from her homeworld, and gave the weakened All-Devouring Narwhal to Skofnungr in the Primordial Sea.

Wiki-listed arrivals from beyond Teyvat, roughly in order: the Stellar Blackbody (brought to the Frost Moon and fused with Ungien before the Funerary Year); the Heavenly Principles; Anacharsis (before the Funerary Year); the Abyss (Funerary Year, brought by Nibelung); Saarelainen (after the war of funerary flame); the Traveler and their sibling, who passed over Teyvat's sky in the distant past and later made a forced landing at Starsand Shoal before the Cataclysm; the Narwhal and Skirk (after the Cataclysm, via Surtalogi). The Traveler's sibling emerged during the Cataclysm from outside the ship, and the Traveler speculates they left long before.

Worlds: Known worlds beyond Teyvat. Teyvat itself. The Traveler's unnamed planet, which the Traveler and their sibling once ruled before a "star-devouring darkness" destroyed it; they then began travelling between worlds in a spaceship. Skirk's unnamed planet, home to humans who can adapt to any environment or energy source; a merchant ship from a neighbouring world judged them a potential threat and an army attacked, and Skirk escaped with Surtalogi's help. Throgg, an empire of the immortal Ysna'qurel, child of Ghel'vur, which was destroyed by the "Dark Destroyer" after sending a warning into space; it is unclear whether the world or only its civilisation died. The warning was received by the Moongazer Nin-Kiggia.

Octavia's travels, from cosmetic-set and collection text, name many numbered planets: for example the 66th, which resembles Liyue and lives under a purple-black haze called "Misfortune"; the 67th, whose extinct dragons survive as fossils; the 93rd, the Academy Planet, which can reshape its surface into one academic collective; the 311th, where flowers express the planet's will; the 503rd, a perpetually hot ocean world where she introduced the lemon; the 666th, ravaged by an "Evil Star"; the 777th, a magic-saturated world whose scholars imbue meteorite dust with spells to counter a threat from deep space; and the 1896th, a bronze-age world of city-states that united against Abyssal enemies. These are told through outfits and shop events, so treat the details as light flavour rather than central lore.

Accounts: The Heavenly Principles themselves are presented, in the Byakuyakoku Collection, as the first Descender. Alice describes the Abyss as the hatred carried by fates that will not come to pass, which is an account of its nature rather than a home world. The wiki does not state where it came from before Nibelung brought it. Weapon text for the Sword of Descension supplies the "star-devouring darkness" that ended the Traveler's world.

Aloy, a collaboration character, is said to come from a post-apocalyptic world through a portal; the wiki notes this is not treated as canon. Alice shows familiarity with real-world Earth ideas (idol culture, the Rubicon), but because she is also able to break the fourth wall it is unclear whether this means an Earth exists in the sea of stars.

Open questions: Canon does not say what lies beyond the Dark Sea in detail, where the Heavenly Principles or the Abyss originated, what the star-devouring darkness is, how many Descenders exist overall, or how the numbered worlds Octavia visited relate to the main plot. Do not invent a map of the cosmos.

Connections: Linked to the Heavenly Principles and the false sky (the barrier), the Descenders, the Abyss, the Three Moons, the Traveler and their sibling, Skirk and Surtalogi, Nibelung, Octavia and the Moongazers.

Roleplay note (this project's guidance): characters inside Teyvat generally have no idea the sea of stars exists, since the false sky hid it. Only Descenders, the Traveler, beings tied to the Moongazers or Surtalogi's circle, and a few others would speak of it, and even they know it only in fragments.

160.comment: Sea of Stars: Sea of Stars
160.content: The universe beyond Teyvat's false sky. Teyvat sits on the edge of a spiral arm of an unnamed galaxy. It is described as a dangerous "black forest" full of planets, civilisations and unknown calamities. The Heavenly Principles, Saarelainen and the Traveler came from it, and the Abyss is counted among its calamities. Teyvatians cannot normally perceive it.

161.content: Skirk comes from an unnamed planet whose humans could adapt to any environment or energy source. A merchant ship from a neighbouring world saw them as a potential threat, and an army was sent. She escaped with Surtalogi's help and was brought to Teyvat after the Cataclysm. What became of the planet is unknown.

162.content: A world once ruled by the immortal Ysna'qurel, child of Ghel'vur, and their empire. It was destroyed by the "Dark Destroyer" and broadcast a warning into the cosmos, which the Moongazer Nin-Kiggia received. It is unclear whether the whole world or only its civilisation was lost.

163.content:
Seven Sovereigns (also: Dragon Sovereigns, Dragon Sovereign, elemental dragon sovereigns, Seven Dragon Sovereigns, seven terrifying sovereigns, dragon-lords of the old world): The Seven Sovereigns are the seven elemental dragons, one per element, who ruled the old world of Teyvat under the Dragon King Nibelung. The Heavenly Principles defeated them and stole part of their power, the elemental Authorities, which became the basis of the Archons' Authorities. Living Sovereigns therefore lack full "dragonhood" until an Archon's throne is destroyed and the Authority returned, which has happened only for Hydro. Current Sovereigns: Dvalin (Anemo, Mondstadt), Azhdaha (Geo, sealed in Liyue), Apep (Dendro, Sumeru) and Neuvillette (Hydro, Fontaine, reborn in human form). Xiuhcoatl (Pyro) and the Cryo Dragon are dead with no successor; no Electro Sovereign is known.

The Chinese title means "Dragon King", which English sometimes renders "Dragon Lord". They are not Natlan's Thirteen Sovereign Lords, who served Xiuhcoatl.

Established: - They were the dragon-lords of the old world. Each held one Authority and a domain attuned to its element.
- In Calamitous Tread (4.1), Neuvillette says no living Sovereign, himself included, holds full dragonhood, and that the power the "First Usurper" seized is the basis of the Archons' Authorities.
- A Sovereign is born only from an elementally pure lineage. Bathysmal Vishaps, which diverged into Electro and Cryo forms, are impure. A Sovereign may instead be reborn in human form, like Neuvillette.

- A new generation replaces the fading originals: Dvalin, born from a convergence of elemental energy high in the heavens, succeeded a dead Anemo dragon; Neuvillette succeeded the Hydro Dragon.
- Lost dragonhood also means lost memory: Neuvillette did not remember his link to the Primordial Sea until his Authority came back in 4.2.

Sovereigns: - Anemo: Dvalin (Mondstadt), alive and Venti's ally again since the Prologue; his unnamed predecessor is dead.
- Geo: Azhdaha (Liyue), once Morax's friend, eroded and sealed beneath the Dragon-Queller; resealed in Zhongli's Story Quest (1.5).
- Electro: unknown.
- Dendro: Apep (Sumeru), purged of forbidden knowledge in Homecoming (3.6); now merely observes gods and humans.
- Hydro: Neuvillette (Fontaine), the only Sovereign with his full Authority back (4.2).
- Pyro: Xiuhcoatl (Natlan), killed about 2,000 years ago by Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon.
- Cryo: the Cryo Dragon (Snezhnaya), long dead; its remains lie beneath a Celestial Nail by the ruins of Hyperborea.

Details:
- Dvalin was drawn to Barbatos by the Holy Lyre der Himmel, became the Dragon of the East of the Four Winds, and was poisoned by Durin's blood 500 years ago.
- Azhdaha fought for Morax in the Archon War, but erosion and mining turned him against humans and he destroyed Tianqiu Valley. Morax needed three adepti to seal him, and Azhdaha allowed it.
- Apep ruled a forested land and its primordial Dendro lifeforms. She let King Deshret build a kingdom in her domain on condition that all the knowledge he gathered would belong to her after his death; that knowledge was forbidden and corrupted her.
- The Hydro Dragon was the heart of the Primordial Sea, from which all life on the planet first came, and so could be called the original "God of Life". It withered after the defeat; the Heavenly Principles made Egeria as a replacement heart, and no new Hydro Dragon could be born while she hibernated.
- Xiuhcoatl presided over light, heat and wisdom and commanded Phlogiston; at his birth he created his "brother" Kukulkan.

History: The world belonged to the dragons from the dawn of time. The Byakuyakoku Collection (2.4) records that when the "eternal throne of the heavens" came, the Primordial One fought "the seven terrifying sovereigns, dragon-lords of the old world" with four shades of itself; forty years later the Sovereigns were vanquished and the seven nations submitted. Later, the seas took in those who rebelled and would not kneel. Surviving Sovereigns fell into deep slumber; Xiuhcoatl lay frozen in liquid Phlogiston in a "false death".

In the Funerary Year Nibelung returned bearing the power of the Abyss. The Sovereigns could not resist his call and joined his "great war of vengeance". They lost again and the world nearly collapsed, but the Heavenly Principles was so damaged it could no longer suppress the old order alone. It and "one who came after" created the seven Gnoses, which set off the Archon War for seven new divine thrones (Neuvillette's Vision story).

Current state: As of 7.1: Neuvillette holds the full Hydro Authority, returned when Focalors arranged her own execution and destroyed the Hydro throne (4.2). Acknowledging human will, he set aside parts of his own power so that Visions can still be granted (Vision character story). Dvalin, Apep and Neuvillette are at peace with the present world, and Dvalin still helps Venti (in Varka's Story Quest, 6.4, he carried the Traveler toward Nod-Krai). Azhdaha remains sealed. The other Authorities remain tied to the Archons' thrones; in A Finale Emberforged (5.5) Kukulkan arranged for the Saurian Little One, a descendant of Xiuhcoatl, to inherit the Pyro Authority, but Little One refused, Kukulkan passed away, and the Authority stayed with Mavuika.

Accounts: - Apep calls the Heavenly Principles the "usurper from beyond the heavens"; her hatred remains, though she sees no purpose in destroying humans, and Nibelung's scales and will "still shine bright" in her heart.
- Neuvillette recalls the usurper appointing its own "God of Life" and creating Egeria to suppress the planet's original vital force. He believes Nibelung was wrong: all kinds of life together are needed against the Abyss.
- The Byakuyakoku chronicle, written by worshippers of the Primordial One, presents the conquest as the rightful creation of a world for humanity.

Open questions: - Who was (or is) the Electro Sovereign? Who was the original Anemo Sovereign, and is Azhdaha an original or a successor?
- What happens to an Authority if an Archon dies without destroying the throne? Canon shows only the Hydro case.

Connections: - The Seven (Archons): their divine thrones rest on the stolen Authorities. Venti and Zhongli each befriended a dragon (Dvalin, Azhdaha).
- Gnosis: created by the Heavenly Principles with "one who came after" (Saarelainen) after Nibelung's war.
- Four Shades: the Heavenly Principles' four shades, including Ronova, fought the Sovereigns.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): Sovereigns are ancient, proud and alien, and may see Archons as the usurper's appointees. Ordinary people do not know the term or the history of the Authorities. Do not invent an Electro Sovereign or a Cryo successor; keep Azhdaha sealed and Dvalin, Apep and Neuvillette non-hostile as of 7.1.

164.comment: Seven Sovereigns: Tsumi on the Seven Sovereigns
164.content: In the quest that opened the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event (2.5), the Enkanomiyan Tsumi called the Seven Sovereigns of the Light Realm "the seven foremost elemental dragons at the pinnacle of the raw and primitive elemental forces"; like all vishaps, they are creatures of the Light Realm.

165.content: An elemental Authority is a Sovereign's dominion over its element. The Heavenly Principles seized part of each Sovereign's power, and it became the basis of the Archons' Authorities and divine thrones. A living Sovereign cannot reach full dragonhood, or its memories of the old world, until the Archon's throne is destroyed and the Authority returned. This has happened once: Focalors arranged her own execution in 4.2, destroying the Hydro throne and returning the Hydro Authority to Neuvillette.

166.content: The original Hydro Sovereign was the heart of the Primordial Sea and ruled the vishaps of the waters. It perished after the war against the Heavenly Principles. Fontaine's children's rhyme says that when the Hydro Dragon weeps, it rains; Neuvillette, its human-form successor, is puzzled by the idea that the dragon could cry.

167.content: The Cryo Sovereign died in the war with the heavens. Hyperborea later used its flesh and blood to try to forge a Primordial Human. Its unchecked authority turned Snezhnaya into the Holy Soil of primordial ice, and Hyperborea was struck by a Celestial Nail. The corpse and the Nail stayed above ground, and a thousand years later the Belyi Tsar emerged from the remains. In 7.1 a dying Ronova fused Eitr with that Nail.

168.comment: Seven Sovereigns: Xiuhcoatl and the Pyro seat
168.content: Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Sovereign of ancient Natlan, was frozen in liquid Phlogiston in a "false death" after the first defeat. Woken by Nibelung, he was later corrupted by the Abyss. In lucid moments he built the Tzitzimimeh and Huitzilopochtli, a device that would turn Natlan into pure Phlogiston, then sealed himself beneath the Great Volcano. Xbalanque slew him about 2,000 years ago and became the first Pyro Archon. In A Finale Emberforged (5.5), Little One, a Saurian descendant of Xiuhcoatl, refused to inherit the Pyro Authority, which stayed with Mavuika.

169.content:
Shadow Realm (also: world of shadow, World of Shadows, Shadow Realms): The Shadow Realm is a strange pocket-space that floats like a bubble over the frozen land of Snezhnaya and swallows those who stumble in. Inside there is no wind, no light and no usable elemental energy, so Vision-holders cannot channel their powers and must fight with firearms that carry elemental power in their ammunition. The ruins of Hyperborea, the Golden City, lie inside it. Fatui soldiers and travellers have been lost to it; the Druzhna contain and clear breaches, with Royal Energy Commission officials posted outside them.

Snezhnayans also speak of it as the "world of shadow." Its origin is uncertain: the Belyi Tsar suspected that it was made with technology from beyond Teyvat and that it shields the world from the Abyss.

The Traveler first enters it by accident in the Chapter VII Archon Quest, when the train bound for Snezhnograd is dragged in. The Belyi Tsar's connection is central: his expeditions into its ruins taught him what he was, and the passage he opened let the Abyss begin to seep into the world.

Established: - No wind, no light, no elemental energy; as Alyosha puts it, even time does not exist there and everything seems to come to a standstill. Most people pulled in are never seen again, and the few who return are never quite the same.
- Those who fail to escape are devoured: in Alyosha's words their shadows are devoured and they are no longer among the living; Druzhna briefings describe them warped into monsters lost to reason.
- Breaches open suddenly in Snezhnaya, like bubbles rising to the water's surface; the Eye of Graeae says the Realm intersects the world of the Light Realm only rarely, in just that way.
- The ruins of Hyperborea lie inside it.

- Vision-holders cannot call on their power there. Firearms, whose ammunition holds and channels elemental power from outside, were found by someone after much research to be the most effective means of attack, according to the Eye of Graeae.
- The Eye of Graeae, a device found in an abandoned station, calls the Shadow Realm the darkest space in the "shell," where even the most high is loath to cast its gaze. It helps the Traveler by marking exits and issuing equipment.
- Breaches can appear anywhere, not only in expected places: one swallowed the Traveler's train on the railway itself, which Alyosha calls almost unheard of. Falling off an edge into the untethered depths may mean never leaving again.
- A breach can "sink back down"; the Traveler escapes through a core that collapses behind them.

- The Belyi Tsar's notes describe the interior as the reverse of what he expected: no foul Abyssal blood, only fine white dust in the air as if all existence had been ground by winds, and beyond the storm a castle that proved to be Hyperborea.
- He writes that the Realm lies at the intersection of the physical, temporal and spiritual planes; that matter has no stable form inside it ("no true form"); and that it teems with possibilities yet unobserved.
- He compares it to a film of oil lying over the known world, separating Teyvat from the Abyss beyond. By his reckoning the science behind it is not of this world and exceeds even Celestia's.
- Hyperborea's sunken ruins have stayed uncorrupted by the Abyss for millennia, which he takes as a sign the two repel one another.

Accounts: - The Belyi Tsar (Pale Crown Palace notes): the Realm was probably made by Anacharsis, "The Saint," directly or as a by-product of the memories he left in the eternal void in defiance of his fate; its science is not Teyvat's; it works as a film protecting the world from the Abyss. He presents these as deductions.
- Alyosha, a Snezhnayan traveller: knows it as a deadly place from stories and a few sightings, and says this is his first time inside. He recalls a story of a "World of Shadows" with a way out.
- The Eye of Graeae, an ancient device: names it the darkest space in the shell and says its own creation was likely connected to it. Its words on this are partly broken off.

- Aksinya (An Ark That Used to Be a Soul): a Hvergelmir scholar who intends to blanket Snezhnaya and then the world in the Shadow Realm to create a "Courtyard of Carefree Light." She says the Hvergelmir recovered records in it showing that Hyperborea sank into the Shadow Realm and only the fae remained above, and credits Izmaylov with helping her escape from it.
- The Primordial Human in that quest says that in the Shadow Realm the binding of fate's threads is dispelled and infinite possibilities remain. This is a mystical statement from an unreliable speaker, not a verdict.
- Popular interpretations link the Realm to the Light Realm or place Nod-Krai's Mysterious Space inside it; canon does not state either (see uncertainties).

History: - Hyperborea, the Golden City of the unified civilization, was destroyed by a Celestial Nail roughly 6,000 years ago and plunged into the Shadow Realm; survivors fled toward Nod-Krai and became the Frostmoon Scions.
- Much later the Belyi Tsar, driven by dark dreams and a search for his origin, opened a "passage" into the Shadow Realm; his notes say the innocent were ensnared at a price heavier than he imagined, and the Abyss began to seep through the rift he had made. In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), Rhinedottir tells the Tsaritsa that the Tsar incited her (then a herald of the court) and Saarelainen, the Third Descender, to open the gate to the Abyss, and that he alone escaped the consequences by fleeing into the Shadow Realm, which also let him keep his memories of the Third.
- Inside he found Hyperborea's ruins and records, learned what he was (an incomplete Primordial Human made from the Cryo Dragon), and eventually accepted Celestia's offer of the Cryo throne about 2,000 years ago.

- He first assumed Anacharsis had destroyed Hyperborea through folly. Records found alongside the Eitr in his 446th foray convinced him the city's fate was sealed beforehand and that Anacharsis and Koitar had only delayed it by thirty years. He also wondered why the Heavenly Principles never purged the Realm the moment it appeared.
- In his last note he wrote that the passage stood open anew and that the Abyss would end everything within the celestial shell within a few centuries; Rotwang reached a similar conclusion by his own calculation.
- The Tsar died in the Cataclysm 500 years ago; the Pale Crown Palace is his mausoleum.

Connections: - Hyperborea, Anacharsis and Koitar: the Realm holds the city's ruins and records.
- The Belyi Tsar, Anastasya and Saarelainen: the passage he opened.
- The Abyss: the Realm is described as holding it back, yet the opened passage lets it seep in.
- The Heavenly Principles and Celestia: the Tsar wonders why they never destroyed the Realm.
- The Eye of Graeae, Aksinya and the Hvergelmir: they researched or used Realm technology and records.

- Eitr: a Hyperborean creation tied to the Light Realm, recovered from the Shadow Realm.
- Druzhna and the Royal Energy Commission: the Druzhna contain and clear breaches, drawing on Commission intelligence.
- Nod-Krai: a similar substance appears in its Mysterious Space; canon does not say they are connected.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the Realm is a third-person shooter mode introduced in 7.0 and first unlocked in the Archon Quest "Gunfire in the Silent Lands." Elemental Sight, food and some gadgets are unavailable; the Traveler uses firearms such as Shatanaya's Frostsilver, Balsag's Sunwheel and Ashamez's Thunder and throws Frag Crystals. Enemies are usually Fatui Oprichniki, Skirmishers and Landcruisers marked by a purple aura.

Mini Shadow Realms (Facility, Floating Base, Maintenance Center, Ice Quarry, Ruins) are instanced breaches with a boss at the end; Pale Crown Palace and Flamefeather Valley are shooter-style areas; the Edge of Survival is an end-game mode with three strong Realms; the Shadow Realm Analyzer on the personal train turns samples from Shadow Wingdrops into rewards; the Special Recruitment Project's Cycle Training has the Druzhna officer Yarovaya send the Traveler to clear weekly Realms. Version 7.1 mainly adjusted bugs and minimap display.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Shadow Realm as eerily still and quiet; light is flat or absent, sound dull, the air full of pale dust. Characters rely on guns and gear, not Visions. Do not let a Vision holder cast elemental spells inside it. Keep its origin and purpose open.

Its dangers are loss and erasure: people vanish, shadows are "eaten," survivors return changed or not at all. Fatui and Druzhna personnel treat it as a hazard to contain, not a place to explore for fun.

170.comment: Shadow Realm: Shadow Realm breaches and containment
170.content:
Breaches open suddenly in Snezhnaya's tundra and, rarely, on its railways. Royal Energy Commission officials stand by known breaches; the Druzhna, whose duties include containing them, set up perimeters, enter and clear them. Fatui soldiers have been lost inside; those trapped are devoured and warped into monsters lost to reason. The Special Recruitment Project's descriptions say that clearing a Realm releases the lost souls, human and fae.

The high-ranking Druzhna officer Yarovaya oversees these operations from the Druzhna headquarters: verifying public sightings, processing intelligence from the Energy Commission, establishing containment perimeters and leading clearing operations. Rewards and the Tsaritsa's favour are held out to those who help.

171.comment: Shadow Realm: Hyperborea within the Shadow Realm
171.content: The ruins of the Golden City lie inside the Realm and remain free of Abyssal corruption. They hold records of Anacharsis and Koitar's rebellion, of the fae's earliest name ("Filii Adamici Evoluti," "the evolved children of humanity"), and the Eitr. The Belyi Tsar explored them over hundreds of forays and restored a castle there.

key: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual
172.comment: Shadow Realm: The Belyi Tsar's Notes
172.content: Six notes in the Pale Crown Palace record the Tsar's work: the opened passage (I), doubts about Anacharsis (II), the film image and the Abyss's slow seepage (III), the Eitr records and Hyperborea's sealed fate (IV), his acceptance of the Cryo throne and the Gnosis (V), and the passage opened anew with time running short (VI).

173.content:
Shadowmoon (also: false moon, fake moon, moon's shadow, shadow of the moon): The shadowmoon, also called the false moon or the moon's shadow, was an illusory moon that occupied the sky of Teyvat for thousands of years after the real Three Moons were destroyed or banished. It also served as a prison for one fragment of the dead Zibai's soul. When the Traveler and Columbina brought the Frost Moon back in Nod-Krai, the shadowmoon lost its purpose and began to disintegrate. It vanished completely on the night of Lantern Rite in Liyue Harbor, in version 6.3.

Until then it was invisible to the eye except as occasional dark patches, which people took for lunar eclipses. Zhongli worked out that mortals' wishes seemed to trigger each stage of its breakdown.

Established: - It was an illusory "false" moon, a projection of the moon rather than a body of its own.
- The Frost Moon's return left it without a place in the heavens, so it began to disintegrate bit by bit.
- It held Zibai's First Deadly Self, Ziju, and with her the Heavenly Soul (Taiguang) of Zibai's divided soul.
- It disappeared entirely on Lantern Rite night.

- Disintegration comes and goes. While it happens the real moon looks as if a black shadow covers it, which Zhongli identifies as the recent lunar eclipse; when it pauses the shadow cannot be seen at all.
- Zhongli suspected that wishes, such as those made on Xiao Lanterns, trigger the episodes. In The Realm of Clouds the Traveler experiences one exactly when Linlang speaks her wish.
