- Because the soul fragment and the shadowmoon had spent countless years together they had merged, so when the shadowmoon was gone Ziju would cease to exist in the world unless Zibai's other two fragments were reunited with her first.
- Zhongli had been waiting for such an opportunity for thousands of years; he used the moment to reunite the three fragments.

- Zibai's soul had been shattered when she died; Istaroth preserved the pieces in the moment before her death and placed them in her Three Deadly Selves. Taiguang, the Heavenly Soul, was held in Ziju and kept in the shadowmoon; Shuangling, the Earth Soul, was held in Zizhi, who slept beneath the earth in what is now the Chasm; Youjing, the Human Soul, was held in Zijiao, sealed in a painting.
- The Traveler gained access to Ziju's "celestial prison" through a broken jade token that served as a medium. Ziju led them out, but stayed behind, saying her time was nearly up.
- The Traveler received the Earth Soul from Zizhi (Act II) and the Human Soul from Zijiao (Act III). On Lantern Rite night the wishes of the people fully disintegrated the shadowmoon, Zibai's souls merged and she came back, with hazy memories.

Accounts: - Zhongli (The Realm of Clouds): the shadowmoon is a false projection of the moon, the prison confining Zibai's Heavenly Soul, and its collapse is both a danger and an opening.
- The wiki's Three Moons page: the Heavenly Principles projected the shadowmoon to cover up what happened to the Three Moons after the war of funerary flame; Istaroth used it to preserve a portion of Zibai's soul. Only the second half is shown directly in the quest.

- Zibai's own wiki summary credits Istaroth with freezing her at the moment of death and storing her soul in the Selves; Zhongli says the same.

Open questions: Canon does not say what the shadowmoon was made of, whether it ever existed apart from the sky it replaced, or who made it. The Heavenly Principles are the attributed maker (via the wiki) but the quest text read does not state this outright. Do not describe the Heavenly Principles as having sworn to it or as having destroyed it.

It is also unstated how much of the old night-sky cycle (the three sisters' alternating rule over the sky) it imitated.

Connections: Replaced the Three Moons after the war of funerary flame, when the Eternal and Iridescent Moons were destroyed and the Frost Moon banished beyond the false sky. Ended by the return of the Frost Moon (Archon Quest True Moon, version 6.3). Linked to Zibai, the Moon Envoy and one-time god of Lang-Gan, to Istaroth of the Four Shades, to Zhongli, and to Liyue's Lantern Rite.

Related lore: the Chasm (where Lang-Gan stood), the Heavenly Principles' false sky, and the Crimson Moon (a different moon, not the shadowmoon).

How {{char}} behaves: Treat it as a hidden, fading thing after 6.3: it is now gone, and only characters who followed the Lantern Rite events know of it. Ordinary Liyue residents may remember the odd eclipses or the legend of the White Horse Adeptus without knowing the connection. (Suggested use, not canon.)

174.content: After the Frost Moon returned to Teyvat, the shadowmoon broke down bit by bit. To observers, the moon looked briefly blocked by a black shadow (the "lunar eclipse"), then clear. Zhongli suspected wishes triggered it; on Lantern Rite night, with countless Xiao Lanterns released, it fully collapsed. The story was told in the A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon event, a limited-time event when it began.

175.content: Zibai split off Ziju, Zizhi and Zijiao, her Three Deadly Selves, before dying. Istaroth placed her shattered soul in them: the Heavenly Soul (Taiguang) in Ziju, imprisoned in the shadowmoon; the Earth Soul (Shuangling) in Zizhi, who slept in the Chasm; and the Human Soul (Youjing) in Zijiao, who was sealed in a painting and later followed Rex Lapis during the Archon War. The Traveler and Zhongli recovered all three before the shadowmoon vanished, and Zibai returned.

key: The Seven Who Rule the Mortal World
176.content:
The Seven (also: The Seven Archons, Seven Archons, Archons of The Seven, The Seven Who Rule the Mortal World): The Seven (the Seven Archons) are the gods who each preside over one of Teyvat's seven nations and one element. They are the victors of the Archon War, which ended about 2,000 years ago. Each Archon holds a divine throne in Celestia and was given a Gnosis, a chess-piece-like focus. Each also embodies an ideal that shapes their nation. As of 7.1: Venti (Barbatos, Anemo, Freedom, Mondstadt), Zhongli (Morax, Geo, Contracts, Liyue), Raiden Ei (Electro, Eternity, Inazuma), Nahida (Lesser Lord Kusanali, Dendro, Wisdom, Sumeru), Mavuika (Pyro, War, Natlan) and the Tsaritsa, Anastasya (Cryo, Love, Snezhnaya). The Hydro throne (Justice, Fontaine) no longer exists.

Only Barbatos and Morax remain from the original Seven; the other seats have changed hands, most of them during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. The Tsaritsa's Fatui have taken the Gnoses one by one: as of 7.1 she holds six, and the seventh, the Pyro Gnosis, was lost when Irminsul burned.

Established: - Archons are gods, not mortals with Visions. Venti calls Visions "primitive" next to a Gnosis.
- Each Archon's power over their element comes from their divine throne. The thrones hold part of the Authorities the Heavenly Principles took from the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons.
- Archons can die. Their thrones then pass to a successor.
- Venti says an Archon's strength depends on how much they govern their land. He calls himself the weakest of The Seven because he refuses to rule Mondstadt.
- The wiki also names faith as a source of power, alongside rule over a nation and the throne's Authority.
- Archons do not choose who gets a Vision and know nothing about the recipients. They are only obliged to give up part of their Authority to form one when notified to do so (Raiden Shogun's voice-overs, Neuvillette's character story).
- People in Teyvat commonly believe the Archons grant Visions.

- Archons choose their successors, and most chose someone close to them: Ei was Makoto's younger twin, Nahida was created by Rukkhadevata from Irminsul's purest branch, and Focalors was one of Egeria's Oceanids.
- Pyro Archons are mortal humans who age and die. They win the throne through the Pilgrimage, and on ascending the Sacred Flame gives them much of the land's knowledge and memory.
- A divine throne can be destroyed. This takes enormous power and the death of the Archon seated on it, and the Authority inside returns to its Dragon Sovereign. Focalors did this in Fontaine (4.2).

Members: Current holders of the six surviving thrones (7.1):
- Anemo, Mondstadt: Barbatos (Venti). God of Freedom, ascended 2,600 years ago.
- Geo, Liyue: Morax (Zhongli), called Rex Lapis. God of Contracts and eldest of The Seven. Retired as a mortal in 1.1.
- Electro, Inazuma: Beelzebul (Raiden Ei), who rules as the Raiden Shogun. God of Eternity, Archon since 500 years ago.
- Dendro, Sumeru: Buer (Nahida), Lesser Lord Kusanali. God of Wisdom and the youngest Archon, about 500 years old.
- Pyro, Natlan: Mavuika, holder of the shared divine name Haborym. God of War.
- Cryo, Snezhnaya: Vassaga (Anastasya), the Tsaritsa. God of Love, Archon since 500 years ago.
Hydro, Fontaine (Justice): Egeria, then Focalors. The throne was destroyed in 4.2, so there will be no more Hydro Archons.

Predecessors:
- Electro: Makoto (Baal), who died in the Cataclysm. Ei served as her kagemusha, so Inazumans saw the twins as one Archon.
- Dendro: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who died in the Cataclysm and was later erased from Irminsul.
- Hydro: Egeria, the "Mistress of Many Waters", who died in the Cataclysm.
- Cryo: the Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi, who died in the Cataclysm.
- Pyro: a long line of mortal Archons, beginning with Xbalanque about 2,000 years ago.

Regnal titles: Rex Lapis (Morax); Raiden Shogun (Makoto, then Ei); Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata before her; "Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws" (the title Furina used while ruling in Focalors' name); Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya (Anastasya) and Belyi Tsar before her. Pyro Archons inherit Ancient Names: Xbalanque's "Kiongozi" passed to Mavuika. Venti uses no regnal title. Neuvillette calls Barbatos "the God of Breeze and Hope." The divine names Baal and Beelzebul come from the 2.1 quest Wishes, Buer from the 3.2 Sumeru Archon Quest, and Vassaga from the 7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quest.

Powers: A divine throne gives an Archon authority over their element. A Gnosis, normally kept inside the Archon's chest, amplifies elemental power and links its holder directly to Celestia. Archons keep their elemental power and their thrones without a Gnosis.

Gnoses can be pulled out by force, as Signora did to Venti, or handed over willingly, as Zhongli and Ei did. Those who are not Archons usually cannot use another element's Gnosis freely. Dottore said Nahida could not fight with the Electro Gnosis, though she used it to enter Rukkhadevata's realm of consciousness and later used the Pyro Gnosis to burn Irminsul. The Wanderer could wield the Electro Gnosis only after heavy modification by Dottore and the Akademiya. Neuvillette and the Traveler have each used a Gnosis briefly without that limit.

Archons have used their Gnoses to power national infrastructure:
- Liyue: Morax's power minted Mora at the Golden House, which has stood idle since he gave up the Geo Gnosis.
- Sumeru: the Dendro Gnosis powered the Akasha System.
- Fontaine: the Hydro Gnosis powered the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, which was secretly merged with Focalors.
- Natlan: Mavuika kept the Pyro Gnosis in reserve and used it to sustain the Sacred Flame during the Abyss's attack.
Ei tried and failed to turn the Electro Gnosis into an energy source for her puppets. Gnoses, like Visions, can hold their bearer's obsessions, and the Wanderer lost his ambition when his Gnosis was taken.

History: After the war of funerary flame about 6,000 years ago, the Heavenly Principles set up seven divine thrones in Celestia and had gods fight for them and their Gnoses. This was the Archon War. Many gods died. The last seat was claimed about 2,000 years ago, and the victors founded the seven nations. The original Seven were fairly close and shared the duty of guiding humanity; they used to gather in Liyue to drink with Rex Lapis.

Different regions settled their wars at different times. Morax held Liyue from its founding 3,700 years ago. Barbatos rose after Decarabian fell 2,600 years ago. Makoto, Egeria, Xbalanque and the Belyi Tsar took their seats around 2,000 years ago. Natlan's gods never took part, because the land was consumed by war between dragons and humans; Xbalanque became the first Pyro Archon by defeating the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl. In Fontaine, Celestia ordered Egeria to succeed the fallen Remus.

The Cataclysm 500 years ago, when Khaenri'ah fell and the Abyss spread, killed Makoto, Rukkhadevata, Egeria and the Belyi Tsar. Ei, Nahida, Focalors and Anastasya replaced them. Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame so she could return 500 years later. Venti says the Tsaritsa changed after that catastrophe; he knew her well 500 years ago but has not seen her since. She cut ties with the other Archons.

Afterwards, Ei built the Shogun puppet, finished about 400 years ago, gave her Gnosis to Yae Miko and withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia. Nahida was confined in the Sanctuary of Surasthana for 500 years while the sages promoted Rukkhadevata's legacy. Focalors split from her body, leaving Furina to play the Hydro Archon for 500 years. Anastasya took in Pierro and founded the Fatui, whose aims are to collect all seven Gnoses and rebel against Celestia.

Losses of the Gnoses, in story order:
- 1.0: Signora tore the Anemo Gnosis from Venti.
- 1.1: Zhongli handed the Geo Gnosis to Signora under a contract with the Tsaritsa.
- 2.1: Yae Miko traded the Electro Gnosis to Scaramouche for the Traveler's safety.
- 3.2: Nahida recovered the Electro Gnosis from Scaramouche. Dottore then received the Electro Gnosis in exchange for erasing his segments, as Nahida demanded, and the Dendro Gnosis in exchange for information about the false sky.
- 4.2: Focalors destroyed the Hydro throne, and Neuvillette gave the Hydro Gnosis to Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift".
- 5.x: Capitano failed to seize the Pyro Gnosis from Mavuika by force, acknowledged his defeat and abandoned that mission.
- 6.6: The Traveler took the Pyro Gnosis from Mavuika so Nahida could burn the corrupted Irminsul, and it disappeared.

Gnosis origin: The 7.1 Archon Quest revealed where the Gnoses came from. The war of funerary flame left the Heavenly Principles too weakened to enforce their order directly. The Third Descender, Saarelainen, was Anastasya's lover and an ancestor of the Khaenri'ahns. After the Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya, he let his body be split into the seven Gnoses. In return they resurrected her and promised never to harm their descendants, and his curse sends them into slumber if they break that promise. They harmed the Khaenri'ahns in the Cataclysm and have been dormant since. The Gnoses were used to consolidate the Archon system, and Visions, which derive from it, are linked to him too. All memory of Saarelainen was removed from Irminsul, so Anastasya does not remember him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, six thrones remain, since the Hydro throne is gone. All six current Archons are alive. The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses (Cryo, Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro). The Pyro Gnosis is missing.

- Venti lives freely in Mondstadt.
- Zhongli lives as a consultant at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor in Liyue, which now governs itself.
- Ei co-rules Inazuma with the Shogun puppet.
- Nahida rules Sumeru openly.
- Mavuika leads a recovering Natlan.
- Furina lives as an ordinary Fontainian, and Neuvillette, the Hydro Dragon, remains Chief Justice.
- Anastasya rules Snezhnaya directly and in 7.1 cooperated with the Traveler against Ronova.
On the missing Pyro Gnosis, the Tsaritsa says that, being formed from the Third Descender's remains, it cannot coexist with the Ley Lines for long and will one day be excised from them.

Most of The Seven are known to the Traveler personally, but few ordinary people know that Venti, Zhongli or Nahida is a god. Ei and Nahida are publicly worshipped. In Liyue, the public believes Rex Lapis died at the 1.1 Rite of Descension.

Accounts: - Venti, in Ending Note (1.0): The Seven "don't always get along well", but he never expected the Tsaritsa to plot against another Archon. He says a Gnosis marks an Archon's status as one of The Seven.
- Zhongli, in his character story: Rex Lapis remembers the moment the last Archon took their seat. The Seven were scattered and diverse but all bore the burden of guiding humanity, and many titles have since changed hands.
- Ganyu: the youngest current Archon is Sumeru's god of Dendro, "merely five hundred years old."

Open questions: Whether the Archon title depends on a Gnosis; what a Gnosis does for the Heavenly Principles; where the Pyro Gnosis is now; what the Third Descender's seal holds. Canon leaves all of these open as of 7.1, and none should be resolved in roleplay.

Connections: Separate entries cover each Archon, each Gnosis, the Archon War, Celestia, the Heavenly Principles, the Seven Sovereigns, Visions, and the Statues of The Seven (the Archons' roadside statues, where the Traveler resonates with each element).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): Archons are rarely recognised in person. Venti, Zhongli and Nahida move among people unnoticed, and many people know their god only from statues, temples and stories. Keep them distinct: each embodies a different ideal and governs differently. Venti refuses to rule, Zhongli gave up rule, Ei and the Shogun guard Eternity, Nahida rules gently, Mavuika leads in war, and Anastasya rules absolutely. When elemental power runs through an Archon, the ends of their hair glow in their element's colour; Mavuika's whole hair lights up.

Ordinary people believe the Archons hand out Visions; a scholar or an Archon may know otherwise. No one but the Traveler remembers Rukkhadevata. Fontaine has no living Hydro Archon, and Furina should not be treated as a god. Do not have Venti or Zhongli get their Gnoses back. Do not invent a council of Archons or friendships canon does not show: as of 7.1 the Tsaritsa has had no contact with Venti for 500 years.

177.comment: The Seven: Divine Thrones of The Seven
177.content:
Celestia holds seven divine thrones, one per element, each containing part of an Authority the Heavenly Principles took from the Seven Sovereigns. Neuvillette says the First Usurper "seized a part of the dragons' power" and that it is now the basis of the Archons' Authorities (4.1). A throne passes to a successor when its Archon dies. Destroying a throne takes immense power and the seated Archon's death, and returns the Authority to its dragon. Focalors destroyed the Hydro throne this way in 4.2, so only six remain.

Before the Archon War ended, phrases like "divine throne" did not necessarily mean these Celestial seats. Decarabian's death, for example, is called the crumbling of "an ancient seat of divinity."

178.content:
The first Seven were Barbatos, Morax, Baal (Makoto), Rukkhadevata, Egeria, Xbalanque and the Belyi Tsar. They took their seats at different times, ending about 2,000 years ago, and would gather in Liyue to drink with Rex Lapis. As of 7.1 only Barbatos and Morax survive. Morax is the eldest and Barbatos the second eldest. Ei fought through the Archon War beside Makoto but only became Archon after her twin's death.

Because of the 3.2 erasure, the world believes Nahida was one of the first Seven and does not remember Rukkhadevata.

179.content: Egeria became Hydro Archon about 2,000 years ago, after Remus fell, and died in the Cataclysm. Her Oceanid Focalors succeeded her, split her divinity from her body, and left that body, Furina, to play the Hydro Archon for 500 years. In Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2) Focalors had herself executed by the Oratrice, which destroyed the throne and returned the full Hydro Authority to Neuvillette, the Hydro Sovereign. Furina abdicated and lives as an ordinary Fontainian. Neuvillette gave the Hydro Gnosis, unaffected by the throne's destruction, to Arlecchino.

180.comment: The Seven: Pyro Archons and the Pilgrimage
180.content:
Natlan's Archons are mortals who age and die. Each new Pyro Archon wins the seat through the Pilgrimage, gains the Sacred Flame's knowledge on ascending, and carries the divine name Haborym. Xbalanque, the first, defeated the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl and established Natlan's system. The current Pyro Archon, Mavuika, placed her life in the Sacred Flame 500 years ago so she could return to finish the war against the Abyss, and she has returned.

Capitano's attempt to take her Gnosis ended without a result, and the Fatui never obtained it. Mavuika later gave it, through the Traveler, to Nahida to burn Irminsul (6.6), and it was lost. She said she sensed its loss even after handing it away.

181.comment: The Seven: Representatives of The Seven
181.content:
Some Archons ruled through figures the public took for the Archon:
- Ei served as kagemusha to her twin Makoto, and the people saw them as one Raiden Shogun until Makoto died 500 years ago.
- The Shogun, a puppet Ei finished about 400 years ago, has ruled in her place since. After 2.1 they share rule, and few know the two are separate.
- Furina was publicly the Hydro Archon for 500 years, though only Focalors held the throne and Authority. She abdicated in 4.2.

182.comment: The Seven: The Tsaritsa's Gnosis collection
182.content:
The Fatui have collected Gnoses for the Tsaritsa since 1.0. As of 7.1 she holds six: her own Cryo Gnosis, plus the Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses. Before Signora's funeral (teaser "A Winter Night's Lazzo"), she played chess with Pierro with the Anemo and Geo Gnoses on the board as pieces. In 7.1 she told the Traveler her two reasons: to amplify her power beyond a single Archon's against the Heavenly Principles, and to open the Third Descender's seal. She asked the Traveler where the Pyro Gnosis was, the only one unaccounted for.

In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), the Tsaritsa combined her Cryo mastery with the six Gnoses to slow time around Rhinedottir over tea. This made Rhinedottir miss the window to revive Ronova's victims, and Celestia stripped Ronova of her Authority. Rhinedottir chose not to fight her and called her "quite a worthy rival".

183.content:
Thirteen Sovereign Lords (also: Thirteen Lords, Sovereign Lords, Thirteen Dragonlords, Sovereign Rulers' Council, Ch'ule-L): The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were thirteen artificial rulers made by Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, to govern ancient Natlantea. Each held a territory, and together they met as a council in the Chamber of Deliberation under the First Lord as Speaker. They oppressed Natlantea's humans for thousands of years. Ten fell when the Sacred City of Tollan collapsed in the war between Xbalanque and Xiuhcoatl, and the Ninth Lord, long sealed in Chichen Uctokah, was freed from her bonds and put to rest by the Traveler at her own request. A few survive in changed form, notably Ajaw and the Eleventh Lord's surviving core in Ineffa.

They are not ordinary dragons. Citlali explains in the quest "Smoldering" that they were artificial intelligences built with secret source technology, with greater intelligence and authority than the Pyro dragons themselves. Their personal names end in a number in a Mayan language (Hun is one, Ka' two, and so on up to Ooxlahun, thirteen) plus the designation Ch'ule-L.

Established: - Creator: Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon of the Seven Sovereigns, who ruled Natlantea.
- Role: each Lord governed an individual territory of Natlantea; they assembled in the Chamber of Deliberation to debate and vote, with the First Lord, the Valiant One, presiding as Speaker.
- Fate: ten fell in the fall of Tollan; the Ninth (Ixlel) was freed from her imprisonment and put to rest by the Traveler in "Open Your Heart to Me"; Ajaw (probably the Tenth) lives on as a bound companion of the adventurer Kinich; part of the Eleventh lives on in Ineffa.

- Rank and title (as listed by the wiki from in-game records): 1 Valiant One; 2 Jade Maiden; 3 Weaver of Secrets; 4 Hermit of Myriad Fates; 5 Bestower of Bitter Springs; 6 He Who Shakes the Earth Like Thunder in His Wrath; 7 Toxic Rain Over Boundless Forests; 8 Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers; 9 Chronicler of the End Times; 10 Undying Wings of Lofty Isolation; 11 Mirror of the Dawning Morn; 12 Murmuring Spring; 13 Bonebreaker. Each Lord's records carry a number "CL-01" to "CL-13".
- In the Chamber of Deliberation, the council records state that once consensus was reached, even abstainers were bound to uphold the decision.
- The Lords and Xiuhcoatl survived the Heavenly Principles' invasion by sheltering in the underground city of Tollan.
- After the War of Funerary Flame the awakened dragons destroyed the angels who had guided the human civilisations, sparing only Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night, according to item and quest text. The Lords then oppressed the humans of Natlantea.

- Treatment of humans: apart from the Eighth Lord, canon shows the Lords as hostile or contemptuous toward humans. The Fifth Lord proposed burning human settlements above a certain size to forestall rebellion; the Twelfth countered that humans should be manipulated into thinning their own numbers; the Third abstained, calling humans soulless creatures bound to star-signs.
- Impeachment of Kukulkan: the Regent's experiments on humans led the Lords to vote nine in favour, none against and four abstaining (the First, Third, Fourth and Eighth) to impeach him. He later helped the humans by teaching them to use phlogiston.
- Human victories: the Sixth Lord was killed by an arrow from Lianca, and Ixquieh and Ahpub tricked the Tenth Lord into being buried under a mountain. Xbalanque's army then stormed Tollan.

Accounts: Who claims what: Awanyu (a Secret Source Servant) tells the Traveler in the World Quest "Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment" that ten of the Thirteen fell when Tollan collapsed, one remained in Chichen Uctokah, and one survives, though not in the form it would have wished. The wiki's table adds that the Third Lord's consciousness lives in the Night Kingdom (from weapon texts such as Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow and Flute of Ezpitzal). The Flower-Feather Clan's account in the book "Fires of Autumn Twilight" holds that the Sixth Lord survived Tollan and was killed by Lianca's second daughter in Och-Kan's reign, while the council record B-CL-13097 already speaks of him as fallen earlier.

The Eighth Lord was not killed in battle: record B-CL-16130 shows the council trying her, on the Twelfth Lord's motion, for her favour toward Lianca and humanity, and voting for her execution. Smoldering says she stayed loyal to the dragonkin to the end. Citlali's reading, in the same quest, is that Ajaw is a Sovereign Lord who has lost most of his memory and power.

Open questions: Canon leaves open which Lord Ajaw originally was, what elements and territories most Lords had, and how a Lord's artificial nature relates to dragon bodies and "cores" (the Ninth was bound in a statue over the Core of Chu'ulel; Ineffa's heart-core is a surviving half of the Eleventh). Do not claim that any element or territory is certain where canon is silent.

Connections: - Xiuhcoatl and the Seven Sovereigns: the Lords' maker, the Pyro Sovereign who was frozen by the Heavenly Principles and later killed by Xbalanque.
- Kukulkan: Xiuhcoatl's younger brother and Regent, impeached by the Lords.
- Lianca and the Flower-Feather Clan: the Eighth Lord adopted Lianca, who then fought the dragons.
- Och-Kan: the half-human ruler who sealed the Ninth Lord in a statue.
- Ajaw and Kinich: the Tenth Lord's present-day form and his contract partner.
- Ineffa: carries the Eleventh Lord's benevolent core; the Eleventh's hostile half was imprisoned in the Temple of Cascading Colors.

Quests to reference: "Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment" (World Quest), "Open Your Heart to Me" (5.2), and "Smoldering" and "Searing" (5.8). For the Eleventh Lord's story as told in "Searing", see the entry below. No Lord is reported in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content in the sources read; their status is as of the Natlan-era quests.

184.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Eleventh Lord and Ineffa
184.content: The Eleventh Lord despised humanity more than her peers. After Xiuhcoatl fell, she split her mind into two cores: one longing for a place to belong and one that kept her hostility. She asked Lianca to destroy the benevolent half, falsely calling it hostile; Lianca saw through the lie and imprisoned the hostile half in the Temple of Cascading Colors, after which the Eleventh Lord cursed the benevolent half to suffer for any goodwill toward humans. Lianca sent that half away from Natlan. About two thousand years later it was scavenged in Nod-Krai by Aino and used to build Ineffa, who began suffering malfunctions from the curse. In "Searing" the Eleventh Lord posed as the Eighth Lord, then revealed herself and tried to take control of Ineffa. Ineffa overloaded the curse and, with the Traveler and her Moon Wheel, destroyed the Eleventh Lord's form in a Secret Source Automaton: Configuration Device. Her last words admitted that she too longed for a place to belong.

185.content: The Ninth Lord ruled Chichen Uctokah, the original name of Ochkanatlan, and kept an unusual interest in a "well" that other Lords feared, now the Old Core of Chu'ulel. Och-Kan had it excavated and found her; he later bound her in a statue. In "Open Your Heart to Me" the Traveler lowers the water around the statue, gathers the pieces of her heart and frees her at her request; she pours her remaining energy into the heart and her soul is put to rest. She is proud, insists on her rank, and believes only the Chosen of Dragons may release her. The item Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon describes its heart as that of the Dragonlord of Chichen Uctokah.

186.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Weaver of Secrets (Third Lord)
186.content: The Third Lord ruled land in the Tezcatepetonco Range. She was skilled in divination and held that humans' fates are fixed by the Heavenly Principles. Pitying her dragons, who were degenerating into beasts after the War of Funerary Flame, she made a pact with human tribes (forerunners of the Masters of the Night-Wind): she would provide a labyrinth of mirrors and a fortress of mist if they appointed a "Holy Sovereign" to put the dragons into a dream state. She merged her consciousness into the Night Kingdom. Her friend, the Eighth Lord, predicted the plan would bring humans more suffering, and weapon text shows the Holy Sovereigns did suffer. The pact later lapsed under Och-Kan and was renewed through the priest Wagadu, as described in weapon texts.

key: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
187.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Eighth Lord and Lianca
187.content: The Eighth Lord ruled Ch'upikaq Tajin, today Flower-Feather Clan territory, and is the only Lord known to have been kind to humans, raising Lianca as a dragon princess. She had the Second Lord forge a longbow (Chain Breaker) for her daughter and accepted that Lianca might one day oppose her. For this she was tried by the council and executed during the siege of Tollan.

188.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Ajaw, the Tenth Lord
188.content: Ajaw calls himself an almighty sovereign ruler and is bound to the adventurer Kinich by a contract: Kinich receives Ajaw's power and Ajaw will eventually take over Kinich's body at his death. The council records say the Tenth Lord was tricked by humans (see Ring of Yaxche) and sealed alive in a mountain, matching how Kinich found him. In "Smoldering", Citlali concludes from a slip by Ajaw that he is a Sovereign Lord; he does not remember which one.

189.content:
Three Moons (also: Three Moon Goddesses, Three Moon Sisters, Moon Sisters, Moon Goddesses, Trilune, Trilunar Authority, Lunar Palace): The Three Moons are three ancient moons and the goddesses bound to them, also called the Three Moon Goddesses or Three Moon Sisters: Aria of the Eternal Moon, Canon of the Frost Moon and Sonnet of the Iridescent Moon. The Dragon King Nibelung raised them from the planet's crust, at what is now Nod-Krai, to oversee Teyvat and wield his authority while he travelled the sea of stars. Their power is called the Trilunar Authority or Trilune. In the war of funerary flame the Heavenly Principles shattered the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and flung the Frost Moon beyond the false sky. All three goddesses then died, because Teyvat no longer accepted them. To hide this, the Heavenly Principles hung an illusory "shadowmoon" in the night sky.

Their story is the core of the Nod-Krai Archon Quest, Song of the Welkin Moon (5.8-6.6). There, Columbina, born in Nod-Krai as the new Frost Moon goddess (Kuutar), receives the authority of all three moons and becomes the Trilune Goddess. She defeats Dottore, who had stolen the moons' power, and the Frost Moon returns inside Teyvat's sky.

Established: - Eternal Moon (Aria): the first and largest moon. Its gravity was said to raise the tides. It was shattered.
- Frost Moon (Canon): the second moon and the brightest. It was banished beyond the false sky, but has now returned to Teyvat's sky with Columbina as its goddess.
- Iridescent Moon (Sonnet): the third and smallest moon, with a faint light that made fleeting halos. It was shattered, and its remains became the Crimson Moon.

- The sisters lived in the Lunar Palace. One at a time, they ruled the night sky, riding through the heavens in a silver carriage or chariot and changing places about three times a month.
- When a goddess dies, her remains can condense into a Moon Marrow. The Moon Marrows hold what is left of the sisters' power and are a source of Light Realm energy.
- Before the war, many civilisations worshipped the moons rather than the Heavenly Principles. Some accounts also say the moons received the dead, with "boatmen" ferrying souls to cities upon the moon.

- Nibelung made the moons with draconic Secret Source technology. The Eternal Moon in particular is called a piece of that technology (Natlan Archon Quest, 5.3). Nicole describes the goddesses as "shadows of the planet", extensions of Nibelung's will, created to keep the world alive and working.
- The sisters agreed to share their power equally so that none of them would grow too strong. They saw their role as protecting Teyvat, not ruling it.
- A Frost Moon map description says the ancient spirits of the frostbound reaches called the three silver lights "Dilimbabbar", and that the lights first marked the waxing and waning of light, the seasons and the passing years.

History: Nibelung left Teyvat and the moons kept it for him. When the Heavenly Principles arrived, the sisters let them stay. They then watched the Heavenly Principles remake the world's rules and destroy the dragons. When Nibelung returned, corrupted by the Abyss, the sisters could not agree whether to side with him. He imprisoned them and turned their moons into weapons. The Heavenly Principles answered by destroying or banishing the moons, and the goddesses died.

The Heavenly Principles, the First Descender, came several millennia after Nibelung left. Canon calls them "a guest in our home". They reshaped Teyvat down to its foundations, partly by using the sisters' authorities. Sonnet opposed this. Aria and Canon chose to wait and see whether the new order would help the world. After a 40-year war, the Heavenly Principles and the Four Shades overthrew the Seven Sovereigns and raised the false sky. Because the moons, also creations of Nibelung, never stepped in, the dragons came to see the sisters as traitors. The Heavenly Principles let the moons remain because their task of maintaining the planet did not conflict with heavenly aims. When celestial nails began falling on civilisations that pushed against the rules, the sisters were horrified. Canon tried to help some of them, but the sisters obeyed in the end, since their duty was to keep Teyvat intact until Nibelung returned.

In the Funerary Year Nibelung came back carrying the Abyss. He took the sisters' disagreement for disloyalty and sealed them inside the "moon's reflection", a prison of warped space and time. Then he turned the moons into weapons against Celestia. The Heavenly Principles treated this as a breach of their peace: they shattered the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and flung the Frost Moon beyond the false sky. Most dragons celebrated.

Cut off from moons that were destroyed or exiled, the goddesses lost their "rationale" for existing in Teyvat. Alice later explains that the world itself then rejected them and drained their strength. Inside the prison they were shielded from all of this, but could neither escape nor learn what was happening outside.

Their ends came separately:
- Aria died soon after the war. Part of her remains condensed into the Eternal Moon Marrow, which the Frostmoon Scions later kept as a sacred relic. Other pieces of the Eternal Moon rained onto Teyvat, and the rest was hidden beyond the false sky.
- Sonnet, in agony over her shattered moon, fused her soul with the Abyss to stay alive. She became the baleful Crimson Moon, which Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty revered as a source of Abyssal power.
- Canon lived longest because the Frost Moon was still intact. She guided the survivors of Hyperborea to Hiisi Island, and by their tradition gave them hereditary gifts such as kuuvahki sensitivity and their antler crowns. Then she too faded. The survivors took the name Frostmoon Scions in her honour.

Present day: In the present (5.1-6.3), the false sky briefly cracked over Natlan, Dottore stole the moons' power in Nod-Krai and was defeated by Columbina as the Trilune Goddess, and the Frost Moon returned inside Teyvat's sky, ending the shadowmoon illusion.

- During the Abyss's assault on Natlan (5.1), Mavuika's strike broke the false sky for a moment, revealing the true sky and the Eternal Moon's shattered remnants. The crack closed, and the public was told it was an astronomical anomaly.
- The Fatui pulled Eternal Moon fragments down into Nod-Krai and built the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau around one of them.
- Dottore schemed for the moons' power. On Moon-Prayer Night (6.2) he seized Columbina's Moon Marrows and later built an artificial one, briefly making himself a false god with trilunar authority. Columbina returned as the Trilune Goddess with the sisters' greater authority and defeated him (6.3). Sandrone sacrificed herself to complete the plan that revived Columbina. She was later reactivated and is active again as of 7.1.
- The Frost Moon was drawn back inside the false sky and lights Teyvat's night again. The shadowmoon lost its purpose, faded, and vanished during Lantern Rite, releasing the fragment of Zibai's soul held within it.
- Lauma keeps the Eternal Moon Marrow and Arlecchino keeps the Iridescent Moon Marrow.

As of 7.1, Columbina is the sole moon goddess and holds the Trilune, and the Frost Moon remains in Teyvat's sky. The Traveler can visit it: Columbina took them there, where the Heavenly Principles had hidden the twins' spaceship after the cataclysm. Dottore survived his defeat inside Irminsul as the "Exalted Master of the Heretical Path". He was finally killed when Nahida burned Irminsul (6.6), and he did not use moon power in that last fight. No 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya content found in this research changes the sisters' fate.

Accounts: After the moons disappeared, the people of Teyvat passed down conflicting legends:
- Liyue books (Moonlit Bamboo Forest, Records of Jueyun, Heart's Desire) tell of three sister goddesses in a Lunar Palace who took turns crossing the sky in a silver carriage. Some versions say the sisters betrayed and killed one another. Others say only two died and the moon now in the sky is one of their corpses.
- One weapon legend (Moonpiercer) says the last surviving goddess grieved so much that she never left her palace again.
- Dragon-side accounts (Fractured Halo) treat the sisters as traitors to Nibelung and record that the dragons cheered their deaths.
- The sisters' own account, given to Columbina, describes naive acceptance rather than coercion.
- Nilotpala Lotuses are said to be tied to the three sisters, which is why they bloom at night.
- The angel Nabu Malikata told King Deshret stories of the three moons, and from them he deduced that the false sky exists.
- Ziqiao, one of Zibai's Deadly Selves, told the moons' story to people she met across Liyue. The Liyue books grew from her tales and are not always faithful to them. Zibai herself once served as a Moon Envoy, sent by the Heavenly Principles to help the sisters.
- Nicole and another angel, writing together as "Mr. Nine", put the Three Moons into Flowers for Princess Fischl. The Mitternachts Waltz text tells how two of three bright moons were "shredded by a sword".
- Tsurumi Island murals address the moons in Latin as "Trivia". Columbina's Elemental Burst calls the moon goddesses "Iynx".

Open questions: - Canon does not settle whether the sisters were coerced partners or willing observers of the Heavenly Principles' order. Both views appear in-game.
- It is not clear whether the Heavenly Principles knew Nibelung had imprisoned the goddesses before they struck the moons.

- Exactly how far the Trilunar Authority reaches: the wiki groups it as rule over Life, Death, Time and Space, later passed to the Four Shades. Treat this as summary, not a verbatim definition.
- The meaning of Moonlit Bamboo Forest's "one love", the morning stars, and of the names "Aralos", "Solnari" and "Cannon" on Alice's note in a teaser.
- How long the sisters were imprisoned, given the prison's distorted flow of time.

Connections: Nibelung (creator); the Heavenly Principles and Four Shades (rivals and inheritors of their authority); the false sky and shadowmoon (the cover-up); the Moon Marrows, kuuvahki and the Moon Wheel (what remains of them); the Frostmoon Scions and Hyperborea (their worshippers); Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty (Sonnet's corruption); Columbina (successor and Trilune Goddess).

Gameplay: Nod-Krai's Lunar reactions and Moonsign mechanics are presented in-world as drawing on the moons' power (kuuvahki). See the system entries for the rules. The Spiral Abyss shows lunar imagery, including an Abyssal Moon Spire and phase shifts called the "Moment of Syzygy". Whether these connect directly to the Three Moons is unconfirmed.

190.content: The "moon's reflection" is a prison of warped space and time that Nibelung made to keep the Three Moon Sisters out of the war of funerary flame. Every path inside it leads back to the moment of their imprisonment, so they could never escape or learn what had happened outside. In Song of the Welkin Moon, Columbina banishes herself there to escape Dottore. Travelling backwards through it, she meets the imprisoned sisters, who give her their authority. She then leaves her soul there, anchored by Luonnotar, until she is revived in the present (6.3).

191.content: The Trilune, or Trilunar Authority, is the combined power of the three moons. Aria says it is bound to Teyvat's most fundamental rules. Dottore took its raw power by capturing the Moon Marrows and later made an artificial marrow. The Traveler was unaffected by the authority he gained, and authority drawn from marrows proved weaker than what the living sisters had handed to Columbina. Since True Moon (6.3), Columbina is the Trilune Goddess, the one moon goddess of Teyvat. Lauma and Arlecchino keep the surviving Moon Marrows.

192.comment: Three Moons: Moon Sisters and the Heavenly Principles
192.content: The sisters first welcomed the Heavenly Principles as a guest and let their authorities be used to rewrite Teyvat's laws. Sonnet objected, while Aria and Canon waited to see what would happen. Under the new order, angels guided humanity. The sisters got on well with the angels and, by some accounts, even with the Four Shades. Many peoples worshipped the moons for comfort against the harsh rules. On the wiki's reading of the 6.7 world quest The Unmanned Vessel, around this time the sisters gave up their old forms for human ones. They also witnessed the union of the angel Koitar and the voyager Anacharsis about thirty years before Nibelung's return. The celestial nails horrified them. They had begun preparing countermeasures after Hyperborea fell, but Nibelung returned before they could act.

193.comment: Three Moons: Xiuhcoatl and the silent moons
193.content: According to the weapon text of Fractured Halo, the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl went to each of the three moons in search of Nibelung during a time of upheaval. "Shadows poured over the sky", snowfields turned black and volcanoes clogged with ice. None of the sisters answered him. Canon does not say whether their silence was chosen.

194.content:
Three Realms (also: Human Realm, realms of the world): The three realms are the Light Realm, the Void Realm and the Human Realm. The Light Realm is the home of pure elemental beings such as dragons and elemental lifeforms. The Void Realm, better known as the Abyss, is a destructive force that corrupts and unmakes. The Human Realm is the realm of gods and humanity, created by the Heavenly Principles. They are not separate places but concurrent facets of one world that can occupy the same space.

Each has its own current: ley lines for the Human Realm, elemental currents for the Light Realm and dark currents for the Void Realm. The Light Realm and Void Realm are opposed, the Human Realm sits between them, and the Abyss Order and other Abyssal monsters seek to tear down the human world.

Established: - The Light Realm (elemental), the Void Realm (abyssal) and the Human Realm (created by the Heavenly Principles) coexist in the world of Teyvat as facets of it, not as distant locations.
- An area may be dominated by one realm's power, while elsewhere the three keep their influence in balance.

- When the Heavenly Principles descended, it vanquished the Seven Sovereigns of the Light Realm, subjugated nature and the Light Realm, and used phlogiston as the basis for the seven elements' Elemental Energy. It then created the Human Realm, including gods and humanity (per the books "Before Sun and Moon" and the Bathysmal Vishap records in The Byakuyakoku Collection).
- The Human Realm was at some point interposed between the Light Realm and the Void Realm.
- Creatures of the Human Realm and of the Light Realm (elemental beings) share the continent, though the two tend to conflict. The Void Realm threatens both, so the other two may cooperate to halt its encroachment.
- Elemental beings and Human Realm creatures can be made compatible with each other. Vishaps were modified to accept Orobashi's coral despite its Human Realm origin, and Sangacorallia break the Light Realm's pure elemental energy into something the Human Realm tolerates. The Void Realm's power, by contrast, has only been shown to destroy or corrupt.

- The Void Realm originates from the sea of stars and is opposed to the Light Realm. Its corruption affects creatures of the Human Realm under Celestia's dominion and is especially harmful to elemental beings, who can repel it with the Light Realm's power.
- The Light Realm is called "undissipated hope itself" by the Belyi Tsar and Aksinya. Narrowing its possibilities into the seven elements and anchoring Fate is said, by Neuvillette's Vision profile and the Tsar's notes, to have turned its "love" into resentment that must be suppressed to maintain the Human Realm, and to have let the Abyss anchor into Teyvat at the end of time.
- Barbeloth describes the Abyss as the hatred carried by every possibility of fate that never came to pass.

Accounts: - Tsumi, in the Three Realms Gateway Offering quest, says the people of Byakuyakoku believe in three realms, the Vishap Realm (called the Light Realm in most books), the Human Realm and the Void Realm. She names the three currents and presents the Light Realm's energy as able to vanquish the Void Realm's darkness. She also believes the Abyss Order finds the Void Realm's power addictive.
- The Heavenly Principles' account in "Before Sun and Moon" presents the refraction of the Light Realm as founding the Human Realm. Later voices, the Belyi Tsar and Aksinya, present it as a loss of possibility and hope.

- After Enjou tricked the vishaps into upsetting the balance of the three realms in Enkanomiya, the vishaps, despite hating humanity, aided humans against the encroaching Void Realm (Three Realms Gateway Offering: Aftermath).
- The wiki reads the volume of elemental power each realm can handle as the main difference between the Light and Human Realms, inferred from wording ("elemental flow" versus "elemental currents"). This is interpretation, not an in-game statement.

Open questions: Canon does not say what the realms physically are, how they overlap, or how their currents behave. Do not resolve this with theory.

Fan theories that the Light Realm became the Abyss, that the Shadow Realm belongs with the Light Realm, or that the Human Realm was literally built on the Light Realm are unconfirmed. Nor does canon reconcile Nibelung's role with the Tsar's claim that narrowing the Light Realm anchored the Abyss.

Connections: Light Realm: cosmology.light-realm. Void Realm: cosmology.abyss, cosmology.abyssal-corruption, faction.abyss-order. Human Realm: cosmology.heavenly-principles, cosmology.celestia, cosmology.ley-lines. Rulers and key figures: cosmology.seven-sovereigns, historical.nibelung. Elements: system.elements, system.phlogiston. Enkanomiya and its quest: location.enkanomiya, npc.enjou, quest.three-realms-gateway-offering.

How {{char}} behaves: This is the project's suggested handling, not canon. Few ordinary people use the term "three realms"; scholars, Enkanomiya natives, vishaps, dragons or those close to the Abyss might. Keep it mysterious and avoid stating fan theories as fact.

195.content: The three realms are the Light Realm, the Void Realm (Abyss) and the Human Realm made by the Heavenly Principles. They are concurrent facets of Teyvat, with analogous currents: elemental currents, dark currents and ley lines. The Light Realm's energy overcomes the Void Realm's darkness, and the Void Realm threatens both others.

196.content: The Void Realm, better known as the Abyss, is an unworldly destructive force from the sea of stars, opposed to the Light Realm and corrosive to the Human Realm. It corrupts people and creatures and is harmful to elemental beings.
